text: I received your welcome letter of the 20th a few days ago. I would ask now what I should do with regards to books, clothes, etc, as also when your scholastic year begins. I suppose you were informed about my bill of $525.00 at St. Francis'. What should I do about that before I go to join you? - supposing I could not pay cash.

Father was here on the 10th and all are well at home, thanks be to God! He said that you seemed to be lonesome out there, being so far from church etc. Well Dear Ella, I only pray you to content yourself for the present and pray and hope-even as you know poor dear Mother did, at the River-bank & at Trimbelle. You must know that there were trials in those places and indeed patience & resignation exercised. Now after so many years Father speaks of great consolation. It is really enough to draw a tear of admiration and gratitude for God's merciful providence, if one only considers the past (of our dear Parents) and now beholds their present circumstances and prospects. May their sky continue to brighten as their end approaches. For my part dear Sister I congratulate you on your present trials much rather than if you were "prospering" in riches even within a block of the Most Blessed Sacrament. I think you and yours are safer, especi- ally in the long run. If you only make your acts of contrition, etc. properly you need not be so uneasy about so frequent oral confession - and then your spiritual Communion. I pray you also to have our "Mass- prayers" at Trimbelle imitated, and Owney come to the same if possible- your neighbors, also even if they are not-Catholics, and do not neglect, in your rosaries to think at least sometimes of poor me. I received sub- deaconship Dec. 8th and will probably be ordained deacon-and priest be- fore August. May the Holy Ghost direct my Superiors in their decisions in this regard & His holy Will in all things be done. I asked my Super- ior for material and permission to write to you and he gave me also this little picture for you. With love to Br. Thomas ( Traynor) and Owen and all & a caress for the Little Ones from your brother. P.S. Admonish Br. Owney not to neglect the most salutary -- almsgiving for poor and orphans.

Please accept my sincere thanks for the little card you sent with Easter greetings. It is the first picture of my dear Patron I have ever received. Be sure also that I here- with return similar good wishes for yourself and for all at Graymoor. I take this occasion also Dear Sister, to assure you that I thanked Almighty God - and do thank Him for hav- ing inspired some one with such truly Franciscan sentiments as were manifest in your gentle protest to the plaintiff at- tornies of that Graymoor Church property case. I am fully con- fident that there are too many upright lovers of justice even among our separated brothers and sisters who read the Lamp and paused at that letter ever to hold their peace while an act of such injustice were perpetrated as would be perpetrated should your community be ejected from Graymoor. In my opinion there is no sane man who has a spark of Christianity who will hesi- tate when he knows the facts and the present circumstances at and around Graymoor, to second these sentiments - and acknow- ledge your sentiments as really Christian. Continue Dear Sis- ter in your determination never to quarrel, as our holy rule enjoins and be sure you will have more powerful patrons on your side than intrigue with irreligion and silver and gold can ever procure.

Rev. Father Superior who has been in with a severe cold for about two weeks wished me to convey our sympathy to the Sisters on account of the unreasonable and unjust eviction which the "killing letter of the law" has enabled unscrupulou men to score against them. - an eviction which we are confi- dent the great majority of our separated brethern will con- demn as done in their name and will regret. Needless to say we all hoped that things would never come to such a farce a- gainst common justice and charity. However, the victories of the world are short-lived- "man proposes but God disposes." We may be sure that Almighty God has not permitted things to take such a course without some good design of His own - to turn evil into good. At all events the words of our Divine Master, "Blessed are ye when they shall revile you and per- secute you ... unjustly for my sake .... ", should be a consola- tion to you and an encouragement. The sisters will hardly be able to do anything better than to pray earnestly for their persecutors, according to the same divine authority. "Do good to them that hate you, and pray for them that per- secute and calumniate you. Praying Almighty God to direct you and them - and us all according to His merciful will and inclosing a little donation from Rev. Father Superior to help you in your present need, I remain

. With the earnest appeal of the late Pope Pius X regarding an efficient Catholic Press, fresh in memory; and with the honest efforts of able pub- lishers before our eyes; and in view of a secular press everywhere, that in general, makes nothing of confusing fact with fiction, ready at any time to cater to Passion and "Bitterly hostile to Justice and Truth", it is surely not without regret that one sees in pages labeled "Catholic", indications of dependence on sources of thought, positively atheistic -- not to say mani- festations of docile servility to dictations of news Agencies, responsible for their existence to that one power, of all powers on earth internation- ally hated as the most prolific source of crime and injustice. Your present correspondent hardly believes that you wish your, other- wise esteemed little weekly to be a Publication of any such pages. In fact he is confident that you are not conscious of its ever leaving the Press as such, -- and this, notwithstand hisses which he tried to frownaway at a re- cent mass meeting, mostly Catholic, when the Catholic News was mentioned. Nevertheless, he wishes for the general good to call your attention to the fact, that, occasionally at least, you do give out pages indicating such said independence. As a proof of this contention he would ask you to review, just your own Editorial: "A SANE VIEN OF IRELAND", in your issue of August 5th; or again your Editorial of August 26th: "ASAD BLOW FOR IRELAND." Let us consider this latter, first. From the very beginning, and throughout, a weakness, sadly common even among our honest Editors, manifests itself. You show, namely, what might be quite excusable in an ordinary reader, a regrettable one-sidedness of infor- mation. With the above-referred to Agencies you seem to espouse views of the situation in Ireland, which Britain would like very much to "believe personally" to be the only proper views. Please just glance it over, and ask yourself if such an article might not be expected rather in a London Daily, or in any of our Metropolitan Yellow Jackets -- every one of them heart and soul in sympathy, not with a crucified Nation or with Catholic Principle, but with Brazen Brutal Britain. Now it is not the object of this correspondent to discuss the merits or the demerits of the treaty-proffered "Free State", or that of its pro- moters and founders -- one time acknowledged Champions of the Republic which now they seem to have given their lives to suppress. I will only say this just now, in favor of the same or against them; if Britain is in favor of the said "Free State" - and she seems to mightily so-then, honest, un- selfish, lovers of Ireland, and of truth, and of justice, ought to be opposed to it. Why? Because as centuries of Britain-broken Treaties, and British hypocrisy make manifest - the English government or the people composing it cannot be honestly or unselfishly interested in Ireland. Consequently if your correspondent knew absolutely nothing of the claims or the aims of any faction in Ireland - or of any party in Ireland -- for example just now, the legitimately established Republic and the said free-state, which later as its authors evidently hoped, was to sneak real British - fashioned into the place of the former, he would simply point to the history of British interest in Ireland and ask the one little question: "On which side of the dispute is British Favor?" In the present crisis, the thickest thug in the tombs prison to whatever side he might incline, would wonder that anyone might be so "thick" as honestly to ask such a question -- perhaps rather, so ill-informed. The wail, therefore, that went up all over British quarters at the fall of unfortunate Collins, not in December, when by the weight of his own name on the London Pact, he lost his balance and tumbled from the heights of Patriotic confidence to the plain of England's "Hero Irishman", but eight months later, when pushing the interests of that pact - some of course say of Britain too - he fell from said plain, beyond all hope of British dic- tation, - that British Wail, I say -- would indicate satisfactorily to my way of reasoning, just about in how much the death of Collins, R. I. P., might, under existing circumstances, be rightly termed "A SAD BLOW FOR IRELAND". Pardon me the rather long digression; but you will probably see thereby that there must be quite a little obtainable information about present Irish- British relationship other than, perhaps the majority of our, otherwise honest Editors seem to be concerned about. It is hoped, too, that the British views of the Irish situation - perhaps we ought to say the Northelif- Hearst and Co. music, so in harmony with the little Welsh "Wizard's" notes, and so cleverly and unsuspiciously danced to by so many Editors and even Clergy and other leaders in America, - are dangerously at variance with both fact and reason; And therefore, dangerously far from Pius X's ideal of an "efficient Catholic Press." Now, as to your above mentioned "SANE VIEW OF IRELAND"; briefly, you start out quite as a thinker, on the authority of fair observation and honest conviction might be expected to do; and you rightly admonish "ordinary Readers" to beware of accepting "Newspaper Reports" above re- ferred to as "Gospel Truths" But you do nottell us why such newspapers should be suspected; or why they dare not tell the truth - especially about Ireland- even if those immediately responsible were so disposed. Let me ask you: Is it not because the Power behind such cewspapers is quite the same as that which through calumny and hypocrisy got our own Country to take such a re- grettable share in what has resulted in the present degradation of Central Europe? Is it not because of their direct or indirect dependence for ex- istence on that same power - that furthermore and immeidately after the "trice" uniformed its most inhuman criminals (Higher intellectuals excepted, ) and sent them from British penetentiaries equipped with every implement of modern savagery against poor little Ireland? Aye, Ireland unarmed except by her Faith in God! Unoffensive except for her surpassing determination to stand by the principles of righteous Freedom -- principles for which from 1914 to 1919 humanity was bled white! Great God! Is it to be all for nothing?

And you hestitate not to commend as a sane view, in regard to Ireland, the dictum of one holding his title of honor and his commission from that same intriguing, hypocirtical power? And look how you quote him! Nearly half a column! Let me cite just a line or two from your quotation, " ... Therefore, my first word to you about Ireland is: Do not be too much dis- turbed by rumors about affairs in Ireland. "Ireland is on the way to Peace." Smoothe words indeed! How soothing to anxious souls in America! Do you not suspect the polished parallel of the referred to Agencies and Newspapers. Is the meaning of these words of Lord Shaw satisfactorily clear to you? They are not so to me. I would ask: Does your hero - if he be not a wily Briton - get his inspiration from the President of Ireland or from the Primer of England? Is it Cromwelian Peace he predicts, or is it the Peace for which Pearse and Comrades died in 1916 and since, down to MacSwiney and Brugha and Boland? Is it finally the peace for which DeValera and comrades are still holding out, which God only can give -- and is giving shortly - or what Shaw's King would be satisfied to call Peace? Do not forget that he tells you plainly that he is, "talking as an old Politician" - a British one, of course. Strange he did not know that his title assures us that he was both, before he was lorded. Ah Shaw! "Do not be too much disturbed -- "lest it be once more officially probed and found that your government's welfare work in Ireland still "stinks" in the nostrils of civilization "worse than it did eighteen months ago. Now before quoting from an acknowledged adept at lingual smoothness and duplicity - "an old politician", before poor Shaw was born or thought of, and undoubtedly as active in 20th century politics as any of his titled juniors - let me assure you that your correspondent is not doing this in any spirit of vindictiveness or out of malice to any one. He wishes simply to save, not only The Catholic News, but as much as he can, the honest press in general from humiliation more serious than any honest criticism could be, and that must come unless something be dore to arrest the above lamented in- clination of positively favoring British views, and British Calumnies, and worst of all because more dangerous, British Colored Truths. Who will doubt, at second thought and in the light of the present British-Begotten and British-fostered - and I must say British-waged War in Ireland that the above words of Lord Shaw are at least a weak parallel to those we find in the Third Chapter of Holy Writ? Here they follow: "And the Serpent said to the Woman: No, you shall not die the death, for God doth know that in what day soever you shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened and you shall be as Gods, knowing good and evil." (Gen. 111, 4) That is just an example of colored truth and of dubious prediction. No one doubts that their eyes were opened. But alas for their vision! and alas for your vision and mine! Alas, too, for peace and Ireland unless the Lord deliver her from Shaw and his kind, and from the peace they would wish for the Ireland of the Saints! God help our civilization at all events, for its hopelessly darkened understanding. We sometimes wonder at the simplicity of our poor first Parents and at their docile blindness toward their seducer. Yet, with all our science and with all the manifestation of historic ages, we refuse to recognize -- nay even to suspect-behind the blasphemous press of to-day, the same power that animated the wretched serpent. Aye, positively nothing less than blasphemous in the "Great Press" of to-day, because "Bitterly hostile to justice and truth" and therefore hostile to God himself who is eternally both. (See encyc'1 Leo XIII-1902) A civilized humanity, or as uncivilized, we act in general these days as though that power were nothing more than a childish myth. How? We sacrifice untold millions of our choicest youth and manhood for the prin- ciple of "Self-Determination" - nothing more or less in reality than a jus- tification of the Catholic Dogma of "Free Will" - and the nations stand mute at the 74 days martyrdom of a MacSweeney protesting and the age-long cru- cifixion of his nation protesting in the name of that same awful sacrifice and in the name of eternal justice against nothing less that the astounding outrage of an international attempt to destroy that very fundamental prin- ciple" - that God-given faculty. Does not such silence alone brand our so-called civilization as a sham and a farce? An outrage it is, pure and simple, on intelligence and decency. Does it not brand the professions of the allied nations for their war against and their degradation of Central Europe as manifest hypocrisy? Let no nation, much less individuals deceive themselves: God will not be mocked forever! And the allied nations, and their civilzation have been mocking the honest peoples of the earth, and surely not less the Eternal God of honest people. Who is to blame? Where is our ideal Catholic Press? Offensive and Defensive? God help us! Aye, God help us, and forgive us! That individual leaders have been and are guilty of that criminal silence and that mockery, is as positively clear as the fact that nations are made up of individuals. They seem now, however, to be going further into crime. In- stead of blushing for shame, personal as well as national, that no one has a- risen like Daniel of old to convict the hypocrites, some of them are be- ginning to come out on the side of shame itself, on the side of the bull-dog and the lion -- the side of the arch-ravager of nations. They speculate with the coolness of game-cook gamblers on hair-splitting points of morality, thus wittingly or unwittingly-diverting attention from the real source of troubles in Ireland-the presence of British Soldiers, and of British corrup- tion (See Dr. Ryan, E.G. in"America" ) Is not this clearly a case of the Scriptural, "Straining at a gnat, and swallowing a camel?" Shame on the "blind Guides"! Pardon me if your correspondent seem acrimonious, and may the Lord help us to see clearly! for Bittemess like falsity and Exaggeration is to no purpose in an honest cause. But history, it seems here as well as elsewhere, must repeat itself, It was a Bishop that condemned St. Joan of Arc for witchery and that a little later, durressed as he was by the British (and at that, time supposed to be a Catholic), exposed her to unmentionable cruelties and finally burned her at the stake as a heretic. If reports be true there are one or two pre- lates in America who would do the like for a number of Irish Joans, even without British duress. May the Good God deliver us from scandals! But I would ask his Lord- ship from Buffalo and his Grace from Baltimore if "Eamon DeValera seems to have completely lost his reason", who is to blame, if not the despicable power his own Grace and his lordship seem to be now espousing and that DeValera has frustrated, escaped and withstood these four years -- so long and so bitter for poor Ireland, and for DeValera? What is to blame after British hypocrisy more than the above mentioned international silence? More than the already referred to leaders and guides? May God in his mercy overlook the crime of it all and pity such leaders and their respon- sibility. Your correspondent prays for them without exception. But if Eamon DeValera, as it is honestly believed, has still his wits about him, is it not really next to a miracle of God's Providence? If he still has 30,000 patriot soldiers behind him, though practically without arms, is there not still hope for "Self Determination", and hope for Democracy? At all events, if Almighty God is in favor of the principle of "self- determination" for men of free-will, then the majority in Ireland is behind the soul of the Republic still: and notwithstanding all reports to the con- trary, and all criticisms to the contrary, and all powers to the contrary, if God is still for Principle and for the Republic of Ireland, the majority in Ireland are behind DeValera; and DeValera, appealing to the Sacred Heart, as when sentenced to be shot in 1916, will triumph in the end over every enemy, if need be even as the Maiden-Soldier Saint triumped in the crown of a glorious Martyrdom!

Rather than find bitterness in the Irish World concerning the folder recently sent out purporting to be a "statement by Right Rev. Michael J. Gallagher, D.D. dealing with the visit to the United States of Hon. Eamon DeValera," a copy which I have been assured duly reached your office, I want to congratulate you on the digni- fied silence (or prudent oversight) which in this case especially be- comes your long experience and your really responsible position. I do not like to believe that said statement "is really and ex- pression, carefully considered, of a Bishop whom in more than one way I have admired, and who undoubtedly loves Ireland and justice. Pos- sibly, however, he has been beguiled and I deceive myself, as it seems now that I die deceive myself about 10 months ago when speaking about Cohalan's unfortunate break with DeValera, then recently made manifest, I asked you, "let us hope that his motives are not so unworthy." Per- haps a little time and honest criticism of the "statement will bring out other views and other expressions from Bishop Gallagher. For my part, I cannot think of going into details about it at this time, being as you know only a simple religious and therefore, not experienced in and not inclined to analyse such documents. This much, however, I will say in its favor: If "differences a- rise between honest lovers of a common cause mostly because of misun- derstandings," then, whatever the motive for publishing the personal correspondence as therein given between DeValera and his opponents, the author has wittingly or unwittingly taken a positive step in the direction of settling differences between Ireland, in her representa- tive, and those in America who honestly oppose the same representative, De Valera. Personally, at least, if I had never followed up the Irish ques- tion at all, as I certainly have been and am, I would be inclined to ask, on reading DeValera's message and the reply it occasioned - to say nothing of the two pages signed "J. D." -- I would be more than inclined to ask: "Is this the Friendship that joins the F.O. I.F. and martyred Ireland? Does not DeValera's sentence after sentence show at once a disappointed confidence and a depressed hope as well as a determination forced almost to desperation?" -- which determination opponents of Ire- land seem to mistake for unbending pride: though even the bitterest of them have to acknowledge that her representative is , "doubtlessly conscientious." But I would ask further, as I ask now: "Is there anything in Judge Cohalan's reply that would manifest even a consent to co-operate with De Valera, or with Ireland herself in the person of her representative?"is there not, on the contrary, evidence of a decided prejudice and a preconceived determinaation to resist -- not to say thwart cooperation on the part of the F.O.I.F .? In other words, does not the judge, in said reply to DeValera speak for himself and his constituents as really more an American Pro- tective Association than as the F.O. I.F. is defined -- "an association of American citizens founded to assist the Irish people in securing freedom for the Irish people?" How, then, can anyone blame the repre- sentative of the Island of Saints and Sages for refusing, even "to dis- cuss the question" of a compromise with such leaders of a society whose rank and file members would be justly indignant at the very insinuation, though in all truth they might be called real "A.P.A's" instead of Friends of Ireland? Their fear of danger from Ireland's alliance with England would be, or is, just about as reasonable as the fear of the original A.P.A. from an alliance of the Pope with the professed powers of Hell -- just as affected, too. As to DeValera's "Cuban blunder," well, DeValera's every utterance ever since, not to say his every action, including his tragic return to Ireland, seals that as an evident calumny. Talk about "splitters," as long the objective is practically iden- tical sounds to me like so much wind. The splitters -- would-be or other- wise -- in any great cause are those who for selfish motives swerve from first principles, even as the real greatness of any nation --- republic or other -- may be measured by the pervading spirit of national righteousness which, by the way, considering our governmental silence these many moons regarding British and allied outrages, etc, is not saying much for the "greatest republic." Of course, if the F.O. I.F. is the fruit of any one's personal gen- ius, and therefore liable to be claimed as personal property, nobody can blame such genius for frothing a little when a stranger refuses to ac- knowledge his right, but if, as quite a few of us believe, such societie are divinely providential then the more and the longer such a "genius" frothes the more ridiculous and the more pitiable -- not to say contempti- ble he makes himself. In conclusion, while I trust the above may offend no one, I would call attention in a very practical advice of a former president of the F.O. I. F., the dear Carmelite Father McGinnis, now General of his whole Order. "The moment a man or a machine or an organization or a clique gets bigger than the cause, get away from any or all of them because they have ceased to be of any good and have begun to do harm no matter what the past record of any or all of them be." Coming from Rome where they were written January 1, 1920, these words have the ring of at least a foresight of what many an honest member of the F.O. I.F. has taken as a kind of personal matter of thought as is manifested from the multitudes of their brethren of the A.A.R.I.R. May God bless the honest members of both with a sense of unsel- fish justice and consistency and unaffected charity. And may He bless every honest reader of the Irish World and Industrial Liber- ator! P.S. If it were not for your lack of space, I would suggest printing the personal correspondence above referred to so convinced I am that the real root of the would-be trouble is thereby shown.

You will have been naturally more or less anxious about Brother Pasqual if we may still speak of him as such, instead of George Gordon. It would hardly be in place for me to take special interest in his case, but he seems to have a sort of confidence in me that, sorry to say he does not show to others who would be able to do more for him. I am sure a few minor details in this regard will not be unwelcome, and possibly will be of use - I can not say just how, but I got the impression shortly before 3. P. came here from Garrison and went to Hospital, that he was not very practical or it was while he was in the hospital. Nevertheless I visited him twice during his stay there as a patient. I regretted that no one else (that I know of) visited him from here. More still I regretted the reception given him at his return to the Monastery. It seemed to me as an assurance that he was not welcome or wanted. I tried to excuse it. I do not know if I succeeded or not. I heard the words told him as he was starting upstairs: "You can stay here of course, but this is no hospital - - " About half an nour afterwards he came down, saying he was going to St. Vincent's Hospital to get a thorough examination. Not knowing the circumstances, and thinking that was the order of some one at St. Francis, I asked him no questions except if he would be back tonight. I believe he said he would go over to Pitt St. That was Sunday afternoon. Tuesday moming he came to the office sine- barba - doubting what to think of the manner of treatment here and at Pitt St. etc. Fr. Guardian was out when he came, whom he did not seem to want to see, and I told him he should by all means go over and see Father Definitor in East N. Y. and that I would try and phone over in the meantime. Fr. Guardian came in before B. P. left and I told him he was there, and that I had determined him to go to Fr. Martin. Then I proposed - when Br. was gone - that I phone in his name and tell them something of the situation etc. I was simply forbidden to do so. That was the last I heard about the case till two days ago when I received the enclosed letter. Fr. Paul was here last evening and talking about 3r. I told them of this letter. This morning I said holy Mass up in the Assisium and afterwards returning I went of two blocks west to the Hotel Theresa and had a short talk with Br. He had been sleeping till I phoned up. He seemed quite himself; did not exactly complain against anyone, but seemed rather to wonder, what it all should come to. He told me he did not know what to think about it. He had been to a friend of his - a lawyer - yesterday and told him all about the case, to see if he could get something decided etc. I told him as much as that I had not been personally edified at what seemed to me his want of fervor or devotion to holy Communion while he was with us in Our Lady of Angels; and therefore I thought he ought to turn earnestly to Headquarters - meaning the Tabernacle and make some promise to do better in this, or some other regard, if things adjusted themselves favorably to his peace. Then he said something about making a retreat with the Jesuites. I told him that would, in my opinion, be the best thing he could do. I told him I would write you about him and he said he wished I would. I wanted to tell Father Guardian of my visit and of my proposition to write you all about the case, but I decided it as prudent to say nothing to him about it. Before I had a chance to do so, before deciding, he forbade me to correspond with "3r. P." and at culpa before dinner gave quite a little admonition, in a general way, bearing on this case, while we all knelt as novices. Now Dear Father Provincial I do not wish to blame anyone or to excuse anyone else. "Brother Paschal" seems to me willing to be directed. He seems quite conscious that he did not receive entirely "a fair deal" with the superior above - - - Well, may our dear Lord God direct him and us all We received quite a large package of certificates yesterday, for the Seraphic Mass Association. They came in good time and shape. Fr. Guardian just told me that the cash received this month already is $1002. 00. Thanks be to God! the reports of favors as through this source continue. Fr. Adelhelm was down Today from Glencliff with chronicles and good reports. As far as I know all the brethren in this end of the Province are well. The student John Parsons in Yonkers seems quite improved.

It has just struck 10:30 p.m. and I perhaps ought to be slum- bering before this, but I want to do what I've been forced to put off thus far - write you a few works of encouragement, etc. I surely am pleased with words and reports of your now constant im- provement. I would like to have called to see you today but it was raining and when I left the dentist I had just time to get home for dinner. ... I hope you will continue to improve till you are back "on the job" again. Of course it is possible that you may be a little lame in that knee of yours, though we will hope for the best and leave it all to the divine Lover of our Souls - Yes leave everything to Him - offering ourselves to Him to suf- fer whatever His love may permit. When I think of your condition for the first week or two it looks to me almost like a miracle that you pulled through atall. Thank God for it all! I am sure your sufferings were not lost, and that more than yourself have profited by them spiritually.
God Bless you Sr. Cecilia Kiss your Cross day by day Have peace!
- for God's special grace and guidance - God, bless you Sister M. Solania Be as blind to the faults of your neighbor as possible trying to at- tribute a good intension to their actions - at least.
I am sending you Miss Bergta Habib. She seems to think she'd probably like to share your labors Your crown to as I hope.

My Dear Willie: - Many thanks for favor just read. you are well and doing. Thank God for everything. I am glad to know I wish you would convey best wishes and blessings to all my friends you chance to meet in picturesque, beautiful Yonkers. This has been the busiest place I been located in so far . . · Near 31 years now since I went to Yonkers - and Willie was one of Fr. Stephan's boys.
O Course we are glad to include you in our prayers. Do not worry. Special God willing -- i I 1 ! I I 1 1 I 1 1 1 -- for speedy health-recovery -

God bless you. I hope you are well. I was rather disapointed in your decision to drop my friend Garland from your employ. I know that he liked the work and that he took an interest in it such as few of your employes are wont to take. He liked his employer and his associates. I would have been disapointed had he failed to so, because I know something of his ability. Mr. Garland blames no one, though he was dazed at first. He is too big a character to hold petty mis- understandings, etc. He wants me to forget it as he hopes to do himself. I know that he would object to complaining to you and I am not coplaining. I am doing this without his knowledge. I am confident that you will not regret this my information, -- at least if you will have just a little patience with my effort. I have known Mr. Garland for about ten years and I can honestly say that I doubt if I have ever met a person more solicitous to do a favor or more practical in suggesting remedies in time of difficulties. I need not go far for examples to prove this. When your Mr. Portius was in anxiety last March or early April about a very threatening difficulty, Mr. Garland had a remedy astonishingly happy in its marvelous results. Before that, when Mr. Dory and wife seemed next to desperate, and religiously paralized Garland brought them hither and they seemed to take on new life and energy. The story of Mr. J. Phillips' still in the hospital afords another example of fraternal charity, - When C. H. Chisholm was threatened with blood-poison Garland could not wait to get over but phoned first and then came over to have me send the enrollment card. You know better than I what resulted. But why all such details? I simply want to put you "wise" against poisonous intimations regarding Rae Garland, on the part of a certain prominent party" who had a big share in the robbing of Garland of his cemetery, the Mt. Vernon Memorial Park. This of course is coming too late to save Garland his employ- ment, but if you find out the truth about him as I know it, and about said prominent party who has knocked him before, you'll realize something of what you've lost in dropping such a promising employee. But more than this, you will know what to do without hesitation if occasionally you have an opportunity to do him and me a favor.

Holy Job tells us, "the life of man on earth is a warfare". He makes no exceptions. The Psalmist appeals to us all without exception: "Be ye converted to the Lord your God." and in another place "O Lord God of hosts convert us : and show thy face, and we shall be saved." (Ps. 79-20) A Christian poet whispers to us as a loving brother : "Poor wanderers of a stormy day "From wave to wave we're drive: And fancy's flash and reason's ray serve but to light the troubled way, "There's nothing calm but Heaven. Moore More encouraging than all -- for those who realize their weak- ness -- Jesus Christ, the long promised Messiah our Redeemer, assures us: "I am come to call sinners In the light of Christian reasoning, therefore, brightened by these and similar expressions, I presume to address this audience as my brothers and my sisters; and under present cir- cumstances, on the subject of Capuchin-Franciscan Appreciation. One of the outstanding prayers of all history, with consequent approval of Heaven, was the prayer of King Solomon for wisdom to discern between good and evil -- for wisdom to judge justly. "And the Lord said to Solomon: Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life or riches, nor for the lives of thy enemies, but hast asked for thyself wisdom to discern judgement, Behold I have done for thee ac- cording to thy words, and have given thee a wise and under - standing heart, insomuch that there hath been no one like thee before thee .... " In the light of the enthusiasm on the part of our neigh- bors and friends -- our contemporaries without distinction of creed or color -- it is a privilege of our Capuchin Community, in whose name these few words are spoken, to express something of the appreciation that ought to overwhelm us -- something of the gratitude that surely ought to fill our hearts. I refer, of course, to the generous activity on our behalf of, quite a num- ber of our personal friends in arranging the affair, conducted on our behalf in the Naval Armory this evening at O'clock, and so enthusiastically seconded by the public in general on both sides of the Detroit River. What I want to stress To-day is the importance these days of appreciation for favors -- on our part; that we be grateful for such enthusiasm -- grateful to God first for such friends' and then to the friends themselves; for in my humble conviction APPRECIATION with its synonum GRATITUDE IS as necessary for social order and harmony as are the laws of gravity for the physical order of inanimate beings. ONCE more, therefore, let me thank you my brethren, one and all, in the name of our Capuchin Community. May mutual appreciation be the soul of our relationship in the future as this affair in the Armory seems to prove it has been in the past. God Bless You All.

You may think sometimes that it is hard to keep up courage. One phase of contentment - rather I will say a feature of the key to contented peace, - is this: To try to realiz the contrast ( rather than the difference) between Time and Eternity. At the longest time must be so short. But O! Who can fathom Eternity ?!! Then be grateful for what we have -- Existence -- The True Faith God made me to know Him - O what a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure reste in the same. It's Heaven begun - for the grateful on earth To treasure aright? !? !! ... Highest Heaven its worth. Be sure, if the enemy of our souls is pleased at any thing in us it is ingratitude - of whatever kind. Why? ingrati- tude leads to so many brakes with God & neighbor. "Whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth. Some day you will thank God for having been leaf. . God bless you Dorothy B. ...

God bless you and yours, I hope you are well. I hope too that I may not be presuming too much in asking your- self of whom I have only heard, to guide the bearer, honest Edmund Walsh to employment, if you have anything in view. I would appreciate anything you might find convenient to do for him.
When the family all go to Holy Communion the child will be O.K. we hope

The returned letter herewith inclosed will partly explain my silence at your sorrows last August. But though silent, I have not been al- together unmindful of your bereavement. However we may confidently trust in God to manifest some day a merciful design - not only in your case of such sorrow but in every case where He has per- mitted suffering in order that little children may come to Him. How happy you ought to be in reality this holy season! to have your little Owen, not only an altar boy, but one of the great heavenly army of holy Innocents. In this thought, while in another sense I condole with you, I wish you a holy and a happy Blessed Christmastide!

Fr. Solanus with H.J. Macey and Sister. H.J. had left school, for some weeks blind. Was brought to Monastery and enrolled in Ser. Mass Assoc'n. reading on way home (Jan 2 - '34) : went back to school next day. Had been baptized with their father and two younger - Dec. 24th. Now received 1st Holy Communion. Thanks be to God for this and many similar favors reported. You see Dear Owen, I'm getting to look like an old man. 20 years since you and I met, have made quite a change; but O! --- what will 20 yrs. more bring? Let us get ready as J. T. got ready. ·

Mrs. Martha Casey - for her special intention. and for His holy guidance - --- God willing, Of course we be glad to pray for same too .. God bless you Martha; you and yours. Glory be to God that you all seem to be well. Keep it up. Foster Confidence in divine Pro- vidence. It will be "crying necessary" be- fore many decades - of months - even of weeks.

God bless you and yours. I was fixing up a certain cell yesterday when this card showed up. It reminded me of our visit some thirty months back when you served the high Mass and the sisters inside sang - and . after breakfast, we had a conference with the prisoners of Jesus. Quite some changes since those pleasant few days .... Many thanks Martha for your beautiful card, etc. I wanted to answer it again and again ..... We have not heard from Fr. Edward since September nor from Guam - first taken by the Japs - since before the trouble .... I think it best to be, not over anxious about whats coming. One thing we may be sure of - God is watching all and in His own time and way will turn all to His glory and ours in as much as we shall persevered in His service. It seems to me it is once more "history repeating itself as against sins"Thou shalt not comit adultery". Happy New Year.

God bless you Owen and Martha and all the family. Many thanks Owen for your kind favor of last week from Los Angeles. Glad to know all are well down there. Thank God Fr. M. Joachim and myself are well too. I am hoping co go down to see him before long. I am confident that this experience of his will prove to have been a manifest blessing for him and for us all. Pray that it may.

Many thanks for favor of the 16th. Thanks be God! I am glad to know Bernard M. is feeling more contented. I enjoyed his visit as I think he did. I had very little time to really give him but tried at least in a general way, to impress him with the conviction that what ever our faculties be, the one primary purpose of every rational creature is to know God and by keeping the commandments - really just rules of health for body and soul - save our poor souls and gain the crown Eternal.

I found Sister Mary Rosella noted on August 9th: so have made out her certificate accordingly and am herewith inclosing. I hope it will be satis- factory - glad you called my attention. Please pardon oversight and consequent delay. I can easily understand something of how you feel, hustling all day in the hospital, etc. It's a great work in itself and a wonderful opportunity to prac- tice charity and of course mortification in so many ways, which brings one nearer to God and endears to the Sacred Heart. Naturally "social life" often suffers - and what is to be regretted in many cases - family life too. This latter is realy important and in every way should be supplied as far as possible. . Prayer in your and O. J.'s case, I trust has helped - and let us hope will help more than anything else under circumstances.

JOY, PEACE AND GRACE BE YOURS - Better late than never. Many thanks for your charitable favor. I succeeded To-day in getting Bernard's certificate off in the mail. By air this ought to fly over it .. Please tell Patrick our dear Brother I am not forgetting his letter - the one I Owe for his several weeks back. - just now "snowed under."

Many thanks for your kind favor - duly received and noted. I do hope you all keep well - avoiding worry and too much ambition. .... Fr. E'd was down a couple days at Christmas, seems to have enjoyed visit. Am writing him Tonight - his Name day is the 139 E'd.

Many thanks for your favor - aye for you many favors, - that so seldom get time to acknowledge, Rev. Fr. Neil Mccluskey, S.J. had holy Mass her last Thursday and stayed till about 2 p.m. We are expecting M. Genevieve his dear Mother these days when she gets to Mildred's in Chicago. M. and Dean are figuering on bringing her down before joining Neil in N.Y. and going overseas for coure in Louvain. Love and God's grace to all, including each of your patients. .

God bless you and love Martha - you and yours. Hope this - enrollment - speed the hoped-for improvement in Sister Mary Thomas" health. Thank God it hardly ever faill. Fr. - Rt. Rev Mons. - E'd stopped off last Friday at Fort Wayne (25 miles N.E. ) and came down and I served his holy mass. He had been East since July. Thanks be to God he was quite successful in his mission efforts and looks well. I had word that Owen was to have an operation that day. We hope this finds him well back on his feet. How little we appre- ciate our incalculable privileges - blessings of our holy Faith. Glory be to God.

God bless you and yours these unsettled days - at once of threatening forebodings and of God's outstanding mercies. Rt. Rev. Monsignor Edward is about to leave for Ft. Wayne here since yesterday P.M. He looks well and still seems pushing as usual. I have started several times these later months to write you but, God helps! I hardly know where - 15-19 hour days go to -- Fr. Ed. is going now to New York. P.S.

Glad to hear from you again, not withstanding the long silence on my part. I have been here in Detroit doctoring for the last three weeks not that I have been sick actually, I guess I was run down. I had an operation on a grout /growth/ under my left eye. The doctors say that is healing up nicely. I started to write to you a number of times, and I had just about finished it, but I cannot put in this letter, because it is about 200 miles from here, at St. Felix, in Huntington. I had written the letter just before Oune's death. May his soul rest in peace. I surely sympathize with you and yours, and all our dear one and friends, not withstanding the congraulations I offer all his friends for the admir able disposition. Thanks be to God for the grace granted to him and accompanied him in his long heroic struggle for life eternal. Another beautiful death in the family, for which father and mother prayed for faithfully per- severingly; that all their children would be granted the grace of a happy death. I am sure glad, that poor brother Pat, with the grace of God is keeping up. I pray and think of him every day. He is next to me in age. He must be 83 now. Please God, I must reach Pat, with a letter soon. Though there so many urgently crying for help, that one heartly known which one to help first. This is almost continuely. God's will be done, in all His blessed designs. In conclusion let us exhort one another on every occasion to be gratuateful to God for the un- countable graces by which we are surrounded. I am dictating this letter to one of my brothers, my dear brothers. Brother Gabriel. With loving regards to Brother Patrick, Sisters M. Genevieve, Margaret and all our dear ones in the West. I remain
Just a line this busy eve to wish you God's Blessing for a Happy New Year. Love, Best wishes, God's Grace To All.

I hope you are keeping contented. I've been reading of the missions up that way lately and it sure is interesting. Niece Mary was in a few days ago. is well as are seemingly all in the west - and Fr. Maurice. Ed. Sampson sends best regards.

With love and with Christmas blessings to all Comes the Infan once more to free us from sorrow Whose love and Whose power and Whose gentleness call To each heart and Each soul for a manger tomorrow Whose love and Whose Wisdom, Whose wonders proclaim Him the Son of the Virgin as promised of your. O may He estrange us from sin with its shame And reigh in our hearts as His crib ever more! God bless you Brother Patrick Glad to hear your busy. I hope you keep up your frequent and daily communions. Lord have mercy on John and Thom. It was a great consolation to know that they had been practical in this - John for 17 yrs was daily communicant. Thanks be to God. Deo Gratias.
Patrick H. Casey - that he learn to forgive - "Blessed are the peace-makers for they shall be called the children of God. " God bless you - My dear Brother Patrick.

for speedy recovery, God willing - -perpetual member Feast of the Apparaition of our Bl. Imaculate Mary. - Febr. 11th - 1947 God bless you Br. Pat. Offer all to Jesus - Who has suffered so much for us all - for you and me. My Jesus - Thy will be done. Forgive us our sins. Deliver us from the flames of Hell. Have mercy on the souls in Purgatory - Especially the most abandoned. Don't worry Pat. Rather foster confidence in God's mercy by thanking Him for every thin - even ahead of time - Please pray for me -

God bless you these unsettled days; you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of March 12th as also that of a few weeks back, as well as the letter you sent me before Christmas. I am really ashamed of my- self not to have answered or acknowledged any of these before. I did start to do so a number of times. In fact its been on my mind to write you ever since the beautiful death of poor, dear Father Maurice Joachim; who as you know passed from time into eternity on the fifth anniversary of our dear eldest Brother James, January 12th, a year ago, ( 1949) and by happy coincidence we buried him on the fifty second anniversary of my own receiving of the holy Habit. Glory be to God! I hardly thought of it at the time or realized the beauty or the delicacy of the connection in each case, especially my own - the one five years apart, the other, ten times five plus. The more I think it over the better I appreciate it. Deo Gratias. I know you have quite some details of that death - that happy transi- tion I hope - from Father Edward - Rt. Rev. Monsignor rather. But new details of anyone we've loved are always welcome and, since he and myself, of all the family and Clan were the only ones present, I feel I owe at least some such particulars. I probably ought to go into quite some more features of so interesting an event but I am a slow writer - only learn- ing to type - and there are so many other things I ought to be doing. Well to start with; we received a wire from Father Edward Wednesday morning, inside of an hour after M.J. 's passing: "Father Maurice Joachim died the morning at 6:20," Expecting further details and presuming that the funeral would be on Saturday and possibly in St. Paul or Prescott, Wis., I waited till next morning, although when I reached the very Rev. Father Provincial "long distance" at noon same day, in N.Y. he told me without hesitation to go to the Funeral. Of course, you remember Father M.J. had been with us almost ten years before that fearful carbuncle knocked him so completely out. Father Guardian and Brother Cook brought me to Fort Wayne to catch the Golden Arrow Train on the Pennsylvania, which if on schedule would reach Chicago in time to catch the widely advertised Hiawatha on the "Milwaukee". Ithad snown that morning however, and that meant a probable delay in the train service. Sure enough, the Conductor on taking our ticket as we left Fort Wayne lamented their being 25 minuete late, which meant that if they didn't lose any more time in 150 miles to Chicago, we'd make the said Hiawatha and thus reach St. Paul about 7 P.M. On leaving Huntington, however, we had said the Rosary for a favorable trip and safe return and, thanks be to God, I just forgot a- bout worrying that day. The Milwaukee management kindly consented to wait till they got my ticket, though they advised against bothering a- bout a "clergical permit". Mildred and Jean Conley were there and the O'Donnells: - had been trying in my absence to procure said clerical permit, but without success. I forget if I took dinner on the train but I did take a small lunch, a glass of milk, I believe .25 cents, and was in good shape for a worth- while supper - and a night's rest when we got to St. Paul. Then only, however, it was that I learned the particulars about the place, time etc. of the Funeral. Grandma Conley with Helen, and John, instead of whiffing me away, stressed that I get back on the train and they with me, went on to Minneapolis. There I should take another train an hour or so later, for Ortenville 200 miles further on; say Holy Mass next morning and thence, go with the Pastor, dear Father George Campbell, by auto the balance of the trip, 20 miles to Graceville. ... The train was not too warm even with an overcoat, so after about six hours or more of trying to sleep, watching the snow-touched landscape, etc, under a
I hope you're in this great movement. There 7 of us her and each gets a copy. . 4 :p.m. Br. Owen just phoned from Conley in Chicago. Coming to St. Felix to-night.

I hope this finds you improving on the report received recently from Mildred in Chicago. I offered my holy Mass for you today and have been including you and yours in all my prayers and holy Masses. I am really ashamed of myself that I write so very seldom. Still, when I am confident that my dear ones are in the grace of God -- keeping up the "good fight" and at the same time when I know so many languishing under their icad of temptations -- so often with little or no faith I just feel I must do something to encourage and, like- rescue them. There are so many whose faith seems to be chilled and benumbed by materialism and forgetfullness of our primary purpose as rational creatures, viz; grate- fully to recognize our greatest Benefactor - our God and Saviour. -- I wrote a boyfriend of ours several months ago - Chris Adam - with whom we played and associated in our early boyhood, together with his little sisters, Lottie and Eattie; - poor youngsters! poorly instructed and left orphans at one of the most dangerous periods in life, just blooming into youth. I sent him badges of the Sacred Heart. He, too in his 8Os wrote back appreci- atively, in a way but seemed content with hardly any reference other than to material existence. "Lottie never married ... Hattie did ... and has three grown-up children ... " He wrote also of his own family and grand- children. Sorry I can't put my hand on his letter now. I am trying to get time to, kinda wake them up to renewed appreciation of the only science that in the end amounts to more that the snap of one's finger, Religion; The Science of our happy dependence on Almighty God and our neighbor. What a real vestibule to Heaven this world would be if everyone would just be convinced and try to live according to that simple definition! Fr. E'd was here with us a whole week in May. A letter from him in White Plains Y. He seems to keep well most of the time. Deo Gr.

you. It must seem to you a long time now that I have failed to write I hardly know how to explain this neglect. True I have been busy; but that should not have held me from acknowledging your cards about Christmas and especially from expressing sympathy with you and our other dear ones so tragically bereaved - January 25th. I wanted to write you a real letter and not sure of your address, I left other duties demand first attention. I have prayed for you, however, and mean to continue to do so. You surely realize by this time something of the necessity we all stand in of praying and of having prayers .... O! could your dear Father but come back now and tell you what it meant for him in the end. Now he realizes better than we possibly can how fortunate he was to have hearkened to the plea Jesus made to His people in Palestine and now to us: "Come to me all ye that labor and are heavily burdened and I will refresh you" ..... On vacation, nearly forty years ago he was careful to get to daily Mass if possible He would work often till ten minutes before Mass began and then run a- cross the field and try to make the mile we lived from Church in time not to be too late. We usually went together and sometimes raced. Daily Communion in those days was never recommended to us as it has been these recent years. How I often regret that it was not. I feel now that we missed so much that would have so strengthened us against the dangers and temptations of youth - the dangers and temptations that even these seemed to engulf so many contemporaries and now per- naps more than ever before. O! if we could but peep into eternity occasionally during our earthly existance, as the soul does when it separates from the body, how different would be our "Appreciation. . " ... I have not worried about our "John and Tom." I feel with Fr. Maurice that they were and are safe ..... i think it must have been his daily Communion that by degrees and imperceptibly made him "see things so differently, espec- ially death." When he visited me in Yonkers, N.Y. about a year before he married again and seemed so at home with the Capuchins, he re- marked one day as we talked things over " .... I find no attrac- tion in women any more; but I feel I ought to have someone to be with my little Helena." Well, Jesus sent him that someone, though at the time you probably failed to recognize her as such a "God-send" - for your dear Father at first and immediately, and now more than ever for his Helena, with two others for mutual love and companionship. How beautiful and wonderful are God's ways. And O, how far he surpasses us in generosity! Thanks be to God! ! ! Praised Be Jesus

The New Year is still in its baby-hood: so I'll wish you all kinds of blessings before it passes as all others so far have gone. If ever I get up with my letters again I'll write to my dear ones more frequently. I hope. .I am glad you have found someone and that someone has found you wherecy mutual congeniality seems promising. .That he is older than you is a secondary matter. Even that he actually knows little about the True Religion might be secondary too, if only he or anyone else be desirous to learn - be willing to find out - and dispel doubts .. .It is so easy for the Church to vindicate her every Doctrine! !!.. . How your dear Father John was convinced of this! So much so that tho his death was tragic, it was never the less a holy death. I never worried about that. P.S. Preparing for ... Speed up your communions.

How like autumn flowers, bleaches the freshness of youth; and ideals change like raiments of the soul! May God bless you and give you holy resignation and, of course the crown ineffable that must follow, if perfect. Even in this side of the grave astonishments come as for such Christian virtue. A certain over-grown John Joseph M., a contemporary of your great-grand-father, a namesake and probably a relative, skipped school at 13 because ashamed to go to class with little boys; joined the British navy, went to the far East; later failed in an enterprise in London, joined the Hudson-Bay Co., joined an Indian tribe and became the famous "Chief Black Eagle of the North." Very charitable to the poor Indians whom, from the beginning he had learned to love, he was called to something greater. Deep in the wilderness he came across a sort of little clear- ing and there in the crutch of a big tree met a weather-beaten sta- tue of our Immaculate Mother. . .. . Calling his braves together shortly thereafter he resigned, disposed of his vast. estates, went to Rome and five Yrs. later was ordained a priest; returned to Ireland and after several years mission in London became the famous Father John of Cork .... Who does not get a taste of the Cross one way or other and, if only with resignation: "The bigger the cross the greater the crown." . .

With love and with Christmas blessings to all Comes the INFANT once more to free us from sorrow. Whose love and Whose grace and Whose gentleness call To each heart and each soul for a manger tomorrow. Whose Birth and Whose power and Whose wonders proclaim Him, the Son of the VIRGIN as promised of yore. O ! May He estrange us from sin with its shame! -- And reign in our hearts as His crib evermore. God made me to know Him. O! What a blessd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. It's HEAVEN BEGUN for the GRATEFUL on earth To treasure aright ! ? ! HIGHEST HEAVEN its worth. P.S. Would be glad to hear from little Casey M. Tell him I said he is old enough now to think the responsibility and the privilege of working at his own Eternal salvation.

God bless you both and all you are interested in. I've had your letter of January 10th here before me on the desk ever since; hoping to get chance and time to send you a worth-while answer. Of course I've been hoping for brighter outlook and better word than what that letter would seem to intimate. Yesterday, however, I received an in- teresting letter from Martha to the effect that all are well in Seat- tle and down the Coast, with one or two exceptions and Helena's Hus- band, E'd Wilhite. From all reports he, your same Edward, has been suffering something similarly to what Father Maurice Joachim went through twenty years ago, when it seemed he was about done for. Yet think how remarkable is his stomach Today. Thanks be to God. I re- ceived a good letter from him last week. Both he and Father Edw'd are well. Thanks be to God and our Bl. Mother Mary. Now I am going to give you briefly something from my "NOTES ON CASES THROUGH THE SERAPHIC MASS ASSOCIATION", that for several years I was making while in Detroit: Just one case in perhaps more than a thousand, -- a number of them not only fearful tumors but of most posi- tive and threatening cancer. May 25th, 1945. "Mrs. Catherine Nagle - 45 - mother of eight children, opened up for operation two weeks ago (May 9th) in Provi- dence Hospital. Found to be so hopelessly full of cancer that the Drs, simply closed her up again as ' ... never to leave the hospital alive.' "Has been enrolled in Ser. Mass Association several times. Today her husband enrolls the Poor Souls specially (10); - whole family storming Heaven by daily Communion .... " Mother comes home To-day; unable to take any nourishment ... May 29th. "Mrs Nagle as above May 25th. Thanks be to God: fear- ful pains and swelling gone from abdomen, has good appetite and eating fine. Husband enrolls Poor Souls again in thanksgiving." Sept. 14th, Brooklyn, N. Y. "Mrs. Nagle as noted above May 25 and 29th, here Today in perfect health. = I hardly know what to do to keep the letters here from piling up. Otherwise I'd give you a number of the cases that we've had here at St. Michael's lately. I feel I must give you the second last note of the very few I have time and call to record. Feb. 15, 1946. " ... Catherine Mahon of Woodside, L. I. enrolled August 25th, 1945 having lost nearly half of her brain by operation on "brain-tumor" - doctors absolutely hopeless of her recovery. Two days later an enrollment was sent for the Poor Souls. From that day she be- gan to come back to herself. For several weeks was unable to remember - even faces - consequently could not recognize anyone. .. Now, thanks be to God, the brains seem to have grown back in place. She is figur- ing on coming to St. Michael's as soon as the weather permits. Again Deo Gratias. But why worry? "To worry about anything" St. Therese, the Little Flower claims, "is to indicate a want of confidence in God." She very likely speaks of excessive worrying; and yet, why should we worry a- bout anything - tumors? Cancers? Death? Why not rather turn to God, Whose solicitude for our individual welfare - temporarily as well as spiritually - puts all created solicitude out of the picture. Why not foster confidence in His divine Providence by humbly and in all child- like humility venture to remind Him - remind Him in the Person of our divine Brother Jesus - that we are His children - that we are, and at least want to be reckoned as amongst Eis "little ones"; and therefore, thank Him frequently for, not only the blessings of the past and pre- sent, but thank Him ahead of time for whatever He foresees is pleasing to Him that we suffer, and this not only in general but in each parti- cular case - leaving everything absolutely in His divine disposal, in- cluding with all its circumstances, when, where, and how He may be pleased to dispose the event of our death. Try something like this and see if it don't bring you a big in- crease of peace and contentmet. In my opimoon there is hardly any- thing else that the enemy of our souls dreads more than confidence - humble confidence in God. The lives of the saints abound with exam- ples of this virtue. Perhaps no where more beautifully than in the example of S: . Joseph with Mary, God's living Tabernacle seeking an abode wherin .. to give us Salvation. What an example of confidence it must have been to their thousand guardian angels - as Venerable Mary of Agreda was instructed to inform us, Mary had from the day of her Immaculate Conception. What an edification! And again what a surpassing reward that followed! What a HOLY NIGHT for them indeed! - a HOLY NIGHT, the positive dawn of humanity rescued. There has been something else in my mind, however, that I wanted to bring to your consideration. How about proposing to adopt one or more little ones - of whom Jesus assures us: "What you have done for the least of my breathren, you have done to me", if Eld give the doc- tors a surprise and get well? I find it always practical, especially in cases where all human scientifice help is despaired of, to just turn to the divine author of all good - always solicitous to be asked for favors - and with all the confidence we can muster, propose something that we are as- sured is pleasing to Him if we be only spared --? , or be granted the booned favor. But, to even try to raise children for God and society is so manifestly pleasing to God - and this, whether they be procured by natural generation or by adoption ( seemingly quite a matter of indifference to Him), that He has given a specially beautiful color- ing to the love of those whose privilege it is to have become earn- est faithful parents. So that quite appropriately the song of the Psalmist may be here also applied: " ... O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are His judgements and how unsearchable His ways!" (Rom. XI) I am herewith enclosing a letter of Fr. Edward's - rather a copy of Msgrs' that will speak for itself. I wish to stress the verse I have underlined: "God condescends to use our powers, if we don't spoil His plans by ours." Because He is always planing wonders for the patient and the humble. Hence His own blessed words: " .. Unless ye be converted and become as little children ... " Now I'll have to say Good Night. I had hoped to reach you with this before Sunday but I rather fear I am too late for that now.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your regards in send- ing me the telegram of your dear Edwin's passing - from time to eter- nity, from transitory struggling common to mortals, to the destiny, we trust where anxiety and struggling for existence gives place to confidence and union with every ideal ever dreamed of. If not this directly and fully, at least, please God, shortly to gain the crown and to hear the long hoped for greeting always awaiting the just and humble: "Come ye Blessed blessed of my Father possess to joys pre- pared for you ... " Now you are not only a orphan but a widow also. What does that mean? For you and for any one who have real faith and Christian hope it ought to mean "Another string broken that tends to bind our hearts to earth." It ought to mean that you you have now another faithful dear one as we confidently hope, a loving husband to pray for you beyond the grave together with your saintly Mother and Father and so many who have loved you and gone ahead. What a won- derful doctrine and consoling to think of our dear ones awaiting us with not only lited candles but greeting us at our arrival with music and hymns of heavenly sweetness. . .I've been thinking often of the really touch- family - reunion last summer in Seattle. But what about the great reunion awaiting the arrival of the just in Heaven! .. .I am inclined rather to congratulate you therefore, on another friend praying for you and awaiting your arrival as we hope Ed is ..

God bless you and yours. I hope this finds you continuing in good health and hopes and that things are brightening their smiles in your direction .. I am surely pleased to know of John and Marian doing better and sailing along more smoothly with their nice little family. Thanks be to God for the grace to do so. I started to write them away last winter - both of them - but was mostly in bed for a couple of months and that took quite a little pep out of me, so that for several long weeks I was able to do very little. I started to write Dorothy and Charles D'Amico too a number of times as well as yourself but I just do not know where the time flies to. We are sending an enrollment card for deceased Thomas Patrick La Plante to his poor, bereaved parents as directed. Now as to that primary problem of your own. I am not at all surprised that as time slips by and wounds of social bereavements heal, God's laws in common life as well as in the supernatural should seek to adjust their claims. I have no doubt but that our dear Lord and His blessed Virgin Mother has provided a remedy where-by to fully supply what He permitted for a time to be with- drawn from your social and family existence, - a sweet mother- love, a dear father-love, a devoted husband-love. Only just keep on praying for God's merciful guidance - for self and associates - and in His divine wisdom God will not fail you in His guidance for the best. Between the two outlooks in Seattle and Los Angeles, I am in- clined to favor that in the former. This especially if the judge's daughters (are) old enough to take care of themselves and their father's house. In such cases there is nearly always the danger of jealousy. I hardly need tell you of examples in this phase of social wanderings: for as Moore rightly muses: "Poor wanderers of a stormy day, from wave to wave we're driven; And fancy's flash and reason's ray serve but to light the troubled ways; There's nothing calm but Heaven." As for the financial or business affairs referred to, I just do not like to dabble into them. I will pray that the good God guide things - that He dispose everyone concerned, more and more to consider the great profit conscientious administration of tem- poralities can be to souls that try to become imbued with the pos- itive conviction that only lovers of justice can posess the King- dom of Heaven and to be children of God we must be lovers of Peace. Disregard for the claims of justice - under whatever pretext - has always been a manifestation of - to say the very least, of shallow thinking. Rather I would say its a betrayal of a want of' real thinking. In fact it seems to me that the all-outstanding character istic) of atheism is nothing other than just disregard for justice and truth. Atheism, to every normally thinking mind a most blasphemous suggestion of the devil; the "omega" - climax - of intellectual and moral depravity at once; the hopeless con- clusion and the desperate refuge of shallow thinking, of degener- ate minds and of really damned fools, - their primary leader none other than Lucifer himself the outstanding prince of diabolical deceivers and - by God's permission - dictator in-chief in the kingdom of Hell. Only just recently I received a communication as coming from our stigmatic Capuchin the famous Pater Pio, at San Giovani Rotondo, Italy. It is given as like a revelation to him from our dear Lord; and to my mind, in these days of so appalling advances of atheism as just about what is coming to this generation, so fearfully apos- tatizing from faith in God; which of course means from hope in the ... divine and from supernatural charity. Here is how it starts out: "With frightful roar of thunder I will come upon this sin-laden globe in a cold winter night. Scorching winds will precede this disturbance, and violent quakes will shake the earth. Flashes of lightening from fiery masses of clouds will set on fire and turn to ashes all that is in league with sin or is in- fected and corrupted by it, so that it must be destroyed. Then the human race shall realize that there is an all-powerful will over it, which will bring to naught its empty plans of gain glory. The wrath of God at the hands of destroying angel will per- manently cut down all the forces impregnated with deceitful and blasphemous sophisms which cannot nor never could be the teachings of My Gospel. ..... When the angel of death shall begin to carry out his lethal mission with the avenging sword of justice, and when hell shall cast itself in uproar and rage upon the just, especially on my victim souls, to destroy them with its frightening terrors, then it is that your faith and confidence in me must be firm as a rock. I will protect you; I will give you a sign which will indicate the beginning of My judgements. = "Man proposes; but God disposes" is an old proverb that has borne out truth of Scripture millions of times. And just these days of Atomic invention, it would seem that God might be permit- ting men without faith to be preparing the fearfully poisoned lightening fires with which He will arm His angels of wrath on an adulterous, defiant, atheistic generation. Another few lines from above referred-to: "In a cold winter night I will let thunder resound over the earth so that the very mountains will quiver. Quickly close your doors and windows; veil all vision to the outside world. Let not your eyes profane the most terrible of all' happenings with curious glances; for thrice holy is the wrath of God which will purify the earth for you, my remaining faithful flock. Commit yourselves to the protection of My holy Mother; and be not dis- mayed .... " P.S. What I'd like to stressits the very insanity of trying to reckon on anything material these days as amounting to any- thing of importance aside from its use in promoting the glory of God and charity toward lifting humanity - and the necessarily very short time such material things hold their evaluation, etc. P.S. II Dear Helena I am sending your letter on to Fr. E'd ..... Self understood you need not give - deliver the inclosed cards but if opportune - of course.

Thank you for your letter and the alms enclosed. May God reward you for your charity! Be assured of our prayers for your intentions, especially during Holy Mass each morning. Remembering you in my prayers and all your intentions.

"What is religion anyway?" asked a little 8 year-old. "What is Religion re Echoed in the ears of several. "Ah!" came an Earnest answer, "Religion is not only a science; Its the science of all science. It is the science of our happy dependence (we being each our own first neighbor) on God and our neighbor."

Still only half converted - at it since Oct. 1870. In front of St. Felix Chapel. Rational mortal: - 2nd Q. Why did God make you? God made me to know Him. O What a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. Its Heaven-begun for the grateful, on earth. - To treasure a'right! ? Highest Heaven its worth. There is nothing more rational in reason than to love God. By stifling reason and gratitude sin begets atheism. Atheism? The unqualified climax at once of intellectual insanity, of moral degeneracy, of diabolical blasphemy . Holy Saturday. God bless you Margaret - you and yours. I hope you keep well these days .... .Ah! days, as it would seem when atheism - the voice of Anti Christ - is demanding and get- ting a hearing. Barabas still prefered? . .

God bless you and all yours! I do hope you are keeping well. Best wishes from all in Detroit - Francis Molloy & family, who were here yesterday; Doonans, Sampsons, etc,; also from our niece Mary Casey, Jim's daughter and of course from Father Maurice - now Fr. Joachim, O. F.M. Cap., of Huntington, Indiana. His address St.Felix Monastery Route 8. Thanks be to God he seems well and hopeful of making profession in September. No doubt it must seem to you at times that I forget all about my one-time little sisters and brothers. I know I seldom write and am tardy in answering them when they write to me; at least I feel somewhat guilty that way. Be that as it may, I hardly think there is a day passes but what I remember you all. I have here before me letters started to the above S.M.T. Jan. 24th, Feb. 24 and March 25. That of Feb. nearly finished; yet ...? This ought to be a sort of indication that I at least sometimes do remember you. The fact of it is, I believe, that as time and distance separate me from the scenes and associations of my childhood and youth my recollections of both become sweeter and more reinviting - ...! ... But ...! The future holds a better part, .. .. " Surely we were fortunate children that the Good God gave us such sturdy, honest, virtuous parents. How can we ever be grateful enough? Thanks be to God! May their dear souls rest in the peace of the blessed! I often think of the wonderful designs of Divine Providence as revealed in the plans and strivings of these and simi- lar "children of St. Patrick" - so often pioneers indeed. In the case of our own dear Parents, e.g .; how they were directed from city-life in Boston and Philadelphia away to "The River Bank". At that time Prescot must have been little more than a village; and judging what the Eagle Rock - four, miles down the river - must have been at that time from what it was 15 years later, when I stayed two weeks at Aunt Mary Ann's, cone might get an idea of what a perfect hermitage in the wilderness might be. Here it was smiling down on the "Father of Waters", that five of us were privileged to breath our first morning air and "sing our first baby music", No doubt little Bernard must have been proficient in that music; because it was during his term of baby-hood that Papa went blind with the ague - when for two weeks he had to be led by the hand, and his little namesake got a rupture from which he never com- pletely recovered. Like in all other trials, however, the Good God had His designs herein also, and we can say with fullest conviction and in all gratitude To-day: "The Lord knows best." May He be in all His plans eternally praised! ... . How we must have thrived there in real unworldliness and Innocence1 Dangers of course were not wanting, to keep dear Father and Mother "on edge" and often, no doubt in anxiety. Wild beasts and rattlesnakes seem to been the most common cause of such anxiety, though two of our little cousins were drowned together just be- low our little retreat, in the River - otherwise so generous, so noble, so majestic. Trimbelle too !!! How removed! How primitive! How picturisque! How rich in its varity and abundence of wild flowers and fruits and nuts and berries! !! - with beautiful patches of grove to our west, illimitable forests off to the East (down on the "bottoms" and across the Willow River of that county. They call it the Trimbelle. To the South, were vallies and rolling prairies down to Diamond Bluff five miles below on the Mississippi - a fair pasture field for cattle as well as deer and other wild animals. But it was also a fair race- track for our most dreaded enemy the prairie-fire, that nearly every year would darken the sky in its crackling rush toward us through a- bundance of wild grass, prairie-tea, hazel and other brush. On such occasions "Lamb's Road", running east & west on ridge about 30 rods to our south nearly always proved a great protection. If the gale were not too strong our dear neighbors would have time to come to our rescue, as they often did by lineing up along that road and preventing the the fire from crossing. It was just a private road to a twenty- acre field off to our S.E. from the Miller farm on our S.W. The public road, such as it was, ran just past our little log cabin - a one-story mansion about 12 x 30 feet. You may smiles at this title I honor it with, especially when you learn that it had a single partition only be- low, "the bed-room" - Father and Mother on the one side and the little girls, Ellie and Maryann and little Mattie on the other - and the loft above where little boys slept and in the morning sometimes played till they quarreled as little boys are wont to do. An ordinary man could walk straight down stairs, but there was one young J.B. Fahey - six foot two - who was careful not to bump his head on the cross-joices and, therefore, had to stoop a little. The only door led in from the sunny end while a single window on each side let in the light.
