After finishing your letters for the 1st time last night I started to write both of you and your cousin Sister Mary Eileen Clare. I meant to get them done but it was nearing 11 p.m. and my eyes threatened a strike if I continues. I wrote your dear mother a few months ago when she was quite low. Thank God, I understand she improved some since. . · She seemed to pick up wonderfully two years ago at the happy reunion and Solemn 1st holy Mass. . . But how short the joys of earth! - and the sorrows too! Deo Gr. Clerical Novitiate - at present 23 novices, promising young men. We could place fifty priests tomorrow if we had them for the home and foriegn missions. Pray the Lord of the vineyard that He send laborers. Fr. Solanus
God bless you Sister M.J. Keep well - with mother and all.

You and your community. Yes we quite enjoyed our visit to Portland and out to your ideally located Mother house in Marylhurst - on our way to San Francisco and Los Angeles. .We are sending in separate cover book- lets pertaining to wonderful source of blessings, the Seraphic Mass Association. I am enrolling your dear Mother too in the Emergence list for the intention that she speedily improve in health - physically, mentally, spiritually. I hope she give the doctors a surprise. P.S. Yesterday received letter from Fr. Maurice E. Joachim and To-day one from Fr. E'd. Both seem feel- ing well. Deo Gratias!
"God bless you Sister Miriam James." "God condescends to use our powers if we don't spoil L His plans by ours."

God bless you and all yours. I hope this finds you well -- as, than is be to God it leaves me. I really do not know when I've written you last or how long I've been wanting to write you, though I hardly think there is a day passes that I do not remember you. However, your son John now our promising, young Jesuite Father Mc Closkey gave us the pleasure of a visit here yesterday; and so, I determined on writing you at least a few lines before letting it linger longer. Only a week or two ago I learned from some good friends of ours - O'Donnells - of Father John's presence so near, even in Chicago. The had been figuering on driving down ever since early in June, when they were very kind to myself and our Nep- hew Bernard Maurice, when we went out to St. Paul and from there visited Fr. Maurice Joachim in Gracefille. Our visit to poor, dear Maurice had to be short under the circumstances but I think we all quite enjoyed it. Both Fa- thers Maurice and Edward are quite well. Thanks be to God. We had planned on a solemn Mass on the 36th anniversary of M's ord- ination but the chapel is very small - just temporary; so I ser- ved his Mass and he surprised me how well he was able and served mine. It was Wednesday, the anniversary of his First Holy Mass instead of Monday of ordination and I had promissed the Father Guardian who at the time was not well, that I'd try hard to be back for Sunday. I had quite an important sick-call to make in Detroit - Royal Oak rather - on returning whic added about 375 miles or more of a trip. One of our convert Jews -- very clever who we hope will be a priest some day - drove me down from Detroit. We had quite a nice little visit yesterday and Saturday- evening. They all seemed to have enjoyed it. Fr. John had to be back this morning for his classes. So they left about 5 p. m. yesterday. I am sending you a couple of letters I think will interest you; as also a photo taken a little over a year ago. Of course its younger than the original. Anyhow I hope it may not disap- oint or scandalize

God bless you this most cherished feast of our Blessed Mother Mary. I do hope she may bless you specially - you and yours. However, to insure such a booned favor, we ought on our part try to find some way whereby specially to please her our so gracious blessed Mother. This we can hardly do better than by studying her life and trying to imitate her peerless practice of the Christian virtues - or any one of them - charity. pat- ience, purity, humility, temperance, etc. Of course if we remember and keep in mind that the greates doctors of the Church and theologians are unanimous in their conviction that even at the very first instant of Mary's soul's conception she received greater and more abundent graces than all other creatures taken together -- as the brightest moon outshines all the stars -- and that even the highest seraphim can follow only at a shadowy distance her Christ-like practice of the virtues as she grew in wisdom and grace before god and men

My Dear Niece Dorothy: - God bless you this dear, beautiful Feast of the most priviliged Spouse of Mary. May be too be watching over you and yours! I've been wanting to write you these many months. Indeed you have been on my mind quite a little ever since that memorable day we conclude with you and your little family on the "mount" in view of the majestic "old Ranier. Who would believe that nearly three years has passed since that day? How many more-times three, till we follow so many of our dear ones gone ahead of that land-mark event, and join even those who have followed since? -- poor, dear Brother Guss, (at least for me), one of the notables. I would like to continue playing with memories but time forbids me to waste it on events that have passed and do pass like soap-bubles, no matter how grand and gaudy, unless they pertain to the one thing necessary - knowing God better so as to love Him and serve Him better and save our immortal souls. For who can fully appreciate the privilege that Almighty God has given each one of us in just this possibility of our helping Him in the work of Redemption and thus saving our own "destiny for eternal glory?" "O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God!" You will be wondering what all this may be coming to; and there is so much that I would write you that a whole book would not exhaust it. So much, when I think of your dear Mother, Sister Nell or Ellie, as we used to call her in her mother-like efforts to make the rest of us contented and happy in the long decads back in our family history, in Prescott, in Trimbelle, in St. Croix Co. in Superior, Wis. I think you must have been the baby when she - your dear Mother - wrote that notable letter describing the 500 mile-trip to Christmas Mass, that I gave you last Nov- ember. At all events I wanted to have a heart-to-heart talk with you on that occasion but the shortness of your stay and circumstances made that impracticable for what I felt you and poor, dear Charlie needed. I could see from the start that he had something on his mind. He could not resis- Lamenting it in a little personal interview we had together. I'd never met Charlie before that refered-day on the Mouth and then a day or two afterwards out at aurelia's place on Lake Washington and I surely felt like congratulating you on such a husband and on the blessing God had be- stowed on your union - such dear children. I am going to skipp a whole lot that I am sure would interest us but you will be easily able to guess all about what would naturally follow if I had time to continue. So I would like just now to stress one feature of mutual harmony between man and wife that it seems to me must next to everything in matrimonial and family-life. What is it? ? ? I almost forgot to tell you first that a recent letter concerning your family - rather just a few lines of a report about you - took a tear from my eye: D. and C. and the whole family situation immeasurably improved." Pardor brevity. Now what I wanted to stress is this: The supreme importance for PEACE sake in a family that the husband or the mother, adjust their likes - their ideals - so as to harmonize with those of the other "life- partner", thus renewing and reenforcing their "courting-days affection" for oneanother, edifying the children and neighbors and, in this "vale of tears" helping to convince all concerned that after all the very possibility of our making the grade and gaining the eternal goal is worth infinitely more that the comparatively trifling sacrifices demanded. Just a little example that I now remember ought to make what I want to say, interestingly clear and per- tinent. About the time I was ordained ( 1904), the whole current press - Catholic as well as general - seemed to focus almost dangerously undue attention on a certain Tolstoi as the outstanding general genius of the hour and of the age. Said to be "handsom and extremely wealthy" without setting too much importance on either, Count Leo Tolstoi

4 - you and yours. And may the peace of the saints be ours, here and beyond the hopeful borders of this solemn pilgrimage - afterall but a momentary "vestibule to eternal realities". For the severalth time I am starting again a response to your pathetic plaint of April 24th. I do hope this finds you in every way as healthy and hopeful as it leaves us all here at the Friary. Deo Gr. How wonderful, even tho' full of mystery at every turn, are not His - God's own - works and ways! always in the final - never failing in the turning to the Glory of God and the happiness of the faithful, the appreciative, the grateful, and true. History abounds with examples most telling of this happy contention; mediaeval and modern as well as . nay, infinitely surpassing anything- in the ancient world, for real, "excelsior chivalry" and for inspiring loyalty to faith and eternal principle; - divine appreciation, remeration always infinit- ely in the leade. Beautifully romantic and hope-inspiring at once are always the examples of humble confidence, of unhesitationg obedience to God and authority, of persevering loyalty in the face of contradic- tion to faith and principles of RELIGION, -after all and in reality the only science that gives purpose to every other science, "The Science of our happy dependence on God and our neighbor." Or; if you will: "Religion, the Science of our happy relationship with and our providential depencence on God and our neighbor. Hopeful borders of this solemn pilgrimage

Only now I come to your letter of Dec. 190 - after Il p.m. God help us! I hardly know how the time slips by. Your cousin Mildred called from Chicago a week or so back and I had a little word with several of them including Captain Florence Casey was just then being transerred to Detroit Mich. Thanks be to God they all seem to be well - including even your Aunt - "Grandma Grace". In fact Grace gave me a pleasant surprise - a "congratu- lations ... " on my 83rd birthday. Your Uncles Pat and Owen also wrote and Mgr. Edw'd. All well Dec Gr .! Blessed be the Most Holy Trinity in every tick of time ! God bless you Eileen again - two months after this was supposed to be yours. Looking for something quite dif- fierent late last night I felt ashamed of myself to find these cards still "just snowed under" (all kinds of let- ters, etc) Please God I'll get it off today. I hope you are keeping well these days - at once so restless, so foreboding in in the materialistic world; yet by the grace and mercy of God, so colorful and so promising! It is just about ten years now that a certain Rabbi Rosenwasser lamented to one of our fathers ... the prevalence of atheism. The latter without a whis- per, wrote (the R's finger on the corner of the tissue-paper) "If any good is to come from atheism -- in itself the climax of insanity -- "Its going to force believers-in-God together.' 11 Hit- ting the desk, Rabbi exclaimed: "Thats Inspiration! It is hard to reckon the extent of modern martyrdom the Church has suffered these several decades and probably less possible to surmise what seems still-shortly to follow, the judg- ment awaiting enemies of Truth as the glory reserved for those who will have persevered ... suffering for justice, for Truth. .

Written - To the notes of "Believe Me if All" - (By Mamie G. Casey Mccluskey in 1913) With festival gladness we gather today, Dear old Daddy and Mother Machree, And with hearts overflowing sing homage to you On your Golden Jubilee. For fifty long years life's pathway adown, In devotion together you've trod With a tear and a smile in your eyes all the while, True as any to the "Dear Ould Sod!" In the May-time of Life, with our daily tasks o'er, We'd unite at the close of the day, Round you, then you taught us to kneel by your side, In love and thanksgiving to pray. In the world's field of battle, with hearts strong and brave, You marched, comrades faithful and true, Oh! may we, dear parents, wherever we rove- Be as loyal and steadfast as you. And may the sweet lessons of Faith, Hope and Love, That we learned, parents dear, at your knee, Be as beacons to guide us to Heaven above, While we sail over life's stormy sea. And now in the calmness of life's sunset glow, We are gathered once more round your knee, Fore'er in our hearts will burn homage and love, For you, Daddy and Mother Machree. I am sure with a little practic this sung as above ... will edify its hearers. Fr. Solanus Casey, OM Cap. Pl. Pardon Haste P.S. Please Mrs Plunket: This will be more than would be my going thither.

You've been on my mind frequently these days. I wanted to write you but getting aquainted in a new place keeps one on edge pretty much. I inscribed the names you sent me recently thru Rae Garland and I am surely pleased to know your able to keep up the good work. Thanks be to God. The above Monastery is where I made my annual retreat last week. It is across the Hudson from Lady Cliff convent and West Point Military College - the latter about a mile and a half up. Thank God it is quite an ideal place for quiet reflection and study. About 75 priests, Clerics and lay brothers, ...

for God's Holy Guidance - Thanks be to God Grandma! You've wethered another storm ... Congratulations! Pray for all the rest of us, that we learn to love God's holy will. God bless you Mrs. Plunkett God bless Grandma Plunkett and all her helpers and friends.
Please say a prayer that I may catch up with the correspondence. P.S. Many thanks for favor just noted.

I surely thank you for your practical way of remember- ing me on my 76th birthday. I hope the dear Lord may be pleased to leave yourself with us till you round out the 100. After all that cant be much more than a dozen years. So take courage and stay till your ripe enough for Heaven to take a "no stop-passage." . God's blessing and graces to yourself and to all our dear friends in Detroit.

Thank you for your kind favor of July 19, received and duly recorded. May the good Lord always give you true interior joy. Yes God bless you Grandma Plunkett. Keep young in heart and pray for us youngsters - clear down to youngest great-grandchild.

Many thanks again for your cooperation in the privileged work of the poor missions. Thanks be to God, though my shins are stiff and a little swollen, they are improving and I hope in a short time to get at my regular schedule. I hope nothing serious be found with Esther and that she be back soon in good shape. I just received a letter from Fr. Maurice in Gracevill Minn. You remember he was six years in Mt. Hope San. Baltimore. Thank God he seems to coming along o. He was installed out there as Chaplin last Mar. Msgr. Edw'd still working in St. Paul - till his Most Rev. Bishop call him back to the Islands - lecturing, giving missions, retreats, etc. . God bless you one and all again.

- Many thanks for your charitable favor of several week past duely received and noted. Please pardon my so long delayed acknowledgement. Keep well and pray for the conversion of the rest of us -- poor sinners as we all are.

I just received your air favor and have inscribed you in the Seraphic Mass Association for your special Intent. Please God I hope things may brighten soon in regards to that same. However, and by all means shake off that anxiety of yours. Last year it was about something that now you smile about. To-day its about some thing that will not be serious if you raise your heart to God every time it comes to your mind and thank Him for whatever is to come.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of July 17th. I am sure Fr. Lambert acknowledged same befor. Leaving for a trip to see an invalid brother of mine in Baltimore. I took your letter along hoping to answer it as it deserves to be answered; but I find myself almost as busy on my "vacation as in the office in Detroit. However, before I leave here as expected right after dinner, I want to assure you of my appreciation and that I shall surely include Joseph O' Donnell in my poor prayers as well as yourself. Now it's time and for the present I'll say Goodbye and again

In acknowledgement of your charitable gifts of Five Dollars for which we are extremely grateful, and for your civic minded interest in the welfare of God's poor. Pl. pardon delay in acknowledgement. Hope by this time things have adjusted themselves brigher and better than before. P. S. God bless you Mrs. O"Donnell again. Having written the acknowledgement over several weeks ago without mailing it at once, I just found it snowed under other work. I hope things have adjusted themselves brighter before this. Brs. Francis and Leo and all send Best Regards. Now that the season for it is fast approaching we wish you all the blessings that go to make a really blessed Christmas and Happy New Year.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for kind favor of June 29th. I hope that you are back from your trip to the S.West. that you found things favorable and may you profit in many ways. More when I get settled in this new location. Many thanks for your prayers. Please keep them up.

God bless you and yours. Having noted your kind reques several weeks ago (Aug. 29) I hoped to find leasure for a few details. I've put it off again and again and its the same thing. Ny letters acumulate more and more. At al events I thank you (if I havent done it before anyhow). I hope those annoying problems in the S.West have adjusted by this time. We'll continue our prayers that things improve. God bless you again.

In short a joyful Blessed Christmas and success spiritually and temprarely the follow- ing year - years. P. S. The fruit is excellent ·-- Two big bushels really worth while God bless all. God bless and protect all who follow the inclosed St. Christopher --- just blessed.

My Dear Friends: God bless you and yours. Many thanks indeed for your charitable favor noted yesterday. I came just in nice time - especially the smaller cheque - to enroll quite a number of my friends in the Ser Mass Assoc'n for a Christmas gifte. - a double, tripple charity. Thinking you were down in Texas for the Winter I addressed a letter to you only last week - to Palner Hotel Mc Allen Texas - the address as - indicated on the baskets of fine fruit that came to us in your name - and for which I want to thank you again - for the twofine baskets of delicious fruit. You will very likely receive the letter forwarded withe relics of V.Nother fary of Jesus, of Agreda, which had inclosed.

Just uncovering Tin's letter of Jan. 13 I determined without further delay write you at least a few lines. - Better waiting for time to write a letter. First I've been wanting, it seem to ne two months, to thank for that second deliver; from the "Grove" - if anything an improvement on the 1st. The Brethren surely appreciated then. Then Many thanks for your mission-activity - and Win's too - in the many enrollments, including the old simmer who has given us here so much conscience trouble, Fr. Solenus - and the other features of your monthly donations - so often (as must seen to you) unappreciated. I do hope you are both enjoying your vacation in your sumy S.Western sojoum Praised be Jesus and Mary.

God bless you and keep you well. - you and yours. I'd like to write you a real letter but this is just to thank you for crate of fine oranges received here in excellent condition a few days back. They are very good. - in fact I think the best yet. How wonderful is the dear Lord in all His works!

God bless you Josph O'Donnell - you and yours. I was in hopes to catch up with my correspondence and then write you, but it seems the letters come faster and faster so that I have to keep right on the job; and the longer I wait the more what's not too urgent gets snowed under. At all events I want to say at least thank you for the big crate of fine Grape-fruit. Nony thanks indeed. ^You can see for yourself. this is hardly an expert an underwood.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your generous favor of March 19, duly received and noted. I am surely pleased to lmow of your privileged trip to the famous Shrine of Guadalupe, and especially of the hoped-for improvement in your health as surely a part consequence. I surely congratulate you and Mrs. O'Donnell on such a pleasant and praisworthy experience. Deo Gr. Now in regard to the laudable proposition you dream about, vis, the education of a candidate for the Holy Priesthood: I would consider such a proposition as always more or less of a supernatural inspiration. There is so much call for such activity - real Catholic Action - that, as I believe, there are comparatively few outside the Bishops and Superiors of the different Orders who realize its crying necessity. Personally and just at present, however, I would be relictent to advise in such a proposition, when I low of others, in consequence of their office or position who would be pleased and better able to guide you than I might. Hence I am referring your laudable proposition/our Father Provincial, the very Rev. Father Clement, OF. .. Cap. who's address is 1740 Mt.Elliott Ave.Detroit 7, Mich. He, perhaps better than anyone in the Provinc of Saint Joseph, would know best how to advise in such matters. I do imow that the education of poor students and candidates has always been quite a problem in our educational institutions. Often some of the brightest and most promising students come from poor familites and I am quite sure we have never as yet "turned down" on account of financial shortage. However, it is none the less quite a problem for the Province of St. Joseph - your own dear Patron. So I am sure that whatever you may fee able and disposed to do for the Province/ would be gratefully appreciated. P.S. Dear Joseph: I shall inform Father Provincial of your proposition and will probably hear from him before long. He naturally must feel a relief whenever he finds anyone able and willing to help in such a financial difficulty.

Many thanks for your recent favors - duly received and noted. We are preparing for the glorious Feast of Corpus Christi this Thursday and next Sunday - with procession and Benediction at the Monastery - garden Shrine, at 2:30 the latter date. It would be an edifying treat - the only time in the year that the Garden is open to Cath. public. . . . Furthermore, since our Father Provincial was called to Rome to be Most Rev. General; we are to have a provincial Chapter, July 11 - 14th. Please help us storm Heaven for guidance. . . Praised be Jesus!

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your recent favor - duly received and noted. Rev. Fr. Provincial - Fr. Clement evidently appreciated your generous offer to help educate clerics, etc. for the Holy Priesthood. He was unexpectedly called to Rome about the time. An appreciative letter seemed to be about all he could send me in this regard. He hoped at his conclusion to get in touch with you later on. I was surprised - not unpleasantly - at my transfer hither to St. Felix. Only about 90 miles from Chicago. So I'll be expecting to see you some of these fine coming Nay days.

God bless you and keep you well - you and yours. I am glad to know you enjoyed your southern - S-Western trip and especially that you are returned safe and sould. Thanks be to God for all his wonderful, merciful designs. Many thanks to you also for your kind favor just noted. As to the Groves and the young trees; well we'll hope the enroll- ments and prayers otherwise may work something in their favor. We had quite an example here this past Spring and Summer. On the third of May (I believe that was the date), we had quite a heavy frost just when the apple-trees and grape-vines were nicely in bloom. We were rather anticipating what came; so that, in hopes the frost might be thwarted some way, one of the fathers went through the whole, plot or plotts, with stole and ritual and holy-water blessing everything. Alas! Next morning, you can imagine our dismay. Notwithstanding the blessing the frost had come and seemingly frozen many of the apples and about 95% of the grapes. It surely looked hopeless, especially in the vineyard. Father Guardian, now over 76 who had done so much pruning, etc. last Fall and during the Winter, felt worse, seemingly than anyone else. Only yesterday, in a talk he gave us, he acknowledged that he could have cried. Nevertheless inside of ten days other shoots came out and blossomed and now the younger, to everyone's surprize, seem bigger and more promising than the first . Deo Gratias The apple-trees and others, especially the pears and some of the peaches look very promising this morning, if only now the dear Lord sends us a good rain; for we have had it quite dry for the last six or seven weeks. We are praying that during the octave of our Bl. Mother's Assumption at least we may have the favor from Heaven of a good rain. I am surely pleased to know that the Garland Family is doing so well and that Rae and Mrs. - Sr. - enjoyed their privileged pilgrimage to the famous shrines of St. Joseph and good St. Ann. May they live long and have many such happy experiences. P.S .- like. Thanks be to God and our Blessed Mother - The Mystical City of God - the good rain has come! Everyone a person meets seems to appreciate the great good it has done. Praised be His Holy Name ! Yes I would be glad to see you again some of these beautiful days. However, just incidently, the third Sunday of the month is visiting day for the novices and that is more or less a pritty busy day, especially for the laybrothe and the novices themselves. Another day, therefore, might be preferable.

God bless you Joseph and Winnie. Just a few words this time to catch you before going S.W. - in case you desid it necessary. An enrolling "Emergent-lenager and Employees of O'Donell's Texas Pruit Parm." I hope things smoothe off without any serious difficulty- and that the trouble prove "just a little ripple on the surface ..... Many thanks for your kind favor of Sept. 6. I had my two Rev. Brothers Misgr Ed and Fr. M. E. Joachim last week. The latter left yesterday. Expect former back from Boston in week or so ..... Again many thanks and God love and keep you both .... Just say the Our Father sloly and devoutly for above trouble.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor - rather from Win- Chicago via Texas reenforce by Joe., just noted. I do hope that things brighten up before the week is over and that you return to the temperat zone relieved and at least content if not satisfied with the outcome of your, more or less force visitation. It almost seems too bad that it was not a couple months later, sothat you might escape some of the probably cold months we are likely to be in for before the ripening of the next oranges, etc. At all events try and shake of as much as you can of that over-due worry, so common to Chinese, etc business-men - like the O'Donnells and Kes, O'Caseys and Mulligans, etc. We are having quite ideal days here in the vicinity of the Wabash and Maumee "water-shed the one heading for the S-West to the great Gulf, the other North-east to the Great lakes and the shrines of Mont Reall, Qubec and across the briney Atlantic, etc. I sometimes imagine I'd like to follow them - as when a small child, when I was wont to coach little bark " boats" down the rills of melting snows to bigger ravines and deeper waters, - - forgeting all about soaked shoes and torn trouser and often thinking of my soul's journey to eternity. What happy days those! Why? I suppose because we knew nothing of sin and worry, and everything waiving to the wupernatural. Still, as dear Mother remarked on the occasion of her golden wedding when talking about events and places familiar fort and more and less back some one remarked: "Wouldent it be nice if we could go back to those days?",Mother answered as half to herself: "Thanks be to God, I'm glad its over." I thought afterwards, infact it there was something in her voice that seemed to reinvision the trials of those pioneer days in West Sisconsin - happy as it was for the youngsters - as days of trials and struggles outweiging the pleasures, save that she was doing God's holy will, doing something for God and humanity and in hopes of brighter days as the years ripened for her promising family that she was then coaching on the one great pilgrimage to eternity. The peace that still still hovers on her brow - photo on that occasion of her golden wedding - bespeaks the something of joy in her soul at the rememberence of those day of trials for her as well as something of the confidence that filled her heart - confidence - that she had tried at least not in vain, to come up to ideal of raising a family for God and His Church. Incidently, I am not sure if I ever showed that photo. Ic case of neglect on my part heretofore, please remind me when you come the next time and I shall be pleased, as I am sure you will be. Please pardon if this is getting too drawn-out. I'll try and cach you before you leave for the North. God bless you again and I want you to bring me something about the conversion of that manager of yours down ther - or of one nearer the ideal.

Yes, just starting my 77th anniversary as your wrie held me up at my above, first period after the date, - just starting to answer your charitable letter received this am. Many thanks for your generosity as well as for so kind a rememberence on this ocasion. I had some friends down from Detroit yesterday to remind me of and to congratulate on my 76thB-day. I was on retreat last week and on Sunday went to Detroit and in the evening to Windsor, Ontario, Can. to the "Send-off celebration" given to Fr. Julius O.F.M.Cap. by his old friends in the parish of his childhood - Our Lady of Prompt Succor. He was supposed to leave for Guam Missions in November. It was Monday evening when we returned and I felt I must get at my work and catch up, etc. Well, Deo gratia for every thing! Thanks be to Go. As to your German candidate farm-manager's system of religion - lutheran: well, it might be better and would certainly be more promising if he were Imown to be a practical Catholic; but if he give evidence of honesty and the fear of God and thrift as best he can - with experience bhind him, I would be water inclined to him rather than to a fresh graduate from most/ of our universities who have had little or no practical farm experien. After all the lutherans, as a rule, know more of Christianity than most any of the other non-catholic Christian denominations. Besides, these day protestantism as a whole seems to be rapidly crumbling. The whole trouble with honest protestants - and thank God there a lot of such - is that thy simply do not know the real relationship between their own denomination and the Mother-church. Otherwise equal, I would take a conscientious lutheran ten times in preference to just a nominal Catholic. I know from childhood how to appreciate German lutherans. If the change of clamate benot too radical and this man's wife and daughter can aide, etc, I would be inclined in his favor. In the mean time, however, let us pray for divine grudance - especially turning to St. Josep and the Poor Souls. How about inviting the latter to - especially our own relatives amongst them - to take an interest with us and become missionaries with a promise to enroll them, e.g., for a certain % of the proffits. That I always call a double charity; to our neighbor, viz, to our fellow members of the militent Church, the missionaries and their work and then to the Church-suffering, the poor, holy souls. Several years ago and frequently later on, I was assured that one of the great factors in the financial success of "old-man Rockefellow" was often attributed to his having kept a promise to spend something like 10% of his profits to one or other charitable work. I am quite inclined to take stock in such a report. I have seen the like work out in other cases. Plese pardon my prolongation of this conclusion. I meant to close in just a line or two here. Just another case of: "The more hury the less speed". God help us. I was just looking for something else - a copy of that letter I was writing to the big policeman, MeClellan of Detr't and that I wanted to "point up a little" - and I find two of the above and bothe marked "copy". So I must conclude that you never received either. I need no further excuse for tardiness this time - and perhaps more to be regretted of something less or more regrettable ?!?!? Thank the dear Lord for mistaks too. And thank Him that its not ten-times worse. Possibly the delay may to havebeen a salutary one. Please God it may not be other.

Many thanks for your generous favors - fruits excellent - and checks, prayers, etc. I have been with this on my mind for weeks 21st Only late last nigh did I get to read your very interesting letter of the 16th. Thanks be to God! How wonderful was His delicate "hold- up" of that letter I had marked "Copy." ....! I sure congratulate you on seemingly providential guidance on your late trip But after all, what might we not expect if we would trust in God and leave things more and more in His divine hands. Simplicity and confidence in God was the real secret of Young Tobias' success in the Old Testiment - and Jacob's too. I will try and send the certificates - and write to Mrs. Goodwillie soon ..

I just received your letter of yesterday and am hoping to see you Monday night. Do not wory about coming late. It is very seldom I get on the matress till after 10 'clock. Only last evening I wrote my Niece, Mrs. Dean Conley, of (I just have not the number) N. Riordan Road, that you were coming and asking them to get word to you I expected you. I invited them too. I want you tomeet them. I think you would enuoy eachother's company. As for the Farm: Well, ofcourse such temporalities are always more or less a cause of worry what ever way one takes them. As you say: the times are so very upset and abnormal that it is no simple problem to carry on successfully at or with most any business. One hardly knows what to turn to or to invest in. I hoped from your letter a month or so ago - and I am sure you felt that way - that your visit to the S.West was providentially in your favor. I am inclined to confidence anyhow in Mr. Costello. Perhaps we ought to pray more for him and wait gently, viz, that he become a little more unselfish, etc. However, I was talking with Father Coughlin during that threatening Coal-stike about the general outlook and he wastelling us that the finantial-Jews seemed to be expecting a seriou depression, from the fact that at that time they were selling everything they could. Therefore, he concluded as did others, that they were figuring on something worse than came at least from that strike so far. I suppose that we can hardly do better than just pray on, doing the best we know from day today and trust in divine Providence with out too much anxiety. May the Good God guide us all! I was just speaking to Father Guardian - our local Superior about inviting you and the Conleys and he too will be expecting you. He said: " .. We can acomodate seven guests nicely and fi necessary some of the men could be otherwise acomodated. The Conleys have two little boys, the younger must bealittle over two years old. If you dont mind you could call them up to that effect. INcidently, the old violin just arrived this p.m. and is in good condition. Thanks be to God for all His unsearchable designs. In the mean time do not forget to say little prayer now and then that I make a little faster progress in conversion the coming fifty years than during the past. Ofcourse the next will probably shorter than the past twenty-five.

Feb. 5th - 10:30 pm - Before postponements How wonderful is the Lord in all His ways! How can we ever appreciate - be gratiful !!! I enjoyed your letter. . . . Not that this or that person was directly concerned, but it would be a happy theme if one had time a ability to go into details of such a privilege and such a manifestation of God's mercy and generous condescention to any - to us - poor sinners. Thanks be to God for all His hidden designs - as well as for those we praise as manifestations. Fr. Guardian just came across the corridor (almost expected a reminder to retire) to tell me we would have the High Mass on Friday for you and your intentions - the first of five for your Int. - besides Enrollments

My Dear Mr. Costello: God bless you and yours. The O'Donnells told me several weeks ago that you were writing me -- having told me quite allittle about you for several past months. Only just now did I come across your interesting letter of February 26th -- somehow mislaid -- that I've been looking for. So I am not keeping you in any possible suspence as to my identity, interest, etc. You ask about Appleton, Wisconsin. It was in St.Joseph's Church in that neat little city where I had my first Holy Mass, July 31st 1904. God be blessed.Deo Gr. No. I can not say that I am exactly from St. Paul, Minn; though many a pleasant day I spent in that thrifty city - with relatives and friends and in the Seminary, as guest. Coming two years in June, on my way to Seattle, I visited an old friend of mine Mike. Costello who had been moldest brother's bare-foot-boy friend on our farms sixty-five years before and about forty miles down the River on the Wisconsin side. Later, when I was about 17, I did a term in the Stillwater Penetentiary (less thantwo months), and I found Mike there ahead of me and we became bed-fellows - he a boiler-maker and his partner just "a roustabout". However, we had our sleeping-quarters outside the wall. Some years after that the one became a lieutenant in the Saint Paul police- department; the other a poor Capuchin and a priest. Mike was in his 80s and wasalmost hlind when we went to see hm on said trip - seemingly rejuvanited at our visit. Ihhad spoken to him on the phone a number of times but for over thirty years had not seen him. So that, when our O'Donnell Friends seemed disapointed several weeks back I felt there must be a mistake or a misunderstanding "in the woodpile" somewhere. Thanks be to God for all interested it turned out to be so, - just another blessing in disguise I trust. For I feel that as you learn to know these friends, as I have known them for several years, you will come to feel that you are rather working with them than just for them. Indeed I hope such feeling of confidence may become generously mutual between you. God bless you all again.

God bless you J.J. and Win. I'd write at length .. but I just want to thank you for favor of the 8th. Thank God for M.C's change! ! He could not have received my letter befor Monday. - sent Friday on 3¢. It only heightens my hopes in God's designs . . How wonderful! . Brother Pat. has snapped out of dange. . Deo Gr.

You and yours. Many thanks from myself and our whole community for your generous donation of fruit received in perfect condition, - two fine big eratis shiped March 17th (Irish holy-day! ), and four fine baskets March 22nd. May our dear Lord bless yourself - as also everyone who in any way has been interested. · . What a privilege to do a favor for God in doing for our neighbor! The same too can be said of being appreciative and grateful for such favor - Communion of saints.

Many thanks for your kninly generous favor receive and noted yesterday. I am glad to know that you are well and that the outlook is bright for your Daughter Adelaide. I hope she may have best success June 5th is most important and - , seccess that day or no srecess - that she strive by every means that our holy Mother the Church offers us, to keep close and dear to the Holy Family, Jesus, Mary and Joseph. I was rather disapointed, as I quite surmised it reght along, that yourself and Mr. O'Donnell failed to understand eachother. However, as you write I hope it was best that you parted. One thing about it I am more than pleased with, viz, that you both seem decidedly charitable toward oneanother. I do hope to know that you keep up that really edifying and friendly feeling. All this even with a touch of "ire" on either side. I am glad too that while it was quite out of the question for him to leave Chicago the last several weeks you were with him, his Wife Winifred was able to go down and prepare things for the meeting and procuring of a new care-taker. He followed for a "week-end" absence and they seem quite satisfied that they struckin with a quite desirable successor. How wonderful the ways of the good God when we foster confidence in Him by just leaving at least somthing that seems important for Him to take care of! Blessed be His Holy Name.

Just as a sord of P.S. Dear Friends "The O'Donnells". "The more hurry the less speed", the old say- ing could easily be applied to the other side of theis "document". I guess it hardly pays for an apprentice to speed up too much. Any how I thought you'd be pleased to know that I received quite an appreciative letter from M.C.C. I think what "raised his fethers" about my letter before, was my having quoted you as intimating that his heart-attack had possily left him ? not exactly himself. But really that feature just amused me. Otherwise it was a nice letter and quite indicative of a charitable feeling to the O'Donnells. June 5th P.S. Just straightening up for our trip tomorrow P.M. I came across this carbon I thought was off last week am almost ashamed to send it. My nephew Bernard Maurice (Owen's Son) is with me since Monday. He will acompany me on his way to Seattle.

Prepared by patient suffering and by the Sacraments and prayers of our holy Mother the Church, on August 14th With joyful countenance received the final call of the divine Lover, Bridegroom of our souls and gently passed to Eternity. Perpetually - with her whole family deceased and living
with whole Family - on both sides, deceased and living, parents, children with brothers and sisters of both - as one whole - ( enrolled ) a perpetual membership.

God made me to know Him. O what a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. It's Heaven begun for the grateful on earth. To treasure aright !-?-! Highest Heaven its worth. - God himself - even here. God bless you Joseph J. O'Donnell - you and yours. I hope this finds all 100% yourselves in the grace of God - smiling after the wonderful rain He sent us, like lillies and roses. I started these cards several days ago but some how or other they are later than intended and far from what I wanted. However, the little German saying "Nichts ..- " consoles me: "Nothing perfect in this world." In other words, no one is here on this side of Heaven fully converted. Thank the good God, He has infinite patience ! - Adored be his Holy Name!

Many Thanks for your thoughtful kindness, with six crates of fruit that in perfect condition arrived Today. - about which, later. You are fortunate to be in the sunny South-west these days, - rain and snow in a sort of contention and gale from the N.E. urging them on. May the Lord bless your care-taker Johnson and family. I feel that I sort of know them too. Best regards. We pray for them too.
Here are the verses - some of them at least - I referred to Sunday-night. Before further neglect I'll put them in and they'll escape being "snowed under."

new Feast of "Maternity of Mary Bles'd Virgin." May this find you all in the best of outlooks - with lively, firm and ardent faith, hope and charity! - the triune virtue. I am just enclosing the belated account referred to over long-distance last night. I hope you may find it worth while.

Febr.22nd. My Dear Friends: God bless you one and all. Just a word to meet you down there as friend from up north. I hope it may please the Lord to bring you back in better weather and brighter hopes than saw you start on the trip I'd like to have made with you. Permit me to follow in spirit! At the same time, seeing your rather undue concern at dropping prices, etc, I thought a word of observation might help a little to steady someone's nerves. First of all, however, we should re-remember at all events, that success or want of the same is not essential as pertains temporalities. Sooner or later we shall have to drop them - if they don't drop us first. Why, therefore, lose our peace on their account? Then again, God often permits us to make temporal blunders in order to foster humility in our souls so that in the sight of Heaven we may be more amible. Finally this is "Presidential Election year." That means more or less a depression in farm prices at least till after Election-day. Business men will not invest till Election.

(March 27) God bless you Joseph J. O'Donnell - with Winnie and all your dear ones. As surmised when phoning last Sunday, I was set for your high Mass on Wednesday but that morning Fr. Guargian whispered to me a little change in schedule in your favor. "We'll offer the solemn Mass for the O'Donnell intentions next Sunday. Write them to that effect ... " I wanted to do so that day - and every day since and now its almost time for the daily "pick up" So I'll add our simple Easter greeting and felicitations with a hearty God's blessing to all repeated for all the Easter Season.

April 10th 1948. God bless you Joseph O'Donnell. - you and yours. I hope you are all well. Thanks be to God my strength seems to be coming back in pretty good shape, though rather slowly. I hope that Fr. O'Donnell is improving by this time and that the good God may give him the needed patience. Shortly after his consecration Bishop Murphy of Saginaw met with a serious accident that put him on his back for about six months in same position. A year afterwards his condition was perfect. Thanks be to God! We'll include Fr. O'D. in our prayers.

My Dear Friend Joseph: God bless you and yours, especially Mrs; ofcourse. Just a short word Tonight to tell you a little about Rev. Father Guardian's transition, as we all hopeto his better place in God's providence beyond the grave. First, however, I want to thank you for your kind favor of last week, duly received and noted as requested, which I forgot to acknowledge over the phone the night-before-last. About a year ago Father Guardian - Mtthias - took a very threatening turn and for several months, till early March, was not really able to come down to the refectory or to choir-services. During that period he was able to sleep very little and that only in the chair. However, it would seem he'd been reading the lifeof one of our great modern missionaries, the late most Rev. Bishop Hartman of India, and made a noveina to his honor and in petition that he do something for him, to be able at least to fulfil the principal duties of his office. Athe the end of the novena, thanks be to God and the great missionary, Father Guardian came to Choir and refectory and also to recreation up to the very last. Even Sunday night, just a few hours befor his final sleep, he seemed even more than usually entertaining; so that one would almost think he would'nt mind conversing all niggt. He was always a great reader and though apparently cared little about showing his ability, the advantage of his reading and study was often manifest. What was better, he was a man of lively faith with an unusually wide experience and with trials and hardships from early childhood that were hardly ever wanting to tame and to mellow and soften his naturally firey nature. Peerhaps the bitterest disapoint of his whole life was that regarding his, from-early-childhood vocation to be a priest in the Capuchin- Franciscan Order; - a disapointment which having been suffered in resignation, was lifted in God's own merciful way and time; - surely an example in confirmation of St. Paul's " "For those who love God, all things turn for the best." He had become cigar-maker in early boyhood to help raise the big family, of which he was the eldest; and then a gardner and musician, etc. etc; when he learned to his great joy and hope, afteras was generally thought to be too late to study for the holy Priesthood, that in America there was still a possibility of becoming a priest and at that, a Capuchin Franciscan. His smoldering hopes at once revived and as soon as possible he came to America. He had never an incling of the knocks and dispointments still between him and the realization of his goal. Neverthe less, as his calmness of countenance attested while he waited for the undertaker, in exactly the position he had taken for his last long seep -- with his left foot on the stool, his hand under his head inclined to the same side and his rosary over his sholder. The Father who was to have the last holy Mass that morning tiptoed in and out, to see the special intention, never dreaming but that Father Guardian was just supplying, as usual, something of the sleep so much of which he was wont to miss during the nights. Surely his desire to "die in the harness", as he had so often expressed it -- and even about forty hours before, after his solm Mass in the morning and sermon at Brither Cook's final profession, -- was happily realized. Thanks be to the merciful God. How wonerful in His all ways! His long experience as superior and the difficulties metwith during his whole life, by the grace of God, had fitted him to be a really ideal Father Guardian. Much as I was with him - and I assisted him at his first and second holy Masses - I never but once saw him as really "next to upset"; and that was in connection with something that fell to my duty to execute. I was indignant myself at the very appearance of the situation, as I realized at once that it must appear to him. I surely sympathized with him as I saw him just ready to call me down and as I felt he would be fully justified if appearance had not deceived him. Less than ten words fully satisfied his demand without my even hanging up a long-distance call. The first chance he had afterward, he expressed regret at his manifestation of his weakness. May his dear soul rest with the saints!

Having hinished a card to Mrs. - your winnifred- last night, I want to get this off together with it before I forget and something be "sowedunder. I started to kinda started to moralize in my short card but it seemed to me after I was through that my effort was rather vague. At all events I'm giving it to the air this Morning and hope it contribute something to her encouragement. For, this side of Heaven who is there living that neads no encouragement now and then, at least. How, beyond all conception of creatures, how marvelously has not our divine Master Jesus provided such encouragement - with consolations against trials and difficulties undertaken, even when only partly and imperfectly for His dear sake, that, if only appreciated properly on our part, lend to our "lot otherwise in this vale of tears", - Ah! colors and hopes that surpass in reality even the joys of humanity before the Fall in Paradise. O! If humanity could only appreciate, - if in studying appreciation and gratitude in the School of Jesus and Mary - what a taste of Heaven humanity would be given even in this earthly vestibule! Appreciation? Gratitude! Hense the little verse: God made me to know Him ! O! What a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. It's Heaven-begun, for the grateful ON EARTH. To treasure aright ! ? ! Highest Heaven its worth. God Himself is the principal reward even here for each one of us inasmuch as we learn to appreciate; in asmuch as we put on Christian Gratitude. Glory be to God in the Highest! Bles't and prasd be the Hearts of Jesus and Mary!

God bless you Mrs. O'Donnell. - away on the range Many thanks for your kind favor from the "fronteer and the the fields of cotton. The dotton-blossom was quite a surprise I'd like to go into some details but this isonly a card. and I have about twenty other Joes I outht to write Today besides your J.J. So you'll be easy in me for taking only a card and perhaps let me have a prayer for inspiration and guidance rather than a frown. Really, I think both you and Joe have an occasion for merit even in this experience of manifold-sacrifice. It seems to me just too bad that every one of us hear those words of Jesus: " ... He that hath left ... for my sake, etc, will receive a hundred-fold even ... and not to every here in this life ... " - as to some one else trial and cross What an inspiration these and such promises ought to be toevery one of us! O! If we would only learn to keep an eye on ourselves, viz, onour inordinate and unreasonable inclinations to pamper our own whims and desires, etc instead of like Jesus, catering to and adjusting Himself to the Will,not only of His heavenly Father but to the meanest and lowest of men In other words: " .... even to the death of the Cross." St. Terese thinks that the memory of our trials in this exile on earth, will be, as among the sweetes joys in our heavenly eternity. She's rit even as for Jesus our blessed God will be His Crudifixion. So, courage. fortitude! humble gratitude! ...

God bless you and guide you. - you and yours. I was just with Joseph J. He said had been in long distance touch with just before and - God help, us another disapointment! Well ?...? It is a problem what to do - or what it may be possible to do. One thing, which in the final will much mean much is to try again and again in time of any crisis, to keep our old heads from overmuch wrrying. At times of course this will seem impossible but God is always pleased to see us turn to him and His saints and try on. These days especially we just cannot surmise what may be ahead of us. However, that is nothing specially new, for its more or less the same story at ever tum in our earthly pilgrimage. In other words, it would seem that the great lesson Godhimself would want us to learn on that pilgrimage, is appreciation for the Life Eternal He has waiting for us, if by correspondence with His grace we begin to wean ourselves from this temporal - "momentary existance .... courage therefore ... Heroism! In God's grace are we not spouses of Jesus Crucified ...

Many thanks for your kind letter and favors of Dec. 18. Rest assured that I will add my prayers to the Masses for the intentions you mentioned in your letter. The names and intentions have also been inscribed in the records of the Seraphic lass Assn.

God bless you Joseph J. - with Win and all. I just read your interesting letter of July 5th and we surely appriciate your zeal and generosity. Many thanks and God's reward. We pray and trust that the new care-taker's hopeful report may turn out to have been not too optimistic. My new Rev. Associale, Fr. Simeon called my attention to special reference to enrollment of my Intent's. I just asked that he put it down in your own words. "I have plenty of them - and the O' Donnells always included. Thans be to God: I am feeling well again after just two weeks in the Hospital. Thanks be to God too for the ideal weather He has been sending us lately - not over hot during the day and cool rights. Many thanks and God's blessing to each and all. - Fr. Solanus, ofmc

God bless you Nrs. O'Donnell, away out there in the (once-upon-a- time) wooley West, in reality just across the Mississippi some 25 miles up from my birth - blace - 4 miles below Prescott. At that time in 1870 it was indeed a pioneer portion but a wonderfully picturesque section of the Country. Well I just had a talk with Joe and we are surely pleased that your trouble is so hopefully checked - and promising. I hope it may prove to have been the climax, left over from the old year, etc after all, however if, "Thoom the Lord loveth He chasteneth," we ought to thank God for the privileg of being mode to resemble His divine Najesty ... so now I'll say Good Night and again God bless you and yours - speedy recovery . . . Fr. Solanus, O.F.K.Cap.

I hope you are well and that you may enjoy your exile down there and find it more and more congenial - doing missionary work as long as you can. For, after all every one who believes in Christ Jesus and tries to follow Him is necessarily doing work of a missionary. Glory be to God. I started to write you before but something so often thwarts me and then its neglected. I talked with Joseph J. a few nights ago and he seemed well - tho somewhat lonely. No doubt you know what that means down there in the great South West. As the inclosed leaflet certificate will indicate, I am enrolling you for God's holy guidance. If it be God's holy will that you sell the Farm we hope that you succeed - as you did a few years back in selling that old house of your Parents. If not; well donot be over anxious about it; but hope that God have other designs. In the mean time offer up to God your exile etc, in union with that of our dear Lord from Heaven - also that of our Bl'd Mother Mary after the Ascension of Christ and of the Holy Family in Egypt. At all events, we do well to hearken to our dear Lord: "Sufficient for the day is the evil there of." . Pr. Solanus, O. F.I. Cap. P.S. Tell Joseph J. Many thanks for the elastic bandages received To-day. - in case I neglect it. Fr. S.

God bless you Joseph J. - you and yours. Again many thanks for your kind favor of 4th - duly noted - as well as for the elastic bandages - was inclined to write electric and then came back the picture of the remarkably practical blanket of a couple years back you sent us. Thank God, while last year I did use it a short time, this year I never thought of such a thing. - not too bad a siga? Well .... best wishes and God's blessing to yourself and to all, especially our promising Texascan - Exile. Naturally if time and duty permitted I would not mind such an exile myself for a year or so. ... Please don't forget us in your prayers to the Holy Ghost these days. That old essay problem still floats in my memory surface. . ... Now, I almost forgot: Some one from Knipe's Rest enrolled the family - parents and family of Rev Thomas J. lckugo - St. Francis de Paula Church, 7820 Dobson Ave. Chicago - and they did not know his parents names. I would appreciate it if you could let me know at your convenience the name of his Father. God bless you Joseph J. and Keep you. Fr. Solanus, O.F.L.Cap.

for God's holy guidance in his many problem - together with his associates God bless you Joseph J. - you and yours - Now and in Eternity! After all, if the saints have found +++++ and sorrows to bring them closer to Jesus - and they must be so short - why fear to embrace them ! ? !

God bless you Joseph and Winifred O'Donnell - you and yours. Many thanks for your prompt action in "preventing" further solicitude about your so-highly-commended cold remedy, "Brom-Quinin: I hardly took time to read directions - so, as early as possible for good results. Thanks be to God I feel that He must have some way prompted your charilable move I hope we all have the requisite good days befor the week is over; - you with out temperature and Fr. Sol. without his nose running away, etc. I looks better here already Deo gratias. - Time for matins and lauds.

God bless our Friends the Doyls - trying their hand at ... I almost said - being "Fronteer-cowboys". Would likd to be with you. Well I was just talking with our Friends Joe and Win. who thank God, seem to be brightening up consiterably. I made a proposition to them that seemed to appeal as quite favorable. We must get our Bl. Mother Mary and St. Joseph positively in- terested -- in a way we must try and shift the responsitility for real success more to their loving sholders. etc. But about this, more another time. . . I understand your weather down there is not too balmy. Glory be to God, however, sure its the loving Who is sending it. It must be for the best. Congratulations to Peter at least, that he don't have to plow throuth ten to twenty-foot snow-drifts as he probably had to do 25 years ago, and as I did more or less sixty years back, 1888-9, in trolly service at the head of the Lakes. How merci- ful the good God has been to us -- always fitting "the back to the burden, if not vice versa, as often seems the case.

God bless you Peter Doyle you and yours these days - tragic indeed but by the mercy of God, hopeful and beautiful. Yesterday, the Ilativity of our blessed Mother Mary and tomorrow the exaltation of the Holy Cross; both so full of promise and consolation. I was talking with Joe. this Morning and he told me you were not very well and that you are inclined to worry, etc. Ofcourse that is a wealmess of which very few of Adam's children are entirely free. Indeed it is something we all have to be on our guard against as a most insidious enemy to our peace of soul. Afterall, if we look back as many decads as possible and recollect, we will be easily convinced that our biggest worries have always been about womething that never happened; eg, twenty years ago on your way to "Good Saint Ann in Qubeck". .... O! Instead of worrying about anything - past or threatening to come - les us foster confidence in God by thanking Him ahead of time. No creatur, when there is question of generosity, can ever get within a weakest shadow of anythin like even dreaming to beat the Lord in generosity or anything else. But God loves to load confidently loving souls with supernatural, divine generosity. .. As for what they call an anatomical operation after death; it seems to me, such a thing should be the very last thing in the world to worry about. On the contrary, while in the vast majority of such cases there is very little operating done, the idea is possibly to help some similar case or cases still suffering or to suffer in future. For my part I shall consider it as doing an actof charity after my death if they can use my old bones for fertilizing. .... As for worrying because about past stupidities and sins: It just seems to me that we ought to be so occupied in gratefully thanks God for having rescued us from Hell and from the jaws of our unruly passions that we should find no time to worry about anything - save possibly, that about making so little progress toward progress in the way of perfection, etc. ....

If there is a blessing of any kind to come from atheism - in itself the Climax of insanity - it will be this Unity among those professing to believe in God. After all, if Religion can be defined as: "The science of relationship between God and the rational creature, and dependence of the latter on his Creator - and his neighbor - then religion must be one, and whatever is contrary to that unity is opposed to that peace between men themselves and God their Creator that ought to permiate human society - the peace of which the Good God Himself, through the Apostle assures us "surpasseth all understanding" - the peace that the Divine Ruler of the universe will no doubt establish between men and nations even at the cost of hells on earth before that peace be perfected.

God bless you and yours. I hope you are well. I hope you are at least resigned to the cross or crosses that the Dear Lord entrusts to your weakness, your poverty . In regard to those thoughtless associates who refer to the "age of miracles" as past; I would say simply that to doubt the truth of miracles in any age of history of seriously to question their existence, would be nothing less than just to fall in line with the ideals of the unbelieving world - deaf, dumb and spiritually blind, - whose WANT of principle is atheism the climax of insanity and whose prince and inspiration is Lucifer himself the king of all (dam) fools. I have two holy Masses this morning ~ 9 and 12 - and therefore, I can not think of going into details as I would like to do; but just to encourage you to persevere is patience and resignation to God's holy will, I Gu going to give you a few lines from a letter received last March, which I happened to pick up and reread just before opening yours of the-day-before yesterday. It comes from a nurse-friend in the State Hospital, Cleveland, Ohio. Here follows some of the letter: " .... You will remember last August when I was in Detroit how very hectic things were at the hospital. I tried to remem- ber everything religious and beautiful I was ever taught: I tried to think how the Saints prayed for crosses and sufferings; and decided (rightly), it was myself that needed adjusting. "So I started praying to St. Joseph, saying 7 Paters, 7 Aves and 7 Glories in honor of the seven great Sorrows and Joys which he had experienced on earth. I offered this for the grace to bear the little crosses and in- justices that were heaped upon me - at least seemingly so to me. Having started the novena things seemed to get worse but I kept on praying. I was afraid in fact to stop my prayers. "One day when things were at their worst and I could not feel I were receiving any additional necessary grace to manage under such conditions, the afternoon newspaper announced that a new Superintendent was appointed to the Hospital, 'a very fair and peaceful man .. 1 "He is indeed a peaceful man and very fair. Peace seemed to settle all over the place almost immediately upon his arrival. I had almost given up hope of any thing like that, and was just begging for grace to bear patiently with the many annoyances, etc. when on Thursday morning March 19th he came to our office and told us it was his birthday I fairly yelled with glee : "March 19th! What a wonderful birthday" The other girls asked me afterwards, "What in the world is there about March 19th?" ... never remembering that it is always the Feast of St. Joseph "Dont you think that was a generous answer from dear St. Joseph? And so attentive and personal. It just looked as if He had been figuring during the whole novena how to spring his delicate little surprise on me and this way increase my faith and confidence. 11 Now Miss Whelan; God bless you and all your troubles as well as all your friends and all your joys and hopes .... After all the soul of hap- piness here in this old world consists in the hopes we foster. Little children are happy in the vivid hopes that animate them. Ours should be the hopes of the Saints - springing from the infalible promises of Heaven and imbued with the appreciation of the contrast between the eternal and temporal etc. Now I'll say, "God bless you again and good- bye till another time.

God bless you and yours. I hope the outlook for you son is brightening since you wrote me last week. At all events, I hope we can help him. In fact, I think I ought to say, "Thanks be to God, I am confident that we can help him." This especially, if you and Mrs. Bracken and your friends who are interested, will do your part- each in his way. First, I want to tell you that I had an experience of skin-trouble similar to that of which you write your son is hav- ing and can sympathize with him even according to the little stanza: "The mourners tear hath furrowed kindly faces, And left the light of love abiding there, Sweet sympathy and tender deeds are traces Of pain and sorrow soothed in silent prayer." You tell me that Mrs. Bracken is not Catholic. I hope she as well as yourself - both of you - are earnest about saving your own souls. However, I am convinced more and more every day that such afflictions - in fact, that the trials and crosses of life in general - are sent us or at least permitted, primarily to wake us up and make us do better; in other words, "to switch us into line" in right thinking, and bring to our minds something of the short- ness of things earthly - joys and pleasures as well as sorrows and disappointments, etc., and thus incline us to appreciate Eternity and the Eternal. Hence the old saying: "Whom the Lord loveth, He chastiseth." Now, what can we each of us do to help to induce the Good God to lift this cross from the boy? If you send me his name, I shall inscribe him in our missionary work whereby he will have the benefits of prayers and holy Masses continually and, in a way may become - in- directly a foreigh missionary. The inclosed booklet will give you necessary details. Then you can go more frequently to Holy Communion if possible and have the others of the family do the same. This is one thing that I have been advising Catholics to do for years and I assure you, in many cases, with quite astonishing results. Of course, Mrs. Bracken cannot join in this for the present at least. Let her do something in her own honest way; whatever she may deem most pleasing to the dear Lord - only that she be earnest about it and as confident as possible. The following might be a practical example with just a few de- tails. It happened a few years ago when on a certain morning there was quite a crown waiting here in the Monastery office, and old-look- ing couple slowly rose from their seats and approaching the desk, asked in German, if they could speak to me personally. As we started into another room, I smelled a cancer, though I was not certain what it was till the old lady told me that her husband had cancer and could not work any more. She was the spokesman, and made no secret of it what- ever. After a little I asked if they went to the holy Scraments reg- ularly. "My husband is not a Catholic," she answered. "Then, Mr. N.," I said, "You do something in your own honest way to please the God God." "What could I do to please Him? I was raised a Lutheran but for twenty years I have practiced no religion." "It's a poor way to be, man;" I answered, "and especially if you take it as I define Religion. THE SCIENCE OF OUR RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR - I might say - OF OUR DEPENDENCE ON GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR. To practice no religion is making a secondary matter of the primary purpose of our creation as rational beings, viz., TO KNOW GOD; that we may love Him and serve Him and be happy with Him. Now I'll tell you what you can do to please God. Just start and be earnest about saving your soul." "After all" I added, if you are a Lutheran, you believe in Jesus Christ. I believe in Him as a Catholic; so we are both Christians, and one way or other we must be brothers. This last especially seemed to please him and he answered, dec- idedly brightening up; "Yes, yes, that is right." I would have taken the man to be eighty; whereas he was only forty -nine. But from the constant pain and stench of his malady he could neither eat nor sleep and it seemed to me he was wishing that he were ~m already in the grave. Honestly, he did not look as though he would live another week and I feared he might go off in despair. To inspire him with as much hope as I could I proposed to him about as follows: ". Now, Mr. N. . . . I am going to tell you something else that you can do to please God. I am inscriping your name now in our mis- sionary work, the Seraphic Mass Association, for prayers and holy Masses always being offered for the members. You, on your part could promise the Good God in your own honest way, that if it helps, you will be earnest in finding out for yourself the difference, rather the relationship - between your denomination and the "Mother Church", which latter is, of course, none other than the Catholic." Without the least hesitation he answered at once; "Ich tu es." (I'll do it.") Then, seeing his readiness and his growing interest, I added: "And, I can assure you beforehand that inasmuch as you are earnest and hon- est in this matter - and prayerful at the same time -- in just so much will it become as clear to you as twice two are four, that you have your Christianity not directly from Jesus. Indirectly, yes; but directly and historically you have it (inasmuch as it is Christ- ianity) as said before, from the "Mother Church" - call yourself what you may. Like a drowning man who grasped my hand when only a youth, so now this poor patient seemed to hang on every word of hope. "Hist- orisch" he repeated, "Historically? That is true! I'll do it." Next morning, about two hours earlier than the day before, he walked in seemingly quite a different person. There was color in his face and a smile on his countenance. He was twenty years younger looking as he walked over to the desk without stop or hesitation to greet me; "Guter Morgan" - (Good Morning.) "I came to see if I could start taking instructions today. That he was feeling better was manifest. No one could doubt that who had seen him the day before . . . . . I gave him over for instructions to Father Charles, a born Bavarian, who could naturally speak better German than one like myself and had more time at his disposal than I could possible give him. Eight weeks later, Sunday morning, I gave him his First Holy Communion myself, quite unexpect- edly, and a week from the next day just as I had finished telling two ladies about him - one of them a Baptist with a cancerous breast - he, like rushed in thru the door, beaming all over to announce; " I just dropped in to tell you I am going back to work next Wednesday." The above is a single case from many similar - I think I'd be safe to say one out of thousands. I very seldom go into such details and while I've tried to encourage quite a few cancer patients by tell- ing them about this one, I have never written about it before. I hope it may not be a bore to anyone. On the contrary; may it be an inspir- ation and an example for many, not only for cases of eczema and cancer, but for whatever trouble may be met with. Our sad weakness today is our lack of faith and consequently, want of confidence in God. In case you be in Detroit, or if, without too much inconvenience, the boy might be able to call down at the Monastery, I would be pleased to meet you. Hoping that by this time he is feeling improved and again wishing you and yours God's New Year's Blessing, I beg to remain,

God bless you and yours. May He guide you for the best in all your ways! Many thanks for your kind favor of October 12th with charitable request. Having read your really pathetic letter, I started at once to write you a reassurence of my heart-felt sym- pathy and of my prayers for yourself and your three little half- orphants; and now it seems like months instead of weeks that I've been trying to get something back to you worth while; -- sympathy first of course and condolance. At the same time, however, and the more I think it over, I would be wanting in appreciation of the confidence you manifest in writing me such a letter if, even while condoling with you, I failed, to at least intimate a gentle congratulation. This of course, not on the death of such an ideal wife and mother as was your Kathleen but on your fortune - perhaps whollyunmerrited on your part - of having for years had such a model of Christian per- fection to live with and to drinkin for so long the spiritual in- fluences necessarily radiating from the outstanding virtues manifest in the very-day life of any such a Christian. No wonder that you now lament feeling "bankrupt without her". Your bereavement; yes; inasmuch as viewed through the melan- choly lenses of worldly wisdom, so sadly inclined to exclude faith in God and consequently confidence in a favorable hereafter, would be an irreparable loss and misfortune. But O! what a contrast in the light of Christian faith that illuminates the soul of the really practical believer !. "How vain!" exclaims that faith and that phil- osophy; "How trivial and vain in themselves are the joys and the sorrows alike of this 'momentary existence', that worldlings wor- ship as life!" Truly, We hardly need go further than your own letter and your own recent experience to coroberate with the above; in other words to be convinced that though in themselves are vain, still be- cause of our weaknesses they are unecessary or helpful-these joys and sorrows - the one to buoy us up from becoming depressed, the other to chck us in our inordinate esteem of self and of wordly advantages. Is this not exactly the conclusion to which you come in your letter exclaims that faith and that Christian philosophy; "How vain and how trivial /in psis "How vain!" are the joys alike and the sorrows of this really 'momentary existence' that worldlings are so inclined to worship as LIFE !! Vain they are indeed Vain indeed in themselves, when we think of eternity, must seem anything that passes away; and only inasmuch as they buoy us up from depression or check us in our inordinate esteem of self and the world can they be considered really important. In this sense and considering our condition as pilgrims to ETERNITY THEY would seem to be a sort of salvation not only important but posi- tively necessary. We hardly need go further than your own letter and recent experience, to coroborate this philosophy.". . . Her death/has brot out to me the utter emptiness of life except for something too fine to express in words. "Our food, our clothing, our home, our material things mean so little in the final analisis. "I am praying for more of the faith that she had; more of that which, I cannot define, other than a suprime confidence in God and a firm belief in a hereafter. "She had so much of it. "I have so little. "Sometimes I think, that first the death of little John and now her death are but signs, or a writing on the wall, a sort of warning to me. . . . "Now I want to rise up above material things, to get a better picture of life, a truer sense of values."
