God bless you and yours. Many thanks for the air mail yesterday. Glad to hear things are improving with your dear Dad. Thanks be to God for everything. I am sending you the mourning card for Wm. Murphy and the certifi- cates-blanks-for the two others. Not certain of their names I just made a special enrollment ($1.00 or more) for each of two according to your intention. You can fill out the blanks, etc. Dear Muriel: .... You tell me you see others so happy .... O! yes we see such people. Thank God they exist, though many of those who seem happy-who try to appear so-hardly know just what happiness is. Many do not realiz or stop to use their faculty of reasoning that the very soul of happiness for mortals-those who are to die some day-is hope. Children are happy as a rule because in the mind of any normal child "Some day I'll be grown up." Herein we must imitate the child- there is always bright star of hope: "I'll be a woman." "I'll be a man." ren. But instead of their ideals to be mature-a man or woman-we ought to think over to goal ahead, our eternal destiny-for all Eternity- to be proficient in what in this world we can only taste, so to say Know- ledge of God. Knowledge of anyone who is good means love for same in- as much as we be normal. Knowledge of God, therefore !!!! The aim, the purpose of the rational creature's existence. P.S. -- Simply to be grateful to God for what has done for us, what is doing and promises to do. . What Hope. ..!

I hope you are well -- you and all your dear ones. Many thanks for your recent favors. I hope that someday you'll just wake up and start to live for God one day at a time, forgeting the fickleness of creatures -- especially if they figure on getting "a nest in this world where they can find true happiness." The only tree in which to find place to build such a nest, is the Church that pro- vides the material to build in untold graces from God -- all sizes -- with crosses for cement. Without such cement no one on earth can get very far with anything like getting a little taste of Heaven in this world. So let us not take it over serious when trials and disapoint- ments-from whatever source-catch us sleeping. In other words it never pays to become discouraged-at the faults of others or at our own. The sooner we come to realize our own stupidity and unworthyness of the blessings surrounding our whole life and in which we are immurged -- the air we breathe, the light of the heavens we enjoy by night and by day and all movies of visible creation. (All in the natural) To say nothing of the unseen, the supernatural !-- the sooner we'll find peace. P.S .-- God bless you again M.K. Hope things are still bright -- and brigh- tening. God bless you and yours. Many thanks for favor just noted. Thank the Dear Lord that there is at least "A rift in the clouds" now and then. After all that is what "life" on earth is like-ups and downs, rain and sunshine . . .. "Great Life if one don't weaken" Hence: "Poor wanderers of a stormy day: from wave to wave we re driven. Moore. And fancy's flash and reason's ray serve but to light the troubled way. There's nothing calm but Heaven." Courage therefore, with the souls eye fixed-on the goal of Eternity, it behoves us to battle on.

God bless you Muriel Krausman and many thanks for favor of June 6th. I am glad you are feelin not too bad-like myself-battling along one day at a time .... Had a solemn high Mass today - 35th anniversary of my Brother Maurice Joachim's first Mass Celebration. That was in Superior, Wisconsin 1911. Thanks be to God. He is in St. Paul, Minn. now with our Rt. Rev. Br. Edw'd back from the Philippines. Latter was rescued last year, March 23rd. Will be going back before long. It would seem that the Japps had been figuering on a general massacre of the whole camp - that day - over two thousand, including two Bishops, 150 priests and 125 nuns. They ( the prisoners) had been saying the holy rosary and having Bene- diction every day and Pontifical Mass every Sunday that they might be res- cued without anything too drastic. Most of the prisoners were so starved that they could hardly walk. About 20 actually died of malnutrition - starved. . . .

Many thanks for your kind favor of the 5th. I hope you are feeling better by this time. It seems to me your apathy regarding glasses is uncalled for ..... As long as I can remember I was inclined to think that, in many cases, glasses quite improved the appearance of the wearer. I would not doubt this could easily apply to M.K. Thanks be to God I was surprized at looking at your letter today, I could read it nicely without glasses. I started to a Chiropractor in July - two treatments a week and I am feeling improved all round. My Dr. in Detroit who put me on my feet in one month - after trying M.Ds. for years - was Dr. R. N. Schon ( Chiropractor) of 10050 Connor Ave. - just across Gratiot from the Air Port. He positively helped quite a few patients I sent him - even when almost blind. If you go to him .... Best regards! .God bless you now and be grateful to God .... Don't worry . . ..

God bless you Miss Muriel Krausman. I hope you keep well. You've been on my mind for ten days, - wanting acknowledge your favor of Apr. 4th. Well you remember how it was with me when I was up there in January. It is not audiences with callers now but answering letters that is my problem. So please have charity to overlook tardiness, etc. I thank you just the same and pray for you even though I fail to write. Many thanks again.

Many thanks for your kind favor just read and noted. I tried to get you on the phone last Monday and then with so many calling and so much hustling, etc, I failed to get you afterwards. I certainly would like also to have spoken to your dear Father. Of course, I sympathise with you all in your problems, especially that of being without a roof over your heads. But why make so much of that after all? How many millions have in addition to that lamentation . hardly a bite of food to put in their mouth? Why not make a virtue of a necessity or emergency by offering it all to the Heavenly Father in union with the situation in which Jesus found Himself when not in com- plaint or lamentation He whispered to the youth who proposed to be His disciple: 11. .The Son of Man hath not where to lay his Head." But alas! Humanity's outstanding weakness seems to be a thoughtless want of appreciation for the uncountable blessings by which Almighty God is always surrounding it; and no doubt the Krausmans as well as the Kennedys and the KCs are no exception in part of that old humanity. But how incalculably fortunate we are after all that the merciful God has patience with us and notwithstanding such failings has patience with us and still manifests His solicitude for our welfare in such a next-to infinite number of ways? Let us, therefore, shake off the spirit of complaint and lamentation over triffling difficulties that, even though unpleasant for nature and for the thoughtless, who make little of an eternal happiness awaiting those who persevere in, at least resignation to poverty and, which dif- ficulties can so easily be turned to such vast advantage.

I hope you keep well. Many thanks for kind remembrance for Oct. 25th. Thanks be to God for the quite excellent He gives me at 77. Naturally of course my steps are slowing down as to quite to be expected. Next week (10th) my Rev. Brother M. J. Ex- to celebrate his 80th birth-day. Please pray that we be guided so as to please God to the end. Edify - at least in our last days ...

Many thanks for your prayer and for your kind favor just noted. Thank God, while i have been "half down" for several weeks, still its nothing possitively serious. Of course we are hoping it will clear up so that I be able to do a little more toward so much waiting to be done. Thank the Lord too: I am glad things seems brightening up for you and yours. It always comes right if only we have a little trustful confidence in the good God and our Blessed Mother Mary Immaculate.

Evidently M. does not love God as is the first duty of every one of us - to try to love Him .... What's to be done? We'll simply have to have patience, humble ourselves and wait .... Praying in meantime that the Good God increase our faith and confidence in Him till we can appreciate creatures as of secondary importance. Then possibly it will come natural for us to act naturally and tell what's honestly in our minds and hearts.

This time I just thought "I'll write at once." Yes, thank God, my health has adjusted itself again so that hardly feel any effects of my dose of ptomane of two months ago .... Best regards to your Father, to Jack, and all our friends, and keep pleading for God's holy guidance.

Many thanks for your kind favor of the 5th, just noted. I noted the enrollments as requested - also the special holy Mass in honor of the Holy Ghost for your guidance and that of your friends. .Why should we worry? Why not rather ponder on the wonderful and innumerable manifestations whereby God in wis- dom and power and mercy has brought us into existence and thus far preserved us - notwithstanding our waywardness, our stupidity and our sinfulness. Is not His solicitude for our happiness - even temporal as well as eternal more manifest at every turn than that of all most loving parents and other friends? O if we would but keep in mind at all times the sweet words of our dear Lord - at once a philophic admonition and a paternally loving invitation - "Seek ye, therefore, first the Kingdom of God .... " Patience therefore, "God condescends to use our powers, if we don't spoil His plans by ours."

God bless you Miss M. Krausman; you and yours. I am inclined to congratulate you on what seems to be an opportunity of advance- ment. At all events, the old saying: "A change of work is as good as a rest," I hope will apply here in your case. It seems to me that you ought easily be able to convince your present Foreman of the propriety of your accepting the offer of advancement. At the same time show your gratitude his favorable attitude toward your- self as an amployee, i.e., in case you do succeed in the desired promotion. Thanks be to God too for the improved outlook for your dear Father, especially in regard to your Uncle coming back to the source of spiritual strength, our Holy Mother the Church. Deo Gr. I'm sure you will not take it amiss that I so often fail to answer your favors. If I had to answer them all - all my letters I'd be liable to at least lose my ballance.

I just finished reading your welcome letter and thought I'd answer it at once before overlooking. I was in St. Joseph Hospi- tal, Ft. Wayne for two weeks but that was in June and I am back to St. Felix and feeling fine. Deo Gratias. One trouble or weakness that we all have to guard against is worry . Instead of this weakness we do well to foster confidence in God. This we can do by not only patience, but by thanking God ahead of time for whatever He see best for us ... . We'll pray for your intentions too.

Many thanks for your kind favor of yesterday - Glad things are coming on favorably. Hope the your tiny niece shakes off that whooping, etc. Keep well yourself but shake off some of that anxiety about your and others' health. Thank God I am feeling fine again. Hope you can shortly say the same. Before laying your letter aside and then forgetting I tho't I'd just drop you a card - then spoild it. -

Many thanks for your kind favor just Rec'd, noted. I am sending you the Cert. for Helen Mayland. I think she needs it especially from your letter. In the mean time and till I get up a little better with my correspondence, best regards and God holy blessing to all the others - your dear Father especially. I do hope with you, that with the warmer Spring his health and spirits bloom up again and that things in general pick up in his favor. I almost forgot to congratulate you on your February suc- cess, etc. Deo gratias. Please pardon haste and brevity. Hope for improvement in future.

Many thanks for your kind remembrances and prayers. Thanks be to God, though I've had several colds etc. these past months. My health has been good. Today however a real "cold" seems trying to get hold on me .... Deo Gr. Of course I was - am - pleased to know of your dear Father's success in selling that property, so long on the market, etc. We pray his health - as well as M's improve speedily. Whatever comes, however, let us try at least to be re- signed . As to my reception of your letters, please do not worry. For several years I have not been able to even read the majority of my letters to say nothing of answering them. I hardly know what I would have to do if I had no Fr. Jerome or some one to substitute him. In fact I have been thinking for some time of leaving the answering of all letters to some one else - provided by the Rev. Fr. Guardian. Please say a prayer for my guidance in this regard too. I surely do sympathize with so many poor people in the world, - struggle, struggle, Str. Well, that too can be offered up as a sort of martyrdom. So let us keep courage .... Keep faith with God at all events and save our souls. . . .

Take courage! Trust in God! His providence govems all things sweetly, even tho we cannot see it immediately. That is where we must have faith and confidence! Muriel has been enrolled once again and also the Poor Souls. God love you! We will pray for the best. Have confidence! Thank God ahead of time whatever He sends. P.S. Please Miss Muriel: God bless you and yours. You have never called up. (?) I only this P.M. got to read your letter of last Friday. And surely there was urgency enough about your sister and little niece to call Hunt- ington 210. I would have called you but I had no permis'n F.S. We'll pray for them of course; but in such urgent cases we find it practical even by telephone to enroll - hoping of course that the good God show His Mercy and give sanction to our presuming. God bless you now and keep courage.

God bless you Miss Muriel Krausman. Thanks be to God things have brightened in a number of ways, especially in relation with poor little Mary Jane. Indeed, thanks be to God. However, I rather - I do not like that idea of a second O. I know of more than one such "Miracles" where the doctor's efforts at improve- ment has turned fatal. About 20 yrs. back a certain Thomas Ryan of Pittsburgh, Penn. was passed all hope of operation. His in-laws phoned from St. Rose Parish Detroit and we enrolled him ... To their astonishment he went back to work without any operation. After two weeks work, the doctors induced him to go finish up on the X.R. Same T.R .-- Same T. Ryan got a relapse and died. I have known of several such cases. Be grateful to God, therefore, and attribute miracles to whom they due. I hope Drs. find further surgery uncalled for. There is a similar case related in the "life" of our stigmatic - P. Pio. A certain poor, good woman was quite hopeless with can- cer. She and her Husband went to Padre Pio and she was cured. Afterwards (I presume) without consulting Padre Pio and she got sick again and P. Pio said he could, he could do nothing.

God bless you Miss Krausman. Many thanks for your favor of some weeks past - I wanted to write you for Christmas but that be- came just impossible. I am glad to learn that notwithstanding the many difficulties your dear ones meet with, still in general things seem to improve anyhow.
- for speedy recovery, God willing. God bless you Phillip and Aunt Get well amd keep up. Beatrice too.

And many thanks for favor of Nov. 24th Please God - . Philip's arm will be all okay. I am so pleased that you find things so favorable over there. Thank God. Hope it con- tinues so God's blessing for the holy season so near. I am mailing picture as requested. God bless you all.
Hope your arm will come out a hundred % Okay. Keep courage. Go to Communion .. Be a real "little-boy-friend of Jesus and Mary. And don't forget to remember poor me to them. :

God bless you His lamb with Philip and all the rest. I am glad you are well. You always seem well out there. I have been here since last April. Thanks be to God it is quite an ideal place - 18 novices. The youngest about 17 ... to 23. Hope philip keeps well. Our Fr. Julius is down there some where in Tucson. He expects to go in Jan- uary to the Guam Missions. There has been some talk of our getting a place in Tucson.

God bless you Miss Lamb - you and yours. Glad to hear from you - and about Philip. I hope that operation - and preparation therefor, may be not too serious. At all events try and avoid anxiety - and trust in our Dear Lord for Every thing.

I just came across your favor of Aug. 29th on the con- viction that: "Whom the Lord loveth He Chastened", and even while I surely sympathize with you, in your so many difficulties, I do, nevertheless congratulate you on all these experiences that the crazy world considers such mis- forrtunes. If we only try to show the dear Lord a good will and ask Him for grateful resignation to the crosses He sends or permits to come our way, we may be sure that sooner or later they will turn out to have been just so many bless- ings,in disguise. I hoped for quite a time that my "little boy-friend Philip" might have a vocation to some thing special. That, however is a personal problem and in many cases seems to be a very delicate question. I hope of course, that he be earnestly appreciative of the holy Faith - theoretically first of the outstanding "Trace of the Trinity in our souls. The other two, hope and being essentially one with it - hope the soul of happiness in this world, charity, the life and crown of everlasting glory. . . . . I must close now - almost 10 p.m. So God bless you and all our dear ones and have mercy on all.

God bless you Miss Beatrice Lamb. Glad to hear from you. I hope you keep well. Please say a prayer that poor Fr. Sol. catch up with out cor- respondence. - With you and yours Hope our one-time little boy-friend Philip is keeping well .... .. .... God to remember that on this star (earth) that we are living on, there is no real Heaven - and that : "Whom the Lord loveth, He Chasteneth" . . ·

God bless you and yours. While I feel it really a privilege to help one another and to save our neighbor a step whoever he be, I want to thank you for your practical assistance to this - I was going to say - poor old sinner. -- rapidly getting old at least. After all, since we have nothing of our own, what we do, in the order especially, we do for the community and in a way it is sure to come back so us again - in many cases it comes back in many ways. As V. Br. Rufin exclaimed when he was treating my other foot a few years ago, and I remarked: "Every time you save your neighbor a step you gain one for yourself" - "You gain at least two steps for yourself .. " So I hope you gain many favors for what you do for Br. Francis and myself and the whole community. Many thanks too for the medicine forwarded and the per- sonal letters, etc. In case any of my friends ask - just cell them I am improving and thankful for such a restful contrast after nearly forty years - over 18 years in Detroit. God willing, I hope to be well be- fore long and possibly back "at the old stand. " .... God bless you again and Br. Francis too and all the brothers and novices and. .. community ... Praised se Jesus!

God bless you and yours, - including that poor sinner Solanus, who more than anyone else gave me trouble as long as I was in St. Bonaventure's - Isent it a mercy that we really need examine only one "pair of conscience"! Well I received your card a few days ago and thank you for the same as well as for the personal letters therewith. Intimation of further appreciation below, if I can find it for you. We had quite a celebration yesterday of Br. Gabriel's nameday. Father Provincial gave him a nice little "sendoff", praising his work as, "becoming quite proficient as a linotypest" and thanking him for his work in the name of the entire Province, etc. I thought of you rightaway and of your message to him, which he seemed to quite appreciate. At the same time something came to my mind of our ineffable privilege in doing the little things we are able to do for the general welfare - most especially in a religious com- munity - each one in his place without thought or distinction as to what the work may be. To whatever office or service one may turn to it is not easy to say just which is the more privileged - possibly ex- cepting that of sacristan. At all events that of por- ter, even though fraught with dangers, has many ad- vantages, if only we be of good will and cooperate with the graces never failing on God's part and our B1. Mother. Sometimes of course it becomes monotonous and extremely boring, till one is neary colapsing; but in such cases it helps to remember that even when Jesus was about to fall the third time He patiently con- soled the women-folks and children of His persecutors, making no exceptions. How can we ever be grateful as we ought to be for such a vocation - to such privileg- ed positions - even in the Seraphic Order of the Poverello of Asissi? ... Thanks be to God that He .. One of the has such divine patience with us. secrets no doubt, as you surely have seen from "The Mystical City of God," is the fact that our Blessed Mother Mary is always coaching poor sinners on the one hand to confidence and penance, and on the other Jesus our Lord to have mercy and spare. P.S. Talking with Father Provincial last Wednesday he said we'd go back to Detroit together. He has been working on the Messenger and I think very probably we will be leaving here shortly - possibly Tuesday or Wednesday. I cannot say just when. God bless you again. Very best regards to V. Bro. Francis and to all our Dear ones.

God bless you and yours. I hope you keep well. Thanks be to God, I am here in this new assignment of privileged duty just a week. Tomorrow will be the forty-first anniversary of my first Holy Mass, Deo Gratias -and the next day the 21st of my ar- rival from Harlem, Our Lady of Angels, back to St. Bonaventures - 1924. How grateful we ought to be for so many graces and privileges. Praised be God in all His works and ways! Now I hope you have not found that middle cell that succored me so long in too hopeless disorder. I rather fear having left you a difficult job when I asked you to pack up and forward things hither, that would be of no use to any one else and might be of quite a little convenience to me. I am not certain if I brought a trunk with me from Harlem twenty years ago. If I did, it must have been worth next to nothing, so any old box you might find would do, perhaps better than a trunk. The "Letters" box on top of the "wardrobe" containing Fr. Edward's letters are good. The others are not important. Those few unfinished pieces in the cliper on the side next to the desk, I would like to have - if you've not thrown them away. Also that little prayer on modesty that we were figering on having in the office. I started over to bring it for Fr. Provincial's approval but he was not in and then it was neglected and I went off West. I hope to get a little more time for such things here at St. Michael's, although so far - getting aquainted, etc. - I've not had much surplus time. One thing, however, I've taken a little more sleep under the great archangel's wings this past week then perhaps in three weeks before my arrival. Any photos or pictures of Fr. Solanus or the others I hardly know what I should do with them: so you may burn them if you wish. However I , would like to have the one of our golden jubilee that is framed viz. the one with all the little grandchildren. Some of them are grandparents now themselves. Well I guess I'd better come to a conclusion. Otherwise -- ?? Best regards to Br. Rufin and to all. Hope Br. Gerard is improving and that he'll get out of any further operation. P.S. The overcoat and habit arrived okay. Many thanks.

The "bottle in the corner" you asked about is water from Lourdes. Use it in case of sickness, etc. It was sent me from the Shrine directly. . Do not worry about missing this or what piece of junk in Cell #5. I've often figured on how to rid myself of the whole collection.

Many, many thanks for your helping in the good work in office these last few years, and again for your sending me those things - package after package - since I came East. We had our Retreat this year -- last two weeks -- in the Immaculate Conception Monastery. Thanks be to God it was ideal weather and the location could hardly be surpased. Bonaventure and all send best wishes. Brother . . my shins etc. are really doing fine; Tell Br. Rufin bother me very little. Thank God . . . Am trying to keep my conscience at least as good as the same old shins .

God bless you again. I wanted to send you the inclosed card last Sunday before going to Yonkers for the High Mass next day -- and Labor-day Parish reunion. Time was urgent, however, and so without getting it off I made hast(e) to catch a train, etc. Thank God; we had quite an ideal day and celebration. I made a little visit before going down to the Hall, as I was leaving Monday night and offered a few prayers -- pater and Aves -- in honor of our holy Guardians and especially of St. Raphael --- A young Jack Kelly ( ... now past middle age) took me clear to Brooklyn Bridge and into the subway ... Thanks to God -- and His blessed messengers the angels. Time refuses me to give more details. Since starting this letter-card -- your letter and package came in. Many thanks again. Now one or two things I've not as yet found, that would be of quite an advantage here -- one or two of those Fr. Solanus stamps and a dater of some kind. The former especially would help considerably. Many thanks again and God's blessing and best wishes to all.

Many thanks for favors last week. . Am sending you a few of the badges asked for. We've not been receiving any of late. The sister in Cleve- land so active in that line for some years wrote in October that she ... could not continue. Miss Modock also hopes to go to the convent ... can probably not continue. O well as long as we have them we can share. After all it was the dear Lord sent them so far and if it please Him we hope the beautiful sup- ply may continue. Dear Brother Leo, our equipment here for Ser Mass Association is rather behind time. Will you see if Fr. Lambert could muster an extra loose- leaf outfit - as you and Bro. Rufin or someone else introduced a year or so ago. We would ap- preciate it for the new year. In the meantime we'll drill along and do what we can under handi- cap of old "machinery" etc. - always ocourse praying for one anothers final conversion. Praised be Jesus Christ. Best wishes and happy Feast of the Immaculate Conception.

I am sending the original of this carbon to Miss Lyke. I hope it may smoothe the thing off in a manner; though I am not just clear as to what she really com- plains about. Perhaps she expected a personal acknow- ledgement of somekind more than just a rubber-stamp. I've been getting so many cheques - bothe here at St. Felix and at St. Michael's that I would have to posess an extraordinary memory to recollect particulars like this little mixup might require. One thing I do remem- ber, that during the nine or ten months I was at St. Michael's it was very seldom, if ever, that I was with- out letters to acknowledge, even though I sometimes worked on them till after min-night. God be praised, however, I did not mind it and my health kept fine. Seomtimes my two faithful ole sentinels would threaten to go on strike and to quiet them down I felt I'd have to give it up. Well she will possibly writ again. Afer all if she got her check back, she ought to know that things were oky .. ? We'll hope for the best anyhow and pray for the dear Lord's gentle guidence. Praying in the mean time for one anothers' conversion - till some day we can sin no more and the good angels will be able to bear us off to the eternity; forever - really and truly CONVERTED, WE'LL sing on withe angels awaiting that blessed day: 110 all ye works of the Lord bless the Lord, Praise and exalt Him above all forever."

I WISH TO THANK YOU SINCERELY FOR YOUR KIND AND GENEROUS ALMS TO THE CAPUCHIN FOREIGN MISSIONS. I AM SURE THAT THE PRAYERS OF THE MISSIONARIES WILL, ASCEND TO THE THRONE OF GOD FOR YOUR WELFARE. UNDER SEPARATE COVER I AM MAILING YOU THE CER- TIFICATES OF ENROLLMENT, WHICH I TRUST YOU WILL LIKE.
God bless you and all. Many thanks for the kind favor received in best of condition a few days ago. We got home that night just as they were starting supper. Deo Gr .!

I just received your charitable letter and will be pleased to juin with yourself and your friends across Meldrom in praying for poor dear little "Granma Kauffman. Sorry I did not know of her trouble before she went to the hospital . . . Diluted creolin, say 2 to 4 tablespoonfuls to a pint of water will give wonerful relief by simply sponging the parts effected once over, every two or three hours. or every 4 or 5 or more hours. Several years ago, before I got acquainte with mistress creoin, I applied the pure stuff to quite some patches of No. i's area and very shortly - for a couple of minutes - I began to rather fear I'd possible made a fearful mistake - It made thins so hot for me. It was a good lesson without the least injury. Few doctors seem to know about this remedy; so simple != Now; Dear Br. Leo: I've had a big problem on my mind for over a year. - have spoken about it to Fr. Provincial and to sev- eral religious friends, asking their prayers, etc. I started months ago to write F. Provincial particulars about and am still trying to get it off. Of course it is not easy to write important lines of any kind without study and practice, at least for me . To-day of sixteen letters received there were ten personals, which leaves me very little time, so that often it is not easy to what to do. On an average there about a dozen letter per day. In Father Blase's absence - otherwise too - Brother Raphael attends to many of the letters we get here concerning the Ser. Mass Assoc'n. So please pray . Best regard and God's blessing to all the Novices and Candidate & of course all in the Monastery and your dear Parents, etc. Just herein, viz, in praying for success of good works and undertakings the novices and candidates can fall in line as practical religions and Capuchins before-hand.

Just a line to thank you and your young associates -- novices and candidates -- for your charitable remen- brance for my privileged name-day. We hope and pray they all pray for vocations; to to multiply all over the world - in every order and every society and phase of Catholic action. Thus they will at once be doing real missionary work and insuring their own holy vocation - and perseverance therein. For no one who appreciates his vocation, as such a grace deserves, and is duly gratefull will fail to pray for a multiplication of further vocations. Thank God we have a very promising boquet of brother-candidates - including a very care-free, happy darky.

you and yours, especially our young brothers the Novices, with whom you are now seemingly in a sort of exile from your former nest in St. Bonaventure. And of course to Fr. Alouise, for the past years (3 or 4) my next neighbor at Saint Felix's. I can hardly help missing him more than I usually do in most cases because I knew him ... as a novice and now again after close to 25 years - possibly more. However, that is the way it goes in the Order as well as in secular life; though in the latter it is very much more disapoint- ing. Anyhow, best wishes to Fr. Aloisius and to all the novices and God's blessing to all in St. Francis, your new Novitiate. It is possible that before the summer is over I may have the privilege there for a day or so, God willing so, I'll be pleased. Till then In the mean time we'll do well to continue praying mutually for further conversion and - hearkening to our dear Lord's Own most earnest plea . "Pray we the Lord of the Harvest that He send laborers into His harvest". I shall remember you all in my High-Mass tomorrow. Please have them all as much as conveinent - have them all - supply my want of appreciation and gratitude to God for the uncountable mercies and graces we have received these 48 years - graces and mercies that have, not only surrounded us but in which, without our half realizing it, we are continually immersed in God' merciful graces / like the air that permiates us. Glory be to God! How little is it possible for poor mortals that we are, to appreciate as we ought, or to be properly grateful to God and our benefactors this side of Heaven! But after all that is what we became candidates for - candidates for the Kingdom of Heaven - when we were baptized; and every time we receive the Holy Sacraments of Mother Church we take another step forward, virtually pleading with our angels for another white bean at every step. How wonderful and how legion are our privileged opportunités ! Glory be to God a billion.

God bless you and yours. Inclosed herewith I am sending you the ticket of which I spoke to you yesterday when I asked for Judge Maher. In a way I was pleased rather that you answered. I've been imposing on the good nature of both Judge Monahan and Judge Murphy that they are liable to throw me out some of these days with my unfortunate friends .. Trusting that they still have a heart, I hope you'll be able to take care of us this time too. .... God bless the court and all concerned.

Since receiving your recent note favor- for which, MANY THANKS - and your practical request in regard to the benefits of the Sera- phic Mass Assotian, I am moved to earenst thought and action on a project that for many months has been floating in my mind. Thanks be to God for His patience with me in not lifting the thought away from me - the inspiration, perhaps I ought to say -- till your ap- preciated communication awakened me to decision. The benefits of this association, as seem to me, are so mani- fest in many cases and so mnifold that to enumerate them even briefly would require more than a short letter, time for writing which is about all I have at my disposal. I shall try, however, not to disapoint you entirely by giving you a short summary of such benefits or advantages. To start with our holy Mother the Church quite singles-out this association as outstanding in importance by granting to promoters of the work three hundred days indulgence for every enrollment - nay, for every effort made, even if it be but a few words in its favor, to further the interests of the Association. (See inclosed booklet, page 13). The diversity and in some cases the magnitude of The manifold reports of favors received here as through/Associa- tion ought to convince any thinker', of the wonderful benefits acruing to its members thru this providential organization. Let me give here a single example at least, of the notes made in this office of such fav- ors as I am sure would interest the members of your esteemed organiza- tion. I think it was in August that a certain Mrs. B., anxious about her son shortly to leave for over-seas enrolled him in the "Seraphic Mass". The note follow "October 5, 1945, Mrs. Fred Brewer ... reports having enrolled her son Fred and his comrade and ship-crew, etc. The ship crossed the Atlantic Okay; but two hours before scheduled landing she struck a mine and ship and cargo went down. However, of the 2500 men on board no one was lost. The Captain himself said that the escape was miraculous." Now a word about possibilities and obligations. Anyone may be enrolled: -- the sinner (atheist or believer) for conversion; the saint for further conversion and progress in sanctity - in RELIGION, THE SCIENCE OF OUR RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR. (and, if yiu will, of our dependenc: on Both) Obligations are practical. Active members, appreciating the opportunities offered by membership are urged to pray for the missions and the missionaries and for all members of the Associa- tion; and to offer Holy Communion when they can for these inten- tions. Those who can afford to do so, are asked to contribute to the material support - usually 50c annually or $5. as a perpetual member - more if they wish and $2. or more a deceased member - - perpetuall membership or participation. Direct and immediate bene- fits include five hundred and about twenty-five holy Masses every day or 188,500 holy Masses annyally, saying nothing of the indirect participation in all the good works of the whole Order otherwise in- cluding thousands of Holy Masses dai

May 11# You see I made very little progress two weeks ago on the card Br. Leo gave me and suggested I write you. However, while I would like to write you more of a real letter, which in fact I proposed to do, I have found it not easy to get any where. However, I am sending you herewith a letter written to a priest who at the time was in Yonkers N.Y. and quite inclined to worry about one thing or another; - nearly always about imaginary things, i.e. about something that turns out to have been more or less just a temptation. Of course we are all naturally inclined that Tay . From our dear Lord's "Sermon on the Mount.", you can see how the Apostles themselves were no ex- ceptions. Just reat the 5th 60 and 75 chapters of St. Matthew ari see how our dear Lord almost scolded them for their want of faith. No one blames you, selfunderstood for trying to be healthy. That's only a part of the first law of nature. Buit to be over anxious about it is not good; or to think that the good God should work a miracle for us. £ Because we ought to know that He is the only one can work a miracle. We can try of course, to induce Him e.s. through the intercession of the saints and our Bl. Mother Mary Queen of all. . .. When Fr. Exprovincial Theodosious was a cleric it was generally feared he'd never last to be or- dained. .. So keep up courage dear Fr. Sebastian .- just one day at a time and leave the morrow and yesterday to the good God. and pl pray for this poor sinner. .

God bless you and yours. Praised be His Holy Name in all His unsearch- able designs! I read your pathethic oetter this morning and again just now. Yours is certainly a peculiar case. .... But after all, whose case is not a peculiar one? As no two grains of sand can be found exactly alike on all the strands of the oceans and as "star differeth from star in glory", so the ups and downs of this"life". So too the rainbows, the sun bursts, gentle breezes and the real Hellstorms we are liable to meet before, by the grace of God, we shall be able to tumble into our graves with the confidence of tired Children into their places of peaceful slumbers. But dear Sister; we are never justified in being "bitter" toward anyone except ourselves. In very deed, if we were only one tenth as appreciative as we have every reason to be; our gratitude for what God has done for us - directly and through His creatures, most especially through our immediate superiors, - would be such that we would be perfectly content with what we are and what we have, without ever dreaming of what others may be in them- selves, or what in all the world we may have "missed". Furthermore, to ever hope for really "true happiness" this side of Heaven has been alway vain. only a dream Hence Father Ryan, the "Blind Poet of the South in his "Song of The Mystic": " ... I walked in the world with the worldly. I craved what the world never gave "And I said: 'In the world each ideal that shines like a star on life's wave; "Is wrecked on the shores of the real(ity), and sleeps like dream in a grave. The peace, etc promised by the world is the peace of the Serpent - ahellofapeace.Ofcourse, there is such a thing as getting "a teste of Heaven" in this world, as we see clearly inthe lives of many saints. But that is only possible - and its up to each of us to strive for - in as much as our virtue of Hope is inspired by Faith in God and strengthened -sweetened - in confidence of His great, merciful goodness. But O! "to enjoy life in the world" is another thing. How long your Great .... Grandmother Eve dilidallied with Satan before she finally reached for the fatal apple, Holy Scripture does not tell. If it were a hundred years, which is easily probable, she would have enjoyed the original Paradise ten times as long as you've been a nun. Ead she listened to reason and been appreciative for her creation and the unsullied faculties that graced her soul and caused all on earth and in Heaven to smile in her direction, she would never have had time to give way to unprofitable curiosity or to dis- content that the devil never fails to foster in our tainted nature. But alas! ! ! Poor Eve's sad story! Poor Humanity's sorrows! Ingratitude! Poor Sisters of Saint Francis too! we might add; and poor religious of every other order! How often they make mistakes! How often they must have cause to regret imprudence! - miscalculation! - disapointment in even most promising candidates! .. .. to say nothing of doubtful vocations. There must have been something about Sr. M.J. as a tiny infant as well as again when she was in her teens, that at least promised appreciation - cooperation with God's grace. So, rather than leave her in some old ash-can .... or later-on turn her out inexperienced, a probable victim for wolves without conscience or morality, she was nursed-on and mothered as though someone in justice really owed it to her. And now? Bittemess ! ? ! Dear Sister Mary Joseph: what you need most - and you are no exception - is a little more appreation for what's been done for you. Thank God for it all But don't forget the Fourth Commandment and those who take the place of Father and Mother; - who, in your case have taken that place so long. Finally, I would ask you to just compare the two short questions; first, the one of Old: "Why should we - Adem and myself - not be permitted to even look at the beautiful free?" and then: "Why should we - Sr. M.J. and myself - not have a chance to enjoy 'life' as other girls?" Just one little question in conclusion. Where do the great majority of the "other girls" come to in their "enjoyment of life"? If you stop to observe at all you must see that the majority of them find a very short taste of real joy. A sadly portion of them fall to be sickning "flappers", despised by men and women alike; "houses painted in front with vacant attics and nothing stable below". If you had to deal with the cases of lost virtue and of blited faculties and of shattered hopes that every confessor and every doctor meets, one of your first prayers would probably something like the following: "From the 'joys of life' as promised by the world and passion; C Lord deliver us!"

Thanks be to His merciful providence for all His blessed designs. Whether to my discredit or other- wise, I am still here in this remarkable part of country. Instead of a day as I figured on, its more coming a week since I arrived in Los Angels. - A name well befitting such a gentle wonder-land. Last Saturday, after Fr. Stephen (O.F.M. Cap) wired to you, he informed us that the very best he could do - in regard to transportation - was to get "reservations for next Thursday (12th) instead of yesterday (9th) for Seattle, so that I may use my "pass" to St. Paul. To get on the train as I pro- posed, without reservation, he stressed would be foolhardiness. So here I am still - hoping to make the best of missing the privileges of the Chapter. With one or two exceptions, I have met all my nephews and nieces and their children. A few of them seem "straying the way of worldlings," but thank God that seems rather exceptional - here and in San Francisco, in Portland and in Seattle. After all, however, it is not going to be my pres- ence that will work anything worthwhile. Rather it will be someone's prayers. You will be pleased to know that Dr. Turell -- formerly head of Detroit Police -- was at my (child- ren's ) Mass last Sunday with his son Jack. The latter received Holy Communion and seems to be a real practical and well anchored Catholic. He took us up next day to their home in the mountains. Both parents seem quite pleased at the step he took in the direction of religion. I am praying the good God for holy guidance of the Chapter. I only hope that nothing may be done to weaken discipline (notwithstanding my example ) and that worldliness and want of devotion to our Eucharistic King may get a check of some kind. For surely our appreciation in this latter regard is often manifestly wanting. The inclosed card will help in straightening the intention books Brother Leo or Br. Rufin it to me. I have about half a dozen intents as yet.

Dear Mrs. Kenny: God bless you and yours. I came down from Retreat in Garrison a few days ago to find quite a stack of letters a- waiting opening. I just came to yours of the 23nd and sure do sympathize with you and your family. However, we've had so many decidedly worse reports than about your Pat, that turned out most remarkable after several months of suspence and anxiety, that I shall still hope for a good word about Son Patrick F. At all events I have just enrolled him in the Seraphic Masses as requested and we shall not be surprised at any favorable report to come. We'll pray and hope - trusting in God for the best. After all if we look at things in light of faith, the worst, as the world considers things, is only cur Victory - according to our dear Lord's own words: "Greater love than this no man hath that a man give his life for his friends". This I think ought to buoy us up as it is needed in millions of sad bereavements these days God bless you again and love to all the family and friends

Dear Sister Mary Berita: God bless you and yours. I just finished your letter of March 10th and am inscribing the name of Mr. James Peters as a member in the Seraphic Mass Association which I trust may help him some- way. This in fact is the secret of the wonderful prayers they were tell- ing you about in Barclay Street, New York. The following will interest Mr.Peters and his friends. This is taken from "Notes and Favors" I have been making now and then for years. "Mrs. Catherine Nagle - 45 -- mother of eight children having been found so full of cancer when opened up for operation two weeks ago (May 9th) that the doctor sewed her up with out further attempt to help her, lamenting that she'd never leave the hospital alive(Providence) "Having enrolled her in the Seraphic Mass Association, her husband asked: "IS there anything else I could do for her?" "I suggested that he enroll the Poor Souls - having his own deceased relatives specially in mind" . "That's good", he said offering a special donation .. . whole Family storm- ing Heaven by daily Communion." ."Leaving Hospital To-day, though unable to take any nourish't **** "Thanks be to God! Mrs. Nagle, as above (May 25). Fearful pains and abdominal swelling entirely gone. Has good apetite and eating normally. . Husband smilingly enrolls Poor Souls as before in thanksgiving. *** Brooklyn, N.Y. Sept. 14th "Mrs. Nagle, noted above May 25 and 29th here To-day, seemingly OK. here agin in perfect health." (added later - really - 1946) Dear Sister: I hope this may give you all a little more courage to pray on and with your friends, storm Heaven. I often advise a proposition to the Poor souls; viz, that if an operation is averted, e.g., they donate an enrollment for the Poor Souls "of the operation averted - or charity to some good cause, and besides prayers and Holy Communions, etc.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your charitable and generous favor of almost a month ago. I remember you and your pecu- liar case very well. I surely am pleased that things have adjusted themselves so well. God in His wisdom and mercy working so favor- ably in all. I hope too that your Husband has arrived back by now. Please pardon delay.

God Bless you and yours. Many thanks for favor of the 19th just noted. Am enrolling you and family and the holy suf- fering Souls for your guidance. Glad of your interesting meet. on the first. Mrs O'Malley sent me word about it yesterday. Now I must tell you something that, in a way, I do not like to do. Its this. The arch enemy of our Blessed Mother and of im- mortal souls, at all times on the alert, must have received an ex- tra length of rope these days. I have been reported as having been phoning you longdistance and the "Agradan . Society"! ! ! Whatever the source, it seems to have given important offense, if not scandal . . Therefore, I wish that for the present and until you be better known and your efforts recognized, you leave me out of the picture. Afterall if Venerable Mary of Agrata is a saint, about which I find it personally unreasonable to doubt, then., in my way of thinking, its high time she get active in working a miracle of some kind, in clearing away the prejudice or jealousy or at least misunderstanding that has hampered her work --- which is not hers but God's work --- and hes pressed on your sholders for three years and on mine for at least seven. IV Book ". . . not your work . . but the work of The HIGHEST TRUTH." Our M. Mother to M. M. of Agreda. About 575 Coronation about 575

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your favor of the 21st, just noted. I am so glad to know that your dear little one is improving. I surely hope she continues so - and surpriz the doctors. I am you and your husband in the Masses as the herewith cards indicate. You should each make a proposition to the good God in your own best way, to do something in Thanksgiving if the. baby is spared. I think I told you something to that effect last week. In the mean time we'll keep on praying and trusing in the Good God to see fit and best to spare the little one. God bless you all - and breathe a little for the conversion of this poor sinner Solanus who makes so little progress in faith, hope and charity.

God bless you and yours. I have just read and noted your pathetic letter of the 19th and thank you for same -- having enrolled you for your balky knee. I am inclosing a Sacred Heart (blessed) to place on your knee and I hope that our dear Lord may smile at you and cure the "old knee." Rational Creature! Your purpose? . .. Why did God make you? ; ? . Ah! My blue-print primary purpose · God made me to know Him. - - O what a bles'd aim! To love Him and serve Him Sure rests in the same It's Heaven- begun -- for the grate- Ful -- on Earth! -- To treasure aright! ? !! ! Highest Heaven it's worth (God Himself the reward. (even here) .

God bless you Mrs. Helen Winke -- you and yours. I am glad you are still carying on. How wonderful -- the Good God has been to your Family; -- Indeed to us all! notwithsanding our many sins and stupidities. I surely hope the doctors get a favorable surprise when they come to operate on your Husband. I have enrolled him in the Emergency list of the Seraphic Mass Associan and that -- even that -- seems to work wonders at times.

I thank you indeed for your favor just noted. Pleas God I shall comply with your request and shall consider it a . privilege. I surely congratulate you on not only successes that have come to you of late, but I might say -- now that the sky has cleared -- especially on the unusual knocks whereby you and yours were tried some twenty years ago. How can we ever be fully grateful?"

God bless you Mr. Wollenweber - you and yours. Sorry to hear of that old heart of yours playing truant. Do not worry about, but thank the Good God you still have such an organ to play on and keep time. With love and with Christmas blessings to all Comes the INFANT once more to free us from sorrow. Whose garb and Whose mien and Whose gentleness call To each heart and each soul for a manger tomorrow. Whose Birth and Whose power and Whose wonders proclaim Him, the SON OF THE VIRGIN as promised of yore; O! May He estrange us from sin with its shame! - And reign in our hearts as His crib evermore. God made me to know Him. O! What a bless'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. It's HEAVEN BEGUN for the GRATEFUL on earth; - To treasure aright! ? ! HIGHEST HEAVEN its worth.

God bless you Mrs. Barden. Many thanks for your favor of the 6th -- your Son Rex's enrollment and the other poor sinner Solanus. Only when he gets to Heaven will he be fully converted. -- So keep on praying for him -- we'll pray for one another.

God bless you and yours. I hope this finds things brighter and improving with you. Only To- night did I get to open and note your favor of the 8th. I have enrolled your father and yourself. I hope for the best and that you may experience a de- cidedly surprize.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of last week. I am sending the certificates, etc., under separate cover. I am glad you told me of the handicapped little girl with the brain tumor. And since you give such details of the parents etc. , I hope the whole "tragedy" may turn to have been a blessing in dis- guise; viz, to bring the child and all concerned closer to the dear Lord. I am going to copy some notes I made on a case of brain-tumor, the cure of which I know about. This case came to my know- ledge almost three years ago, when two ladies came to the Monastery Office on Mt. Elliot Ave. in Detroit, Michigan; Feb. 23rd, 1943. The elderly of the two introduced the younger: " ... This is Mrs. Wheeler who is not of our faith but whose husband is very sick and she would like to speak to you about him." Mrs. Wheeler was weeping. I asked her what denomination they belonged to and she answered: "Methodist." "Well, thank the dear Lord," I answered, "we're both Christians, so that in a way you belong to my faith anyhow because after all there is only one Christianity." "But what is the trouble?" "My husband had a tumor removed from his brain just a month ago today and just this morning they performed the third operation on him. They give me very little hope of his recovery ." .... "Now Mrs. Wheeler, I have a proposition for you to make." .... It was Tuesday. "You make a promise to the Good God in your own honest way that if your husband gives the doctors a surprise tomorrow, or by the end of the week, you will be earnest about finding out for your- self, at least something of the difference, or better said, something of the relationship between your denomination as a Methodist and the "Mother Church." "I'll do anything to please the Lord," she said weeping, "if He'll only spare my poor, dear husband." The following Friday the same two ladies cameback quite smiling and with them a man with his head all shaven and one side quite tape-up Whom Mrs. Wheeler introduced: " ... This is my husband." ...... He had certainly given the doctors - Peet and Wood - of the Ann Arbor one of the surprises of their life; who together declared, as I have it in the said note " .. miraculous that a patient should talk normally four days after such an operation." They had given him at the longest six months to live. I gave Mrs. Wheeler a copy of the "Conception" of Mary, viz, the first book of the "Mystical City of God" by Venerable Mother Mary of Agreda; that she might learn something in particular about the august Queen of Heaven our Blessed Mother Mary, that in this at least she might get an idea of how sadly those Christians are wanting in the out-standing feature of Christinaity, "Devotion to Mary," who know little or nothing of the same BLESSED MOTHER OF GOD, save that in general she was just the Mother of Jesus. About a year and a half afterwards, October 16th, she same to lament that her husband was not acting as he ought of late. I had not seen or heard from them since a week or so after said surprise visit. I asked her if she had ketp her promise -- and particularly about the Blesses Virgin. She hung her head and acknowledged she had neglected to do so. A few nights afterwards they both came back and were seemingly quite happy and satisfied. They had evidently started earnestly to keep the promise she and probably both had made. At all events he especially seemed enthusiastic about the seid Book. He surely looked and seemed to feel happy. I have no doubt that if those parents of whom you wrote me - the one baptized a Catholic at least and the other, though good at heart, with little or no faith - would wake up and turn to the Good God they would get a happy surprise. In case they come to New York any time, I would be pleased to see them. In the meantime, we will hope and pray. P.S. I just remembered that possibly someone would like to go to see the above mentioned Wheelers. When they called on me last year, according to my notes, they lived at 686 Manistique Ave., Detroit.

Kindly accept our heartfelt thanks for your Mass offering. The Masses will be said as soon as possible. God bless you again Mrs. Weithoff. You may well con- gratulate yourself and be consoled that yourself and your lately deceased Mother have been clients of our dear Bles- sed Mother Mary - under whatever title -- for whether as "Mystica Rose" or Mystical City" she remains the Blessed Mother of God and by His divine wisdom and power and mer- ciful condiscention blessed Mother of redeemed humanity, . therefore, our blessed Mother too. . -

I hope this finds your out-look brightening. I just read your letter of the 11th -- pathetic indeed -- and surely do sympathize with you. Perhaps I ought rather to congratulate you on the unusual experience you are of course inclined to learn/ and which the unbelieving world must look upon as a sad indication of failure. But O: Why discouragement as long as we have a spark of faith left? What different view we get by exercising and by fostering the "triune virtue FAITH, HOPE, CHARITY! In the first place "life" here in this world is so short -- comparatively so momentary -- that in regard to its success or failure one is in- clined to think: " ... After all, what is the difference?" -- "life" so short, that worldlings are so inclined to worship as the only LIFE -- as everything worth. How is it possible that man can be so shallow-minded and still be considered "rational"? Your failure, yes, is an indication of weakness of some kind, somewhere. But if "The weak thing of this world hath God chosen to confound the strong ..... " as St. Paul so wonderfully assures us -- and the history of religion abounds in examples and all creation says Amen -- then why ever be discouraged: unless it be that our faith, more or less weakens? Why dear sister, you ought to rather thank God for having given you such an opportunity to humble yourself and such a wonderful chance to foster humility -- and by thanking Him ahead of time for whatever crosses He may deign to caress you with, CONFIDENCE in His wisdom. Confidence in God -- the very soul of prayer -- hardly comes to any poor sinner like we all are, without trials and humiliations, and your failure, though simple and possibly single, has no doubt been quite a little cross, at least for a "little soul" to carry. There is a little verse I am sure will prof you to keep in mind and ought help you foster confi- dence in God. "God condescends to use our powers, If we don't spoil His plans by ours." God's plans are always for the best: always wonderful. But most especially for the patient and the humble who trust in Him are His plans unfathomably holy and sublime. Let us, therefore, not weaken. Let us hope when darkness seem to surround us. Let us thank Him at all time and under whatever circumstances. Thank Him for our creation and our existence, Thank Him for every thing -- for His plans in the past that by our sins and our want of appreciation and patience have so often frustrated and that He so often found necessary to change. Let us thank Him for all His plans for the future -- for trials and humiliations for as well as got joys and consola- tions; for sickness and whatever death He may deign to plan; and with the inspired Psalmist let us call all the creatures of the universe to help us praise adore and Him Who is the Divine Beginning and the everlasting Good -- the Alpha and the Omega .
A thousand thanks for your good wishes and your favor just noted. We'll pray for you and hope thing go better with your husband, John and will all.
for God's holy guidance God bless you Mrs. Beaman. Nothing more practical to please the Lord than prayers and enrollment for the helpless in Purgatory.
Thank you for your letter and the donation for the enroll- ment. I sent a certificate to Wilfred. May God bless you, We will remember you in our prayers.

God bless you and yours. I do hope your are well and able to smile at at your international enemies - in so many cases perverters of truth and justice. I received your kind favor through Sister Mary Clarissa of the Guardian Angels' Home. about two weeks ago; for which ... many thanks. I was hoping to get a chance to write you a really worth while letter. But the longer I wate, it would seem the farther I get from a "let up" in correspondence. So I've decided to write you briefly, at least for the present. Of course I am not surprised that they are trying again to make trouble for you. I am sure you have been more or less expecting it. This I concluded from what has gone before. But dear Doctor: perhaps the dear Lord is expecting something that you are not regarding. As time goes on I am convinced that we poor mortals are quite alike in many ways. For example, we are naturally inclined to minimize the importance of the spiritual and the eternal and to over-rate the physical and the temporal - the latter at the cost of the former. Hence the Good God, often in His mercy, sends something - at least permits it - to come to us for the purpose of waking us up, lest we forget the final purpose of our exist- ence as rational creatures, viz. to know our CREATOR and, in love and service to blend our existence with His for all eternity. Of course, I know that you have been doing a lot of charity-work these past years and I have thanked God to see it. It indicates to me at least, that you have more faith and more charity than many would like to concede. After all, however, rightly ordered charity begins at home. That means, in my figuering at least, the cultivation and fostering in our own individual hearts and souls the supernatural virtues of faith, hope and charity - essencially one virtue. In other words I might say it means for me personally, that I should strive continually to learn more and more about God my Creator, about God as my Redeemer, about God my Sanctifyer. Because in only as much as I know anything can I appreciate it. as I know a good person can I love him. In only as much Herein God Himself will be no exception. He wants, therefore, to be known in order that He may be intelligently loved. Therefore, the catechism puts knowledge of God first: "God made me to know Him; which means and includes all the rest - to love Him and serve Him. Hence the little verses, which I think you will like. Let them be a simple conclusion. God made me to know Him. O! What a bless'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. It's Heaven begun for the grateful on eearth. -- To treasure arigh ! ? ! Highest Heaven its worth. God Himself is the reward even here below ( though only as a shadow, comparatively). But dear Doctor Koch: what I wanted to propose for you is something like this. You have shown quite a little interest in the one great science necessary for real contentment in this world and for supernatural hope in the life awaiting us beyond the

God bless you and yours. I do hope you are well - and by this time able to smile at your poor inter- national enemies: in so many cases perverters of justice. and truth. Poor enemies! because in sad part materialistic - atheistic - little better than fools. I received your kind favor through Sister Mary Clarissa of the Guardian Angel Convent. This was several weeks ago it seems, to, me and I surely want/thank you for your generosity. I wanted to wright you a worth-while letter and finally To-day for the first time in several months am I "out of the woods" with my urgent letters. Thanks be to God for everything. Sister told me of your said enemies, again trying to make trouble for you, and asked for prayers for your guidance. Of course I am always glad to hear of you and get such reques. I know you have need of prayers. Who in tis world don't need them ? And this, I might say especially for one whose abilities and whose work brings him in contact with so many teptations and such opposition as does yours. I know too that you do much for the community that men know little or nothing about - often are lothe to acknowledge, or to belive. However, dear Doctor Koch: I have been wondering if there is mt something else that our dear Lord may be expecting to see you do for Him; viz, more earnestness in providing for the "insurence of your own soul's salvation". Charity is always good; always to be commended and fostered. But after all, rightly ordered charity begins at home. To my mind that means it should begin right in one's own heart - to be practical, in my own soul. But if the primary object of my creation and my existence as a rational creature is to know my Creator, and this, in order that I may be able to love Him and serve Him, and finally by cooperating with His grace, blend my existenc with His in eternal, unspeakable glory; then my first obligation, my first charity is to fulfil my obligation of gratitude to my Creator by trying as best I may to recognize My Creator/that thus, I may intelligently appreciate and some way manifest appreciation. In other words, reason itself and gratitude for my creation - gratitude for the "next to infinite manifestations of God my Creator's/wisdom and power and goodness and love"/demands that I really ought make the science of my relationship with Him, my Creator and God - the primary and the out- standing business of all my faculties, in all places and at all stages of my rational existence. Perhaps someone will wonder if there is such a science. Well, if there be no such science, then I would say there can be no rational creatures either. Because the very first and surest indications of intelligence, as I figure, is gratitude for favors received. And since the very first favor any creature can receive is its creation and creature can(not) come into existence of itself

God bless you and yours. I do hope that you are well; and that by this time you are able, as once before, to smile at the seemingly desperate efforts of your really pittyable, international enemies. Pittyabl, because so frequent- ly perverters of justice and truth. No doubt you have been wondering at my silence and seemingly want of appreciation/ your generous favor of several weeks ago. I feel that, were my failure to acknowled same to continue much longer someone might even be scandalized. Not that I have failed to remember your kindness and charity or that I have not made efforts to write you; but I wanted to get something to you that would be really worth while, and that takes time. Besides all this dear Doctor; there has been something else in my mind I wanted to get it into yours: viz, to get you to realize that there is very likely something
- for speedy recovery, God willing - God bless you Mrs. Ravine Do not worry too much. We'll pray and trust in God.

God bless you and yours. I hope this finds you well and that the, "kind of mixup" caused by my transfer hither, etc, may not be so grave as to be insurmount- able. First I want to thank you for your constant zeal in the work of the poor foreign Missions as manifest from the realy laudable number of enrollments received from you these past years. However, while I have seen your name quite often, I have been force by circumstances to rely very much on others to keep up my correspondence and acknowledgements. Notably ever since they took me in the ambulance to the Hospital where I remained for nine weeks, That was a couple of years back and for about sex months following I was able to do very little. I went to the Monastery- office; yes, but even after I was well on my feet again, there were so many callers that I had to give personal attention to, that/ I worked for 18 hours a day - as was sometimes the case - I could not attend to one quarter of my personal letters. Since my transfer from St. Bonaventure's my personal callers have been by no means as heavy; though my letters - possibly because I have to take care of them myself - seem a heavy as ever; and you can imagine how I appreciate it to have someone like one of the Brothers or Fathers in Detroit continue their generous assistence in the work that, even with such help, often keeps me - with other duties - from 5 O'cl a.m. Il p.m. Brother Leo and Br. Rufin and Br. Gerard and often one or the other Rev. Father have helped me thus. After all, as long as the wonderful work is done and it goes to the same headquarters, what's the difference who coes it. That Heaven is pleased with the work of the Associ- ation and you Promoters have mighty big share in the merrit - ought to be manifest from the number and often the astonishing nature and magnitude of the favors we have reported as thru the same great source of blessings. Thanks and glory to God!

I wish to thank you sincerely for your kind alms for the Capuchin Foreign Missions. I am sure that the prayers of the missionaries will ascend to the Throne of God for your welfare. The certificate of enrollment are inclosed herewith. - Many thanks for your favor of June 12th God bless you Dear Mrs. Geraci. Yes, Mrs. Geraci, Your letter to Brooklyn was forwarde to me shortly. Noted the holy Masses as requeste and do trust that everything comes according to God's holy designs. How wonderful are His ways -- and His mercy is above all His works. Blessed be His divine Providence!

Thank you for the kind favor of August 26, which has been recorded as you desired. I shall remember you and your sister, Nora, in my prayers, and I hope that the Lord will give you both strength and courage to live according to God no matter what opposition may rise up against you.

Many thanks for your appreciated favor duly received and noted. May our dear Lord bless you and yours and give you His holy peace! We shall always deem it a privilege to comply with such requests. We hope that our efforts will be satisfactory. How wonderful, in the promotion of mutual and common charity, that -- next to our happy dependence on Almighty God Himself -- He has made us mutually dependent also on one another. And, inci- dentally, what a marvellously different society we'd have here, and what an ideal world to live in if we'd all keep in mind the assurance of Jesus, "What you have done to the least of my brethren you have done to me."

God bless you and yours, - every thing that interest you worthwhile. I understand you are once more in trouble - as years ago when we two first met, you took the pledge and, as I thought, we became pretty good friends. (Not?) I have ofthen thought of you Walter Mcclellan, since that night when you took the pledge and, thank God you kept it. Many a time, however, I have wondered if "big W. Mack" ever tried to realize in any way what he has been missing in refusing to believe in RELIGION and in God, and in failing to foster faith in Jesus Christ. I am sure Walter would be quite a different, altogether happier man if he only had the Faith: - Ah! - that faith which down the centuries has been the consolation and the stay of uncounted millions. Of course, the very fact that I respect you as I do, ought to be proof sufficient that I am confident you can not be a real atheist, - except possibly such a one as have been heard to thank God for their atheism. ! For as a matter of fact Walter; in my opinion there can hardly be any thing worse for the individual or for society than atheism; - nothing more positively opposed to right reason and hope, the very soul of terrestial happiness. Hence, the fearful definition to follow shortly. But first, - Think of it! -- if "Gratitude for favors received is one of the very first and surest indications of intelligence" and if the very first benefit possible to any creature is its creation, its existence, then in the Name of God and of right reason and of decency itself, where is there a shadow of excuse/ the atheist and his atheism? We'll let the definition answer. "Born originally in the haughty pride of Lucifer himself, the prince of diabolical darkness, atheism as the climax of intellectual and spiritual insanity, is at once the hopeless con- clusion and the desperate refuge - suggested by the devil - 1st of shallow thinking, 2ndly of perverse, degenerate minds, and thirdly (fearful to say), of damned fools." Its first and immediate, ruinous effect which comes simultaneously with atheism, is the loss of supernatural hope, the very soul of hap- piness in this world; viz, for any one really able to draw the first practical conclusion, "obligation of gratitude".

for Special Inten. God bless you Mrs. Stone - you and yours. Why worry so easily! Is not God watching over us the divine Aut'or of all beautiful solicitude? Rather start now to thank Him for His designs for your future. "God condecends to use our powers If we don't spoil His plans by ours".

I am glad you are feeling improved. Keep up the improvement and don't give way to worry or discour- agement. That never pays. If we could only learn to appreciate the holy faith and the innumerable blessings flowing from it and the blessings other- wise surrounding us; We could never have time to worry about anything - except that we're so little appreciative. P.S. Congratulations to your Husband, H.

Many thanks for your appreciated favor of August 24th. I have enrolled the Poor Souls specially for your intentions and mine. I am confident they will help us out of many troubles that would otherwise come to us. Thank you for your kind prayers. That is something all need very much. Thanks be to God for all things.

I just read your pathetic letter in regard to your little Daughte Lois' eye-trouble. I certainly sympathize with you and your dear Hus- band in this, though coparatively trivial matter. We'll pray, however, and trust that it may turn out to be no more than trivial. It is about twenty years back that a young couple brought their first-born to us at the Monaster of St. Bonaventure, the pupil of whose little eye had been scratched and lost fluid. Their doctor went with them to a specialest in the D. Whitney Bld'g who wanted to remove the eye at once. · Then in consternation they came to St. B. and enrollied promising a perpetual enrollment and especially more frequent holy communion. Thank God the eye healed shortly and they never went back to the doctors. So dear Mrs. - and Mr. Bieke - shake off the ex- cessive worry and istead exercise a little con- fidence in God's merciful providence by first promising some even a little sacrifice of some kind in thanksgiving if things go favorable and then, to show your confidence in His goodness, start and thank Him when ever you think of it for what He may see best to do for the little one and for her loving friends.

God bless you Miss Alice O'Brien -- you and yours . Many thanks too for your kind favor of Oct. 6th -- duely received and noted. Yes I quited enjoyed the short visit with the five guests over night, etc. . . Indeed I did know your Mother Anna -- almost like a sister. I stopped several weeks while learning to run the trolly cars in 1887 with our Aunt Mary and Uncle Pat and of course. She was (I think) a few years older than I but we were quite friends: -- also when I started working in the State's Prison- - Uncle Pat one of the guards. . . . When you write to Joe, tell him. Best Regards and God's blessing from Fr. Sol. I think I owe him a letter or two: but my big problem is my correspondence. So please pray that be able to speed up. --- Fr. Solanus, O.F.M. Cap.
For God's holy grace and guidance. God bless you Miss O'B. Pl. pray for poor sinners and don't forget
