Many thanks again for your kind favor of Nov 74 -- duely received and noted. Only today, however, did I get to answer it. I am enrolling you in the Seraphic Mass Association also. We do well to remember how very short after all it is till our suffering - and our time of merit too will be over. Let us offer everything, there- fore to the divine Soouse of our Souls that He may accept it as helping Him to save immortal souls -- Cur own included. It will help greatly too, if we keep in mind what is meant by Eternity. . St. Augustine was want to say : "What is not eternal is worth little. " That is, in itself - te restrial joys and sorrows alike. . Many thanks for your prayers.

I was pleased to receive your kind favor of the 9% even though it was not as bright, as of course, we all would like to see it. However, God knows best, and, while we'll still hope for a favorable surprise, we can hardly do better than, not only be resigned to whatever God permits, but even beforehand thank Him for His mercifully loving designs. In this way we can foster confidence in God, whis is the very soul of prayer, and con- sequently heighten our hopes for supernatural int- ervention. Not only this, but in thus fostering confidence, we greatly eliminate the danger of sadness, want of resignation and impatience which, though not necessarily sinful in themselves, never- theless sadly frustrate God's merciful designs. Hence the little verse : "God condescerds to use our powers If we don't spoil His plans by ours." Besides this, dear Mr. Morgan; I want to thank you for your practical interest in the apalling cas of Dr. Kraus; whose efforts and personal sacrafices in the cause of the very principles of justice and truth -- of religion as against atheism, the supreme science of our hanny relationship with God and our neighbor against the "diabolical climax of intel- lectual and spiritual insanity -- has been so out- standing and, at times, so internationally recognized. I do hope that something may be done to right some- thing of the flagrant injustices against which Dr. Kraus has been fighting. I am confident that sooner or later his idealism - so really Christian - will prevail; though it seems to me he is fifty years ahead of his generation. I feel that if he only persevere and cooperate with God's grace, never wanting to good wills, there will come great results from his so far, heroic warfare. So, too, do I hope that the good God whose ways are so unsearchable, have something ahead of poor, dear little Rickey Grix. All this, not withstanding scientific conclusions in the one case and, in the other, . . political atheism.

God bless you and yours for a blessed Christmastide and, please God too, a happy prosperous New Year. I was sorry to learn of your not being well. I hope its nothing too serious. But whether serious or not, we may be sure that inasmuch as we take such things as from the hand of God, they will never fail in the end to turnout as having been a blessing in disguise. At all events I am enrolling you in the Seraphic Mass Associa- tion and am praying for your speedy recovery and thereafter speedy improve- ment, - physically of course and, what is infinitely of more importance, spiritually. God knows that, in our stupidity we all need real conversion to Him. Anyhow, I hope things brighter for you soon in both regards. No question about it, if we do the right thing on our part God never fails us. Just here, however is always a danger. We are naturally so inclined to go wrong. Therefore too, our obligation to admonish one another when danger threatens. Hence, Dear Doctor Young: I feel that I would not be your friend or even a decently grateful patient were I to be silent as to dangers ahead of you as I see them without any doubt. Only yesterday a middle-aged couple - friends of yours too - lamented to me that after several years in holy matrimony, they had never been blessed with - what I have long since considered the greatest blessing that, in the natural order, God gives on earth, A Family. And my Doctor Young has no family. ? Because the family that God blessed him with has no head. ? At all events, it is a sad situation; and notwithstanding the fearful prevalence of similar cases, it must be, in the sight of Heaven a most lamentable problem. Not since yesterday only Doctor, has this been on my mind; but since away back in July, and decidedly more so since early in September; when a youth came into your office while I was waiting in one of the apartments and whom, judging from his voice and the familiarity that followed between you, I took to be a son of yours of probably fifteen to seventeen years. He seemed promisingly bright and alert; but what pained me as the little dialogue proceeded was the sad want of filial reverence and even respect shown to his father. So much so, in fact that I almost called out to him: "Boy ... Honor thy father and thy mother". "Alas", I thought afterwards, "The poor lad has only an absentee father and his mother a convert . Where is the responsability? Who's to blame? Honestly dear Doctor, I've been thinking ever since that day, how to devise, or what, to induce something of Christian peace and harmony into that half-divorced family, - something to bring that father and whole, half-divorced family together. You can imagine my surprise this morning, therefore, when a hitherto stranger to me came begging for prayers to help "storm Heaven" for this very purpose. The party was evidently a friend of yours, as well as of your whole family. Of this I was convinced after a very few words. In- cidently, one of the primary causes lamented, with what seemed to me genuinely fraternal solicitude, brought back to me a rather disapointing remark you made on occasion of my first visit to your office. If you remember I had just given a definition of, "THE GREATEST SCIENCE OF ALL AGES" as, "RELIGION IS THE SCIENCE OF OUR HAPPY RELATION- SHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR", adding that, while there may be an in- definite number of "religious systems", there can be only one science of RELIGION".

God bless you and yours. I hope you are well. Perhaps I ought rather to say I am trying to hope for your welfare, - spiritual of course and especially, as well as physically and socially: because after all in the sight of Heaven, the first is what supremely counts. I have been wanting to write you Doctor these several months. In fact I started a couple of letters to you before Christmas, especially when I learned of your serious heart-attack and enrolled you in the Seraphic Mass Association. But first let me too, as a member of the community, thank you for your charitable favor to Rev. Father Guardian several weeks ago. I was doubly pleased to hear of it - for your own sake as well as for the needy poor. For it would seem in many cases that just such exercises of charity has meant the final salvation of many a soul otherwise most likely lost. Tow dear Doctor Young; I want to tell you in all sincerity and truth, that for close to a year you have been a problem on my mind, and I feel that I would not be a friend of yours or a grateful patient were I to let the present holy Easter Season pass without at least fraternally calling your attention to the very grave danger ahead of you, of completely losing the very little faith in Jesus Christ and His Church which, (un) for- tunately at least, you seem to have left. But; "Why such an alarming conclusion?", you will ask. For indeed your outlook in my way of reckon- ing is grave. First. Because, according to the greatest theologians, the first punishment on sin is the withdrawal of sanctifying grace - of God himself, therefore, - and the consequent weakening of the soul to fall again with less resistence into the same and other sins. For: "God will not remain in a soul subject (to) sin." But surely this must apply to the culpable neglect to foster and to practice that God-given faith that we have so gratuitously received and which has been so tenderly and conscientiously fostered in our souls, - God himself breathing it into our very immortal souls with loving parents and tutors so providentially solicitous. But, in God's blessed Name, who can claim exemption from such Guilt? I for one could never dare think of such a thing. Can you Doctor? Then, if "gratitude for favors is one of the first and surest indications of intelligence", then, in the name of everything that is logical, and intelligent and holy; let us be men enough to acknowledge our weakness, our stupidity, our real insanity and guilt in the sight of Heaven: thet by such humble acknowledgement - How mercifully simple and easy! we may recover our friendship and our peace with our God in Heaven -- at once -- the divinely gentle and loving Governor of the universe, and the no less divine Avenger of the proud and the stubborn who refuse to appreciate His merciful goodness and to cooperate with His gracious condescinsions. Something for me as well as you Friend, and us all to think about. Not? Then Doctor: you possibly remember reading the great encyclical of Pope Leo XIII on the Holy Eucharist, even when it first came out. Anyhow, I think it has been generally considered a decided master-piece, at once like-inspired and indeed very inspiring. Here is a notable passage from it that I have often considered and that have often wished were proclaimed again and again, in season and out of season: "History bears witness that the virtues of the Christian life have flourished best wherever and whenever the frequent reception of the Eucharist has most prevailed. And on the other hand it is no less certain that in days when men have ceased to care for this heavenly bread, and have lost their appetite for it, the practice of Christian religion has gradually lost its force and vigor." And because society is made up of individuals these great, great documents, - the encyclicals - pertain to the instruction and the welfare of the individual and society in general alike. Hence it goes on, like a divine admonition and exhortation:" "And indeed it was as a needful measure of precaution against a com- plete falling away that Innocent III., in the Council of the Lateran, most strictly enjoined that no Christian should abstain from receiving the Communion of the Lord's Body at least in the solemn paschal season." Ah! "as a needful measure against a complete falling away ... " Where are any of the protestant sects to-day or the protestant nations in their, "practical faith in God and in Jesus our divine Redeemer, or in God the Holy Spirit our divine Sanctifyer? Where is Russia? Where is official England or official Germany or France? etc? They have followed the individual. To a sad extent they have fallen victims to atheism - the most diabolical cancer, because the climax of intellectual and spiritual insanity, -- at once, -- the hopeless conclusion and the "desperate refuge" of shallow thinking, of perverse and degenerate minds and, almost fearful to say, of damned fools. Hell is its officeal headquarters and none other their supreme knight than Lucifer himself, the prince of diabolical deceivers." Protestantism! Christianity without our eucharistic God! without Holy Communion! ? Christianity without the virtues of the Christian life! We had a memorable funeral in Detroit about ten or twelve years ago, - memorable no doubt for those called to attend it. . A one-time prominent judge who as a youth and as a young professional had been quite commonly looked upon and not infrequently referred to as "a model young Catholic", but who, for some cause or other abandoned the practice of frequent and regular Communion. Little by little he had left off attendence at Holy Mass on Sunday and shortly dropped that practice too, altogether. Finally he turned more or less against religion entirely, as it would seem, since he discouraged at least on 32nd degree mason from personally looking into Catholic claims and practices. Of this I was informed by same mason's own widow, who having called for a priest on his death-bed died a Catholic. This was several years before the unfortunate death of the judge, who seemingly having become disgusted with himself and with everything else, went secretly and hanged himself. I think dear Friend: this ought to suffice to convince you that my apprehension as above, is not at all far fetched. . I am not the least surprised Doctor; that under the circumstances and most especially in your present condition of mind and soul, you simply shudder at the thought of returning home to your family. That condition has been a long time growing in your mind and soul, - most probably starting with the first time you deliberately missed your Sunday Mass or some other mortal sin. Going back to your family, however, is a secondary matter and can in a number of ways be bridged over without great difficulties. If ever again you get back into the grace of God by a good, humble confession, that "preternatural fear and dislike you now experience for things you once revered and loved, will at once weaken, and, little by little you will in all probability come to your old happy self again. But to dance along the "wide road that leads to destruction" and in a state of most probable mortal sin, dily-dallying with a possibility of some day obtaining the grace of God and eternal salvation, is a fearfully perilous course to take. To my mind it is positively following the steps of our unfortunate judge above referred to, in an appallingly close imitation, and something to checkup on at every and all costs. Hoping dear Doctor, that I have not been over harsh in my conclusions and that this may not discourage you. Rather on the contrary that it may simply wake you up before it's too late, from your most threatening drowsyness, I beg to remain Please do not forget Doctor; I need prayers as well as any other poor sinner. In this it seems to me we are all in like need -- not knowing, as the great Apostal of the Gentiles teaches: "not knowing if we be worthy of love or punishment, - love or hatred."

Kay the Lord give you his peace!, you and yours - that peace of which the "world" knows little or nothing; the peace which St. Francis was so astonishingly successful in promoting, the peace to establish which, the Second Person of the Blessed Trinity came down from Heaven and lived, suffered and died as man and the promoters of which, "shall be called the children of God". I have been wanting to write you Doctor but I feared to embarrass you. I have wanted to talk things over but you've escaped me. I was pleased at your bringing that, "Companion of the Summa", as you. called it. I would wish to have seen more of it and to have talked it over with you - in connection with the primary purpose of my visit. For, to be frank, much as I appreciate your treatments and miss them and thank you for them, they must be altogether of secondary importance in face of the condition of your immortal soul and the danger of which I see you to be in of losing it together with your faith in God and His Church. I was happy to see you, as it seemed to me, that you were trying to do the right thing and to be happy. To the rational creature it must mean the same thing. I still hope you are trying. What more can any of us do? Its all the Good God requires or expects of us. - TO TRY. Success must depend on Him. He does expect, however, and He will be the Judge as to whether we will have used the means He offers to insure the success He expects and which His justice will demand. Alas for humanity! How sadly few comparatively, ever think of such an obligation? - Alas! Hence the want of peace for the individual. hence the turmoil! - domestic; - national, - international! Everyone seeking peace, - as positively as the stone in the air seeks rest - and there is no peace for the rational creature except in the willing service of its Creator.

it. Dear Doctor: You gave me a treatment on Tuesday. God bless you for I hope that I shall always appreciate such favors - every and all favors; for appreciation means gratitude and: "Gratitude for favors is unquestionably one of the very first and surest indications of intelligence." But I felt that day there was something on your mind; that you were not your own self - happy as you ought to be. In fact I've felt that way more or less right along. The next day I again had the great privilege of singing a High-Mass, and as usual for several months I had J. P. pretty much in my mind. During the "Pater Noster", possibly due to more than ordinary fervor, when I came to the words: " ... sicut nos dimittimus ... " - And forgive us .. as we forgive those who trespass against us", I almost faltered. There was something like an answer or a response in my very soul to the effect: "Unless and until he forgive .. I can not." That evening at Matins you came to my mind again as I intoned the psalm: "isi Dominus ... " , "Unless the Lord build the house, they labor in vain who build it. " (126) And from the other choir came back the response like a divine sanction: "Unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it." How Doctor: I want to assure you that it is not to embarrass you that I am writing you thus. Cn the contrary, I positivily feel that I could not be your friend without making as strong an effort as possible to save you fearful embarrassment unquestionably ahead of you unless, by the grace of God you open your eyes and cease trying to do without Him, - without God! After all, what is the embarrassment of a friendly fraternal correction when contrasted with the multiplied accusation at the General Judgement Tomorrow before heaven and earth as well as all Hell? For my part I have long since come to the conclusion that when there is trouble ahead, the quicker we prepare to meet it the less its going to amount to; whereas, the less we make of it, if it be real, the worse its going to prove. But you dear Doctor; while in quite a number of ways you have been doing good - have been an asset and a credit to the Community at least as far as the general public sees. You have used the talents God has lent you to a great extent in a creditable manner. Has not God bles'd you too, and temporarily at least filled your heart with grateful appreciation for the ability to do for Him and for humanity? But are you going to drift on, and into eternity satisfied with the natural "rick you get out of it"? - and the temporal advantages, including in this latter the shadowy credit of an unthinking public? I am asking - addressing - these questions as to a brother who can draw conclusions; as to one who, in the sight of Heaven can not plead ignorance. Are you going to continue till too late, to tacitly defy the Church of the Living God - doping your conscience with the poison of modern atheism, the climax of intellectual and moral in- sanity, that you can get along without the Church and her sacraments and consequently without God? Get along without the Church? A peacemaker without humbly confessing one's own sins? ! "Charity begins at home". Peace is an outstanding characteristic of charity. They accompany eachother and must begin, if really genuine, between God and the individual soul. ... "without me you can do nothing." "He that is not with me is against me and he that gatherith not with me, scattereth." "He that heareth you heareth me. .. " If the withdrawal of grace is the first punishment on sin, which means the flight of the Holy Spirit from the soul guilty of sin and if peace is outstandingly a gift of the Holy Spriit, and furthermore, if one of the parents of a family virtully defy the divinely installed and established representative of peace, then Doctor; can any thinker aquainted with the case be surprised at the scandallous want of peace in such a parents home? -- and of course, that every immediate member of the family be upset is quite to be expected. Fo positive faith fostered or appreciated, or moral obligations for a rational creature? Is it not as selfunderstood, Doctor; at least with philosophers, that all these necessarily go together - reason, moral obligation, appreciation, religion? Just to quote one little saying from the prolific pen of one most outstanding and universally acknowledged of all philosophers and moralists: "But if any man have not care of his own, and especially of those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel." St. Paul (I Tim. V-8). Of course Doctor; I know that unless one be some way in the grace of God, this must be boring to read. Neither is the drilling of a hopeful tooth pleasant - for the poor doctor any more than for the agonizing patient. But, But? If you dear Doctor; will have patiently read the above, having prayed for light and a good will, there will be great hope for both of us in your regard. Not only a tooth, but a temporal life worth living as well as an immortal soul will be saved. In the name of Saint Francis, and through his most humble, therefore, most powerful intercession; may the Lord give you His peace - you and yours.

My Dear Confrater Simon: More than simpley to say "A thousand times many thanks" for your practical/in the elaborate preparations and actual celebration of the golden jubilee at dear Saint Bonaventure's a few weeks back (Jan.26); I want to congratulate you and your dear Tertiaries - every Juniors ofcourse as will as the Seniors-and I am inclined to say especially the members of the privileged Eucharistic Mission Band, on their beautiful, artistic, generosity. One could hardly feel other than convinced without a second thought that they must all have worked in real Franciscan harmony together in "so masterly putting over" such a fraternally loyal display. May our dear Lord bless all and each who helped along. I am sure that, even aside from the solem holy Mass itself - whose very ceremonies, etc, I am assured brought tears to many a noncatholic eye - that the mutually fraternal simplicity of the whole proposition was a source of much happy edification. Writing later on when the tention of excitement had gone (if there had been such), a certain Jew who attended and understood the beautiful prayers with the epistle and Gosle, etc, assured me that he could not restrain his tears.

Yes, I shall join my poor prayers to yours so that God may give you the happiness of always conforming your will to His.

God's holy grace and guidance - patience in all trials." Emergenct membership God bless you Mrs. Barnum. We will pray for you and yours.

I received your pathietic letter of January 23rd and do surely sympathise with you. I hope, however, that is His great mercy and in- finite wisdom the good God may see fit to draw good from your plight and as He never fails to do, inasmuch as we take our crosses in resig- nation at least to His holy will, turn your seeming misfortune to have been a blessing in disguise. I have been down here in St. Felix since last April. So for the present am no more at St. Bonaverture's in Detroit; though I was up in Detroit all last week, as the little cards may at least intimate. You might do well, nevertheless to visit the Monastery there on Mt. Elliott (#1740). They can enroll you in the Seraphic Mass Associa- tion as well as I can, and that is a big feature in the "secret" of the many notable favors there reported - as well as in our other friaries. Thanks be to God. At all events, dear Mr. Taylor, I am going to tell you of just one of said notables; that you may draw your own conclusion and as I sincerely hope, draw therefrom a happily profitable lesson. The case was noted close to four years ago in my own hand and runs sub- stantially as follows: "March 26th, 1943, Andrew Wheeler, a methodest of 686 Manistique Ave., Detroit, had 'brain-tumor' removed four weeks ago, (Febr. 23). At first, operation seemed to have been successful but two weeks later infection started. March 12th second operation. "Last Tuesday, March 23rd Mrs. Wheeler accompanied by a Catholic neighbor came weepingly lamenting; " ... They have just operatid on my Husband the third time in a month and they give me very little hope of his recovery. .. " "Now Mrs. Wheeler", I pleaded, "do not take it so hard. We will pray for your husband and enroll him in the Mass Association and try to in- duce the our dear Lord to take over the case Himself". .... I re- corded Mr. W's name, etc. "Now Mrs. Wheeler, I have a little proposition for you to make yourself to the good God in your own honest way". "I'll do anything to please the good God", she interposed, "if He will only spare my poor, dear Husband"! "Vell this is the proposition or promise I want you to make, if you choose this rather than something else, whereby to please God. It is more a suggestion, therefore, that you promise or earnestly resolve in your own mind to look into the claimes of that "Mother Church" divinely planned and proclaimed infallible, and the claims of any other denomination or system of religion. Or I might say that you look into the con- nection between them". .. .. Mr. Wheeler came home the next day - the day before yesterday and is here with his wife and neighbor To-day. A patch of about three inches square was like taped a- round and above his right temple. While I was noting the surprise, he remarked to the party who had given him his place: " ... its great to feel normal again, though I feel a little weak. Drs. in Ann Arbor, Peet and Wood, call it miraculous ... that a patient should talk intelligently inside of twenty-four hours after such an operation". Thanks be to God". I had not heard from them for over a year and a half, when Mrs. Wheeler came to lament the her husband was not very well of late. I asked her if she had kept her promise as I had sug- gested and if she had read the book I had lent her - "The Mysti- cal City of God". She humbly admitted that she had not. She had come without him, as she said, because she wanted to tell me about him first. I told her without hisitation: "The whole trouble is in your failure to keep your promise, or your proposition whatever it was". She promised to return next night with her husband and in the meantime to do something to show her good will. It was very stormy the next evening, so that she phoned their inability to come as promised but that they would come the following eve- ning. Following is the note I made under the original: Oct. 18th, 1944. Thank God they are both here To-day. He has started to read the said, won- derful life of the Blessed Virgin, the "Mystical City of God" and is quite enthused about it". Among other things in praise the wonderful work, the "Mystical City: which has been referred to as the autobiography of the Bl. Virgin herself, he remarked: "I find so much in it that I have often wondered about. I hope dear lir. Taylor, that I have not bored you overmuch with the above. If I were an experienced typest I would do the whole thing over. Under my circumstances, however, that is out of the question. I am enrolling yourself and Mrs. Taylor in our emergency List and will hope for a favorable surprise of some kind - and a favorable report. P.S. Incidently, I think it is slitely an error for one who is a Christian (as I presume you are), or who believes in Jesus our Redeemer, to intimate that he does not belong to the same faith as another who, though believing in Jesus Christ and professing Christianity, happens to differ with him in some details, pos- sibly not even essential. Because I claim that there is really but one Christianity, as scientifically there can be but one religion, though there be a thousand different systems of that "Greatest science of all times and or all generations - "THE SCIENCE OF OUR HAPPY RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR.' "Thus saithe the Lord: Let not the wise man glory to his wisdom, and let not the strong man glory in his strength, and let not the rich man glory in his riches: But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, for I am the Lord that exercise mercy, and judgement, and justice in the earth: for these things please me, saith the Lord". (Jer. IX, 23-24).

Many thanks for kind rememberance. Haven't been here since April 25th. Sorry I missed you. I received word from Mr. Stanton wrote me of your flight to Europe - and shortly after came your cards. · I hope by this time he believes more in his Patron . - St. Anton. ! Best Wishes. Clerical Novitiate (rear) -- looking S. E. to City down a mile and } on the Wabash. We have 18 promising novices pray for 40.

I hope you are well and that the dear Lord guide you. I've "kind-a" been expecting to see you these days and been wanting to write. . . so our sending a card at least on "Little Christmas,". April 24th, 1949. God help us; it just struck 11 P. M. and want to get this off first in the morning. I just came across this letter of yours of Dec. 18th, 1948. . . . with Mrs. Stanton's $20.00 cheque, etc. I hoped to see you last January and get informed --- instructed rather, etc. What shall I do? I am not clear about anything regarding this matter and it must look to poor Mrs. Stanton as if Fr. Solanus "don't care." I'd like to go into details but. . .? I suppose it would be rather out of the question that you could come down closer to St. Felix together. ? We have a "Guests' Apartment," where we could talk things over. We have a "Guest quarters here" to accomodate seven and I am sure you would both enjoy a little visit. am confident that Mr. Stanton was a Christian at heart and a Catholic. I feel too that Mrs. Stanton is at heart a Catholic: for as I have been stressing for years there can be but one Christianity and but one religion - - - the greatest science of all ages and the perfection of that science. God best you both . . all.

I am just starting, for a day or P. S. Pl. pardon hast. so at Milwaukee, Wis. Dear Mrs. Doyle: God bless you . . . I am sending this (above) just as I found it this morning. With several others I got From- ane poison in Milwaukee and had an experience quite worthwhile. Thanks be to God. Afterwards too, here and in St. Joseph Hospital in Ft. Wayne. Doctor Hoffman there, I hear, feared I would lose my lower legs. I never thought of such a serious thing. Thank God they are again quite OK.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your appreciated favor just received and noted. I am taking this before several letters ahead of it. ... I have a brother Patrick Casey of Seattle, Washington. He has been dear to me, having grown up with me since 1871. Ten days ago he was reported as dangerously ill. He has been a successful business-man and a daily communicant, Thanks be to God for both. I would not want to tell him of a namesake of his having no faith. He would conclude at once: "The boy does not know how to think, and unless he pray for an increase of faith he most likely will lose the little he has and in the end drift to atheism "- "The climax of intellectual and spiritual insanity; because atheism is primarily a suggestion of the devel and the hopeless conclusion at onc and the 'desperate refuge of shallow thinking, of degenerate minds and -- fearful to say it, -- of damned fools: - no one the primary leader other than Lucifer himself, the prince of diabolical darkness." Its a strong definition and to choose to be satisfied with tending to follow such a monster rather than foster faith, hope and charity by which alone, progress can be made in the greatest scienc of all times and of all generations -- RELIGION, "THE SCIENCE OF OUR HAPPY RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR", must be the choice of ? to say the least, of an unfortunate creature, - supposed to be rational. You can tell that poor P. C. from me as well as from his older namesake that while we sympathze with honest men who tend to think (?) in that line, or are content with the prospects of an eternal blank of even nothing-ness, - to say nothing of hell, in which the vast majority of every age of thinkers have believed - we would at the same time call attention to/obligation we are all under of asking for faith, a free gift of God and without which, God himself has revealed we cannot please Him. Any one who has been raised a Catholic. - nay who has believed in God and has fallen away from such faith, little as it may have been, will have a fearful responsibility to answer for if satisfied to meet - to take the chance of meeting - the divine King of the Banquet without having on the "wedding garment" of charity; viz, without faith, because without faith neither hope nor charity (profitable for eternity), can exist. A real and outstanding "trace of the Holy Trinity" as the divine "stamp of Heaven on the immortal soul", God will require on the Day of Judgement if we are to be admitted as having on "The Wedding-garment". Its up to the individual to preserve, to acquire, to appreciate that free gift of God's gratuituous liberality. If God made every rational creature primarily to know Him in order to love Him and serve Him as only rational creatures can, then surely there must be something in the very nature of every rational creature inclining him to seek such knowledge. Therefore: "Woe to that man who through his own fault loses the faith he has once received - or who having come to the use of reason will have failed to acquire and foster it. Hoping that this may help some one in some way to wake up before too late, I beg to remain

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your favor of the 20th, just noted. I am certainly pleased to know that things are brightening up in some ways at least. Just keep up your courage and pray on, and you may be absolutely sure that God will never fail to be more than liberally generous. In fact we only have to think of how merciful He has patience with poor sinners who never seem to think of Him - ourselves included - to be convinced that it is out of the question for Him to fail in His goodness to those who call on Him with conficence, sorry for our poor sins. I am glad you are able by the grace of God to have patience with thos who laugh or sneer at anyone turning back to serve God and save their souls. Just that is the very secrete of success in the science of saving our souls, after all the greatest science of all times and of all generations: RELIGION, THE SCIENCE OF OUR HAPPY RELATIONSHIP AND DEPENDENCE ON GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR. Some people have a queer notion of religion and, therefore, I might say an even queerer idea of conversion. . .. . . It seems to me, therefore, that to be converted means to receive the grace of God, one way or other, to come back more and more earnestly and more practically to know, to love and to serve God. And since we are all so inclined to go rong and to sin - even born in sin -- we can always be converted (in the wider sense), from our less perfect ways: and if outside the true Church, people can be converted from paganism and Judaism to Christianity. If they already believe in Jesus Christ as so many good protestants do, they can be converted from their errors and from human, therefore erroneous systems of religion, to the one and only divinely established founded system, viz, the Catholic systom or true Church of Jesus Christ. Let me stress here the expression, systems of religion, because if as above defined, religion is a science, there can be but one religion, whereas there may be a thousand different systems. Furthermore, inasmuch as we believe that Jesus was God amongst us and that as God He keeps His promise, "all ages even to the end of time to be with us", as He is with us in the Most Blessed Sacrament; so we must believe too that according to His promise: " ... Thou art Peter and upon this rock I will my Church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it," we must believe that the system of religion which He founded can not possibly go rong. "For the Church cannot err that has God for its guide." And again: "He that heareth you heareth me .... " And stell again: "He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me, scathereth." ***** ** How disapointing to Jesus! - to professed followers of dis "reforming His Church", instead of following. ... As to that depressed feeling, etc, you complain of or lament, it may be from your age. It seems most women have an experience similar to what you describe, for a time after they are about forty-five. In such cases they usually have to practice quite a little patience - with themselves and with others. At allevents, try and keep up courage and shake off anxiety as much as possible.

It was only last night that I came to your letter of the 9th (Febr.), forwarded hither from St. Bonaventure's, Detroit. How wonderful are not the ways of / Lord as well as His works! I surely was pleased with Jack's Few Years report - almost surpassing my most cherished hopes, that your- self and poor, dear little Irs. Turrell too had received your First Koly Communion on Christmas. It surely brought a tear to my eye, as even now it does writing about it. I once more am glad to congratulate you on your privilege as on that night I did on long-distance. Of course the same goes for Mrs. Turrell as I felt it did that night. I was surprised after we hung up that I did not ask to speak to her personally to con- gratulate her too, but then I thought; its better instead, that we just turn to God and thank Him, the divine source of such graces, such happi- ness, such consolations. Fortunately I was in St. Bonaventure's that night to receive such tidings and particulars, directly. When I told the others next day at dinner they were more than pleased. Father Salesius especially and the others present who knew you while here in the Bast. When I told them of my pleasant experiences on meeting you two years ago in Los Angeles, how I had gotten in touch (with) Mrs. Turrell, surprising her on the phone and about our "children's Mass next day, Jack, with his details about St. Anthony, so tragicly changing his hesitation to determination, etc; Father Provincial thoughtfully remarked: "That is quite a remarkable case." I've been thinking of late, especially since Jack and you all are so rightly solicitous about his success, even as a manager, God will- ing, - why not? - and especially since Saint Anthony seemed so solicitous himself as to give "his life for Jack's decision" to continue instructions and actually join the true Church, we should go after him with confidence in his intercession and not let him rest till he finish the work he had possibly in his mind when (he) awakened his protege,

God bless you and yours. Only late last night did I get to read your kind favor of March 1st, duely received and noted. Many thanks for same. I rather regret, however, that I failed to find the sister's name whose condition is lamented. I wanted to enroll her in the Seraphic lass Association - a great part of the secret (?) of the many favors reported back to our monasteries, as answers to prayer. I shall enroll her any- how, as best I know, in the hope that possibly the merciful God may deign to smile some way at our "daring simplicity". Adored be His blessed de- signs. In the mean time please send me her name for registration. Rather have her write me as she proposed to do and explain the trouble as best she can. Why should she hesitate? Details are not necessary of course. But something personal would naturally be better than a report from some one else. If, as you tell me, she tries I am sure we will be able to help her. We have had cases that I am sure have been more threatening by far than hers, judging from just what you have told me, that have come out better than before afflicted. While waiting to hear from her I am sending you a letter for her, written by one of my reverend brothers to another - ordained just a year apart -- 1911-'12. For five yrs. the elder was hardly ever able to say Holy Mass. Now in his 80th year he says his office and Holy Mass every day. Thanks be to God. I am sure you will all like the letter.

I have just read your pathetic letter and do surely sympathize with both you and your husband, - with him possibly the more, because of his greater danger of losing his soul, unless you be induced to turn back to God. You tell me as much as that our friend Grace Panyard guided you hither and again that you are not "of my faith". Whatever you be, you have an immortal soul - your ownself - to save for God; and I am glad to help you do that. I presume that you are a Christian of some denomination. If I am right, then in saying you do not belong to my faith, you err in a way; because there is only one Christianity. Think a little and see if I'm right. I go further. If religion can be defined as a science, and I claim it is not only a science but the very greatest science of all times and of every generation; in fact the only science that in the end counts for aught, and without which all other sciences are vain allusions. Ah! "RELIGICE, THE SCIENCE OF OUR HAPPY RELATIONSHIP ( dependence on), WITH GOD AND OUR NEIGHBOR". Furthermore, while there may be a thousand different systems of that science -- a thousand various denominations - the science of religion remains one. Its up to the individual with the use of reason, cooperating with God's grace to find which is the best system and to choose it rather than any other. On his choice depends to a vast extent, his own peace and that of the community - as well as their hope for eternal happiness hereafter. Kost probably the trouble of which you complain is an effect, a simple consequence of want of this science, lack of religion. One is almost forced to conclude that neither of you are much advanced in this appallingly neglected science. As to what your husband was once upon a time is a mighty small matter for him to "bank on". He certainly was never one of the Apostals or an archangel. Judas was. Lucifer was. If he has given up the exercise of faith in God and the fostering of religion, rather I'll say that inasmuch as any of us fail in this vital matter, in just so much does the individual stand in danger falling a prey of Zell. Some ten years ago there was a fearfully tragic death in Detroit. A ce tain judge who as a young man had elicited high compliments publicly given as a "practical model of a young Catholic". Even in his youth, however, it would seem the same judge had been naturally inclined to petty jealousy. Whatever the cause, he had little by little given up the practice of his faith - the sad way we are all inclined - and finally abandoned religion entirely and in the end went and hanged himself. May the dear Lord preserve us such a fate!

God bless you and your friends, and us all. I hope you are well and that your friend-patient is not losing. We received your wire some nights ago and enrolled M. O'Laugh'n in the Seraphic Mass Association as an emergency case. Today we received your special and are enrolling as the enclosed will indicate, a perpetual member. Thanks be to the merciful God, we have had several notable cases of cures reported as through this means here as, especially in Detroit, and esewhere. Rather than detail instructions what for anyone to follow, I am going to give you here a brief resume of a letter I wrote several months back to a presbiterian whose father, grand-father and great- grandfather were all presbiterian ministers and who I believe is now taking instructions or is possibly already a practical Catholic. In fact there are two cases here involved, - bothe noncatholic, therefore, Seery or an O' would say: "on the other side of the fence". It follows about thus: " ... I am sure dear Mr. R.J., I tolde you of the W. case, noted here just about two months ahead of yous. Lest I be mistaken, However, here it is in brief. 'March 26, 1943. Mrs. W. ... W. was a methodist, had been given up after the third operation on a brain- cancer as destined for death inside six months. (The first opera- tion was on February 23rd). Mrs. Wh. weeping was introduced same after-noon by a Catholic neighbor. .. "Ill do anything to please the good God if he'll only spare my poor, dear husband"., she answered. "Then, Mrs. W.", answered, "This is about what I would advise you. "Make a promise or proposition to Almighty God in your ovm honest way as a methodist, that if your husband gives the doc- tors a surprise tomorrow or by the end of the week (it was Tuesday), you'll be earnest in looking into the difference or rather the re- lationship between your denomination and the "Mother Church". .... They returned the following Friday with Mr. W. all taped-up but smiling. He had come home from the Univ .- hospital in Ann Arbor next day Wed. Doctors Wood and Pete had pronounced his recovery miraculous. October 18th a year and a half later they came back - the last time I saw them and he looked and acted as he'd never been sick. This, however, was two nights after she had phoned me, lament- ing that he was not well, etc, and I had admonished her to do some- thing toward the fulfilling of the promese she had made so many months before, if her husband were spared her. Besides, I had given her a copy of the "Mystical City of God", - the winderful Life of the Blessed Virgin Mary, which I honestly consider her own autobiography; the actual writer being as her secretary Venerable Mother Mary of Jesus, of Agrada Spain. He especially seemed enthused over the book that night - had evid- been on the "job" of reading the book, those couple of days.

God bless you and yours. I hope you are well, as evidently you are not too bad to write such an interesting letter as that which I have just read from your pen. And all notwithstanding your trying berievement of losing your dear, patient Wife Mercile. I surely would like to have seen her and consoled her before it were too late. Rather I should say, to encourage her in her acts and disposi- tions of faith, hope, charity, patience, resignation, confidence in God etc. What a privilege; what a happiness to have been of assistence to anyone in their final struggle and to have whispered an encouraging prayer into the ear of the patient when naturally everything must seem dark and hopeless! From what you have written of her, however, with all her struggles and humiliations, etc, I think she must have learned quite a little of the one most important art of "dying well". Incidently, I had an "atheist" in-law lose his eldest born, ten years ago on his way with his family to the diamond jubilee of his wife's parish - St. Joseph's in Prescott, Wis. That was where myself and a number of my brothers and sisters had been baptized, including one of my Rev. brothers. I said "atheist" because he had never been taught much, if anything in childhood, about God and the science of religion and consequently had never joined any denomination. He was a good, clean-living man, however, and from the outstanding example of his wife - Kathleen C'Brien her maiden name - and the sweet prayers and peace pervading his home as a result; he had learned to admire the wonderful faith, so inspiring of hope and real supernatural charity, she practiced and fostered. The son drowned in Chicago on their way to the Jubilee. It happened on his seventh birthday. They took the little corpse along and we buried it in her family plot a few paces from the graves of my two little sisters who died in one week when I was eight, 1878. Pardon such details. But you were considerate in the details of your letters to me and I hope these may be to good in one way or more, so just briefly, I am inclined to believe it difficult for anyone except a parent to realize what such a death must have meant to my in-law. The poor man just seemed to wonder. It certainly made him think more deeply about essentials. However, that was not the worst. Just six years later after a brief illness, his said Kathleen also was taken; leaving him three children to mother for himself as best he might. He wrote me at the time that at first he had just wondered like if the sun might shine again. This, however, seemed to be the turning-point. The greatest sermon he had ever witnessed -- her example of never failing Christian virtues -- had planted seeds of admiration for Christian faith in his

God bless you and yours. I have just read your favor of the 8th - pathetic enough in its way, though indicating nothing to be over anxious about. Good housekeepers and good busines-men are careful to have "a place for everything and everything in its place." In this they show a trace of the divine character of the universal Guide and Master, Who of course, has a place for each one of us. He, the Creator and Divine Governer of the universe in all its details, could create children as in the case of Adam and Eve without parents. He could teach little children without nuns or schools and give the holy sacraments as has been the case on several occasions, - without priests, therefore. In His divine economy, however, God has been pleased to honor His creatures- most especially His rationals - by giving them, each accord- ing to his ability, a part of His own work to do. Rather I ought to say, by participation and cooperation in His won divine activity, etc. Why be over anxious, therefore, about something that God himself is infinitely more solicitous than any of His creatures can be? If you go to the divine Headquarters by receiving holy Communion frequent- ly, and earnestly and humbly plead with the divine Spouse of our souls for guidance not only for yourself but particularly for each of those friends of whom you write - I am sure you will have nothing to be par- ticularly anxious concerning the important matter of your vocation. In the meantime of course we will be glad to include your inten- tions in our poor prayers.
I hope this finds things brightening. I have just enrolled Richard for this intention. We'll pray for you all - that our dear Lord guide and guard.

November 4th. Again many thanks for your generous favor of October 16th. May the dear Lord bless you for same. Thank you specially for enrolling me. Yours must make about a dozen perpetual enrollments I've had this Jubilee year, and I have no idea how often I've been enrolled annually. The continued favors we have reported as through this association gives me an appreciation for such enrollments that I could hardly have otherwise. Thanks be to God. .. As to taking children for adoption, I look at that according to our dear Lord's own appreciation: "What you have done for the least of my brethren You have done to me. " -- It is getting late now: So. I'll say Good Night for the present and clerical novitiate. This year Thanks be we have 24 promising novices. to God. We could place a hundred more priests if we had them -- in home and foreign missions. P.S. Congratulations on your joining the privileged Family of the Franciscans.

So glad "little Tommy" is bigger now and doing so well Thanks be to God. Snapped to the side of the Chapel St. Felix Monastery, Nov. 4th 1947. God bless you, Mrs. O'Flaherty. I hope you are all continuing well. Please pardon delayed acknowledgment. Many thanks. I wanted to write you a letter : but ---! "God condescends to use our powers If we don't spoil His plans by ours."

Many thanks for your kind favor of just a month ago -- duly received and noted. I've had it right here waiting to get a chance to write worth while and it just seems such a time never comes; I do hope that by this time Mr. Flaherty is quite o.k. and that Tommy continues to like it in the Seminary more and more. Indeed that is a grace initself for which we should never cease praying viz. to be grateful for and love the vocation to which, in His great mercy God has called us. This of course really applies to every vocation, for after all, What a privilege to serve God in even the least capacity! -- Nay even as an irrational as the flowers and the birds! and the bees that praise the Lord providing for man. !

I recieved your very interesting letter several weeks ago and started a number of times to enroll your little "hopless case" in the Seraphic Mass Association; and each time I found no name to record. Consequently post- poned further action. Now I am going to give you a few particulars about that notable case that you probably never heard. Then you will easily conclude something as to what I would suggest and advise. It was Saturday Morning January 10th 1925 that a neighbor-friend of theirs from Port Huron, brought your dear Parents to the St. Bonaventure Monastery in Detroit. Your poor Father was hardly able to talk. He tried, however, to tell briefly how he felt and that the doctors said he had "ulsers of the stomach". Later on I learned that they had sent him home as a hopeless case of cancer. I told him quite a little about the Ser -- Mass Association and suggested that he do something for the missions. "Now I have you name Mr. Eagen." I said. "And you can enroll perpetually if you wish. If you are anyway short, however, I would advise that you enroll for just a year now and promise a perpetual enrollment as soon as convenient, if things go favorably." With a feeble quivering voice he answered: "I sure will." I took him to be 75 years old or upwards; Your poor Mother looked old too. Sunday morning eight days later your Father dove his own car down to keep his promise. From their appearance alone I would hardly have known them; but themoment he spoke I thought: "This is the fellow from Port Huron!" He looked thirty years younger. He was only thirty-nine at the time. . "But Father"; he said, "The I doctors in Pt. Huron want to take an exray ... What do you think?" asked him : "How much is it going to cost you?" " ... $25." "What do you think?" I asked your smiling Mother, They were bothe smiling all over. "Father, he don't need it. Look at him!" she exclaimed. "Listen." I said. "You make a promise to the poor souls in Purgatory, that if you are able to forget that apointment tomorrow, you'll enroll them for a part of it." "Gee!" he said, "I'll give them half of it. I'll go them fifty-fifty." After that he drove down every week for several months. Febr. 29th - I believe he had the whole Family down - having enrolled some other, as he nearly always did, he concluded about as follows: "Now Father; I want to enroll the Poor Souls as I promised them I would. Put them down for a good half of that $25. - fourteen dollars." Some years afterwards I was up to see an old lady in Smith's Creek who died shortly after with cancer of the stomach and your Father having heard of my visit came and took me over to see the little farm you refer to and I remember seeing little Dorothy. Congratulations on my "dream" even then of her vocation. Try at least to become appreciative for such a really surpassing privilege. - Think of it Sister M.C. of. .. A chosen spouse from among millions, - a spouse of the eternal King/kings! How little it is possible for any mere creature to be adequately grateful for such a privileged calling! We can only try and that suffices. Do not forget to send in the name of your little "hopeless case" friend, and to have as many as possible to offer prayers and holy Communions, not only for her but for so many more sadly unfortunate "big shots" in hospitals and elsewhere who, having little or no faith, in the super- natural, refuse to believe in even the possibility of miracles, and who by a manifest miracle might be induced to at least pray for the gift of faith -- which Almighty God is only waiting to be asked for. Sincerely

God bless you this blessed day of the Lord, - you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of several weeks back. I started a number of times to acknowledge same. I hope my tardiness may not scandalize. Not only this favor, however, do I want to thank you, but more I want to assure you of our appreciation of your generous activity these several years in the really privileged, though not less arduous work of the holy foreign missions. I am sure that the Good God will bless - has blessed - you in many ways for your practical interest in this outstanding phase of really Catholic action. Besides this, I want to congratulate you on your having been so guided as to be able to write of a business associate as you do of the young man with whom you condole on the death of his amiable mother. It is always a relief to know of such a person. The very fact of his having been a "bible student" ought to spell something in his favor. This, even though, for want of proper guidance, many a "bible student" has anchored in dangerous waters. But these days when atheism, the very climax of intellectual stupidity, of moral insanity, of diabolically devilish perversity; it is a hopeful indication to see anyone of good will taking more than ordinary interest in the divine messages from Heaven as are those conveyed to humanity through the inspired writings, the divinely guided compilation and the appreciative, prayerful study of the Holy Bible. This all the more now, that in the family of governments one of even the "big powers" is not only permitted to show its shamelessly criminal face, but brazenly to insist on dictating hell's own principles of peace. Indeed an unmistakable indication whither our godless system of public-education is, not only tending but tumbling; unless by an effective S.O.S. call of true religion. Pardon my digression. I would have enrolled your friend-associate as also his deceased mother, but I did find their names. I have no doubt but that they would both profit thereby. So if you just send me their names I shall be glad to do that for you and for them. Wishing you and yours God's blessing again for a happy day of national Thanksgiving; and especially in case you do not in the mean time hear from me again, the grace of a blessed and happy Christmas celebration with all success for the coming New Year and thereafter. Sincerely Yours in Christ.

Many thanks for your charitable favor of Dec. 22nd duely received and noted. Only To-day, however, did read it. I've been "half down" for several weeks and have not been in condition. Thanks be to God for it all and that things are clearing up again You were right · about the Poor Souls, I did refer to those in Purgatory primarily. You idea further is right too. So many poor Souls. I am glad to know that you know from actual experience so much about the benefits of the Ser. Mass Ass'n. I have forgotten the particulars of your trouble but your idea of doing something in thanksgiving for the favor you hope to receive is certainly practical -- just as I often suggest. I hope it brings the hoped-for results.

Many thanks for your favor of May 6th. It is rather hazey in my memory what your trouble was in December, since I get different cases often mixed. However, I feel you are taking a practil way for any and every "hopeless" -- so called. We'll pray for your intention and try as best we can to foster confidence in God - and in the intercession of our blessed Mother Mary.

for a speedy recovery, God willing. Special member God bless you Mrs. Turner, Do not worry. God bless you Mrs. Turner. If "courage is half the battle" then with confidence in God it must mean sure triumph -- whatever the natural outlook.

Thank you for your kind favor of July 19. I shall pray that the good Lord will grant your intention, if it is for the good of your soul. I do not think that I know Mrs. Jennie Ferreri personally, at least I can't recall her just now.

God bless you, and keep you fostering the happy resignation in your souls which looms out in that little word of Mrs. Turner: "I have eased up on offering prayers for a complete cure; feeling that perhaps my constant inconvenience may help the poor Souls and also in the conversion of poor sinners." And then again: "God knows my needs, etc., etc. That really sounds lile fostering confidence in God, than which hardly anything can be more pleasing to God and at the same time more profitable to our own poor souls. Such resign- ation and Confidence is a great grace in itself, which we should at all time and in all circumstances foster. Your promotion of devotion to our dear Bl. Virgin Mother Mary by means of the rosary and the scapular will surely bring untold blessings on you and yours. By all means keep it up. for we can never be to grateful enough to such a singlarly chosen and privileged blessed Queen of the entire creation, God's own blessed Mother, whom, in His infinite condescention, wisdom and mercy has deigned to give to each and all of us if we only appreciate. As to the stole proposition; well I do not remember or know of any one specially in need of such a prized garment jus off-hand now. I do know we have many priests on the Missions in Central America and in Islands who would surely appreciate such a donation. Probably the simplest solution would be to give the equivalent to some one in immediate touch with the mission-work going on in so many places. Our own Father Pro- vincial of course would know best where to place such a dona- tion. I am sure Brother Rufin or any one at the desk in St. Bonaventure's in Detroit would be able and pleased to receive the favor. Or if preferable you could include it sometime whenyou send a check hither to St. Felix.

God bless you Mrs. Alvera McCarroll. I am glad to hear from you though sorry to learn of your poor dear Husband's affliction. However, it must be for some good purpose and will turn out to have been such if you keep courage while battling along and making the best of the situation. Try and have your Husband and friends go to Holy Communion more frequently with you. Nothing like frequent communion to bring peace into a family or into a soul. At the same time it fosters faith in God and heavenly relationships - with all God's dear ones gone ahead of us. Many thanks for your prayers for poor Fr. Solanus. Like all other poor sinners he need the grace of God in order that he be fully converted. Clerical Novitiate 23 Novices this year. Pray for them and for vocations.

God bless you and yours. I do hope you are well and that this long delayed little message finds you with brighter outlook than seemed to be yours when last I heard from you. Though thank God, it had already brightened. Now Sister: though my past silence might seem other- wise, I want to assure you that you and especially your poor, dear Parents and folks have been on my mind more than you would think. I surely do sym- pathize with you all. Most especially I may say with your poor, dear Father because, as you seem to think and is quite probable, of the bitter disapoint- ment and scardal he must have met with in some unfortunate judice of a priest. Alas! it seems to be a sad fact, there had to be a Judas among the Twelve Apostles, and ever since there have been those among the priests of holy Mother the Church - sometimes even bishops that have betrayed her. In fact we know that the most terrible scandals have come just thru the falls of priests and bishops. No doubt St. Bernard had this in mind when speaking of scandal he concludes: "Since the scandal of the Crucifiction of Jesus Christ it is never reasonable to take scandal." For that was surely the most terrible scandal of all. And still Almighty God has turned it into the salvation of those who will be saved. O the mysterious ways of the Lord! "How incomprehensible are His Judgement! And how un- seachable His ways!" As for yourself dear Sister Agnes Carmel; since I read the first half dozen pages of your big letter, I have been convinced that there is nothing wrong with your mind atall. It has seemed to me that you have been suffering for someone else - most likely for just your same dear Parents and folks, and of course at the sametime for your humiliation and con-sequently your purification. You really ought to thank God for offering you such a mission. I might rather say for imposing it on you; for other- wise you woul hardly have had the courage to consent to it. I mean to the sacrifice it has cost you. And the victory (over the devil and scandal), is not as yet gained. At the time of your last letter, when you requested the return of said long letter, I did not really know where I had put it and consequently had to let go. Just a few days ago I came across it and I decided again to write to your Father and see if possibly I can do somthing to promote peace in his poor soul and in his family; for I am sure that after these long years of estrangement from the Church, from the Holy Sacraments and from religion which alone promotes peace that the world can not give, He must be longing for a change of some kind. I have no doubt God will have mercy on him and help us. For I believe he has a heart that wants to do right. I thought, therefore, dear Sister Agnes Carmel that before I would write him, I would ask you about any change that possibly has come to your Father since you wrote me about him. This es- pecially sinc it is so long that I have not heard from you - and about him, And otherwise too the outlook may have changed. Besides; if you have any suggestions to make as to the way I might approach him, etc, I would certainly be glad to receive them. Furthermore, if you still wish me to send you that letter to help others in matters of your conscience, and you find satisfac- tory results, just let me know. Hoping this finds you and your whole outlook brightened and brightening, I beg bo remain in the privileged service of our dear Lord's "least brethren". P.S. Dear Sister Agnes Carmel: After the above conclusion I read your interesting letter of April 27th last, which I should have taken time to do before writing; and again as before I would stress the necessity of humble patience -- of patient humility. Do not lament or be discouraged at your inabilities, e.g., of mixing with associates, etc. The conscientious exer- cise of the tallents God has otherwise blessed you with surely excuses you from such and ought to makeup for the former. At the same time just the weaknesses we experience -- and who is so stupid as to imagine he is an exception! -- are natur- ally providential guards against one of the very greatest dangers to genious, "the big-head". So instead of lamenting such weaknesses we really ought to thank God continually for them. In fact I believe that in the sight of Almighty God just the light to see such poverty in our own makeup and to realize thereby something of our stupidity to which sin has caused in our characters is a special grace to make us other than crazy worldlings that have no faith and never learn to really think.

Many thanks for your kind favor of a week ago. I certainly do remember you and your folks. How fortunate you have been in the faith God has given us strengthening it so often by super- natural responses to prayer -- as in the case of your dear Father Earl -- with his "hopeless" cancer! Glad to know he is well as also your little Sister Dorothy -- now V. Sister Mary Celia -- also wrote me. I have told hundreds of your Father's case when they brought him first time to St. Bonaventure's January 10, 1925, and how he surprised us when eight days later he brought your good Mother with him driving his own car -- looking 25 years younger !.

God bless you this beautiful season -- you and yours. I do hope you are well, as thanks be to God we all are, here at St. Felix.
