It is by one whose earnestness and honesty and really deep thinking has been proven beyond the shadow of an honest or reasonable doubt. And that "poor-guy-friend" of mine and, if you will, possibly one of God's very least brethren," is Dr. A. J. Kraus. in many ways an

We are enrolling your Association. If he be God bless you Mrs. George Schulte. We are enrolling your little Thomas in the Seraphic Mass Association. If he be not improving by the time this reaches you, let us trust in God's goodness that the doctors get a good surpris of some kind. In the mean time have as many of your friends as possible offer holy Communions and promise some extra Receptions in thanksgiving if the outlook shortly takes a decidely brighter aspect, etc. We will pray too for your intention, especially in regard to little Thomas.

To know is to appreciate - is to love what is good - is to reject what is of evil - is to adore the Divine. What consolation this offers us! What a hopeful outlook it ought to afford! What a sublime horizon for poor sinners, -- if "hope is the very soul of happiness here" and if the revealed purpose of our creation, TO KNOW GOD is kept in mind -- what a horizon for us, even though we be sinners -- if we but keep in mind the primary purpose of our creation, TO KNOW GOD. Hence the lines: God made me to know Him. O what a bless'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the same. Its "Heaven Begun" for the grateful on earth; -- To treasure aright? ! Highest Heaven its worth. But how can I know what the senses fail to perceive? How know the Incomprehensible God whose attributes - wisdom and power and goodnes and mercy-are infinite? A simple question may, in the first place, demand a simple answer. But right here, we shall do well to rem- ember a trite proverb: "A fool can ask questions - can make ob- jections - that will puzzle a philosopher to answer." A nave of course, can ask such questions too. But perhaps the nave is sup- posed to be included in the proverb; because after all, in asmuch as anyone is a nave in at least somuch does he prove himself in the end to have been a fool too. While it would be uncharitable, therefore, to say that every fool is a nave' it is always logical; to say that every nave is a fool. However, a simple answer to the above objection intimating the difficulty or impossibility of a finit creature knowing the infinite God, might be to ask another very simple question; viz. Do the senses perceive the electricity - "the juice" in a live wire? Or again: Do men gaze into the sun to consider its bene- fits? Objections like the above are futal and vain and if meant to excuse athesim, are criminal. For there is absolutely no ex- cuse for any rational creature refusing to recognize its Creator. In fact, if "Gratitude for favors is one or the very first and surest indications of intelligence", and again if according to all logical reasoning, one's first possible benefit is his crea- tion; then the ingratitude of the atheist, must of its very nat- ure - without further proof or parley - condemn him with his atheism as most woefully wanting in intelligence; and consequently, whatever his tallents or brilliance my be otherwise, must rate him as an unqualified fool. The most fearful example of such insane want of appredation and of such damnable ingratitude, is that of Lucifer and his reprobate legions, where-Heaven itself was depop- ulated and Hell's creation was made necessary - the most terrible prison-asylum ever designed or conceived. If the primary purpose of my creation as a rational crea- ture is to know my Creator so that I can love Him and serve Him and be happy with Him; amd if according to Holy Writ, no one but a fool can say in his heart, "There is no God"; then the necessary conclu- sion would seem to be that God's existence, at least, must be mani- fest, one way or other, to every one who is not a fool; consequent- ly, that every normal person able to think, can and ought to recog- nize his Creator - can and must worship God. And this under pain of losing everything good in the end and of damning his own soul - "cast out out into exterior darkness, where there shall be weep- ing and gnashing of teeth". However, in a matter of such tremendous importance it would be nothing less than positively criminal to be satisfied with the minimum. The foregoing is simply no answer atall to what we ought to have, -- and Please God to what we shall have. In the first place, there is something intrinsically in the very nature of man - and in the very nature of every rational creature -- that instinctively feels its dependence on something greater than itself - on something supernatural. History and philosophy alike prove this beyond the shadow of an honest doubt, -- to say nothing of common sense; or of theology, the queen of all sciences, so much so, in fact, that to question it seriously, would be to intimate atheism again or a denial of God's existence which accord- ing to all sciences is nothing less than an insult, not only to honest reason to every normal generation back to our, Adam and Eve, but a most flagrant ignoring of Holy Scripture, and of divine re- velation and of Gods own supreme Majesty, Who admonishes, Who pleads, Who commands: ". . . I AM THE LORD THY GOD . . . THOU SHALT LOVE THE LORD THY GOD WITH THY WHOLE HEART AND WITH THY WHOLE SOUL AND WITH ALL THY MIND AND WITH ALL THY STRENGTH . . LET NOT THE WISE MAN GLORY IN HIS WISDOM, AND LET NOT THE STRONG MAN GLORY IN HIS STRENGTH, AND LET NOT THE RICH MAN GLORY IN HIS RICHES: BUT LET HIM THAT GLORIETH GLORY IN THIS, THAT HE UNDERSTANDETH AND KNOWETH ME, FOR I AM THE LORD THAT EXERCISE MERCY AND JUDGEMENT AND JUSTICE IN THE EARTH: FOR THESE THINGS PLEASE ME, SAITH THE LORD". (Example: The graduate from Calcutta) "Dr" Schroeder (unfinished draft)

I hope this finds you well, which means of course hopeful too. This latter is something that is sadly overlooked, to the great de- Triment of spiritual progress as well as physical. The probably all-outstanding example or proof of this is the historical scandal that some of the disciples took at Jesus' choice of the CROSS AND CALVARY whereby to establish His Reign of love, rather than any other; - the scandal that drew from St. Peter Lim- self: "Master! Far be it from thee .... " and the alarming response: "Get thee behind me satan. . . , Thou saverest not of God". It is well to remember that such scandal was never intended to be confined to the Apostalic-age. Hence, Saint Bernard - the out- standing Doctor of the Middle-ages - wisely reminds: "Since the scandal of the Cross it is never reasonable to take scandal". A- mother occasion of the first disciples taking scandal is the detailed insistence of His giving us Himself for our own life of soul: "I am the bread of life. Your fathers did eat manna in the desert and are dead. This is the bread which cometh down from heaven; that if any man eat of it, he may not die". (Jno. VI, 48) Of course it is only natural for honest, upright people to resent falsehood and injustice as was St. Peter in striking off the brutal Malchum's ear. The same can be said of the wave of international in- dignation that the damnable hypocrisy manifest these days in the sacri- legious treatment of Cardinal Josef Mindezenty. Of course it is but natural for moral integrity to resent false- hood and injustice wherever accosted

No doubt you will have been expecting a report of some kind con- cerning the privileged trip conceded me recently to the Funeral of poor, dear brother, Father Maurice Joachim. I started to do this the day after the solemnities; for all considered it was a real solemn funeral and seemingly a happy one. Blessed be God in His angels and in His saints. A wire at about 7:30 Wednesday, January 12 from Ortonville, Minn. announced to us: "Father Maurice Joachim died at 6:20 this Morning". I erroneously took it for almost self understood that the Funeral would take place on Saturday, waiting for more particulars till near midnight, when a call came; but it was from a poor party - convert - lamenting their unfortunate divorce. Your Very Rev. Paternity, on my long distance call had benignly bidden me go thither. Deo gratias. We concluded that possibly the funeral might be Friday and decided accordingly to take no chances. Hence, our plans to catch the Hiawatha as probably - surest train to make the desired connections. It snowed that Thursday morning and to be sure of catching the "Golden Arrow" train on the Pennsylvania, we left early, for Ft. Wayne; - Brother Cook, Ignatius at the wheel and Rev. Father Guard- ian accompaning. Leaving Fort Wayne, the Conductor had to lament that he was 25 minutes late, which to me meant that we'd be nip and tuck in catching the Hiawatha in Chicago, if we didn't lose any more on the schedule thither. On leaving Huntington, however, we had said our Rosary for Divine guidance and protection and safe return and thanks be to God, I forgot all about worrying. We made it, even if the train had to wait a little, till they kindly got me a ticket. I was still figuering on the Funeral being on Saturday and on my staying over night in St. Paul till, the first passenger off the Coach, my friends held me up. I had to go back on the train and they accompanied me on to Minieapolis, whence, after an hour and a half, I was to take another train and go on two hundred miles further to Ortonville, Minn. , right near the S. Dakota border; thence, after holy Mass next morning drive twenty miles to Graceville for the fun- eral at ten ocl. It was 3:30 when we pulled into that station. It had been moon-light all night, though rather pale, but with the snow on the ground I heard the train-men's view come out in harmony with my own: "Its a beautiful night". We were about thirty miles from our train-destiny when I was able to stretch my bones in the empty smoking-car which was better than in a corner of a seat. Thank God that was a relief. I was at least half-asleep, when the gentle brake-man called me and I went out to find the Pastor patiently waiting. We were a half hour late. He, Father George Campbell, tooted when he saw me leave the train and greeted me like an old friend. He has a nice little (Church) - one altar - to accomodate about two or three hundred, St. Mary's. After holy Mass and breakfast, we made the twenty miles in a dense, freez- ing fog about twenty minutes before services. Father Ed'd had hardly expected me and was disappointed in his figuering on Monsignore Reaordan of Mineapolis - a one-time pastor of M.E.J., to give the ser- mon. No one else seemed ready for that privilege; so that I was a- shamed to decline when asked if I would say a few words. I took the text that came to my mind as we were leaving for the Altar: "Quid Retribuam ...? " .... Thank God; though a most happy theme if properly developed, it could not, under the circumstances, be more than exten- pore. It seemed, however, to be satisfactory. A nice crowd of in- telligent looking school children together with the silent sermon of a happy death of one who had weathered the storms of 81 winters con- secrated to Almighty God, naturaly inclined my thoughts to vocations. (for 20 minutes) .

Praised be Jesus Christ. Deo Grt. Honestly I hardly know how to begin. That million-dollar proposition has been on my mind since months before your Paternity held Visitation here last year; And the longer it go on the more it seems to me timely, opportune, urgent. Besides the encouraging proposition of our Benefactor, Joseph J. O'Donnell of Chicago, a copy of whose letter I shall herewith enclose, there are other - quite a few, perhaps mostly religious - praying for the "million-dollar essay contest. I mentioned the proposition to Rev. Mother Mary Fidelis - helpless invalid at the time - and afterwards to about fifty of her nuns, of Notre Dame Milwaukee, the day of Unvaling Fr. Stephen's Statue and of my own very fortunate ptomane-poison ex- perience, - anything but pleasant of course but - most profitable to my soul. I hope the students from Calvary profited too by their taste, at least, of similar experience. Deo Gr. for all His designs. Well, Mother Mary Fidelis and her said nuns seemed quite interested and promised to pray the good God bring it to success. I had hardly come to the parlor after blessing them with several relics and a little visit in the Chapel when I urged, "Sister, please get me a vessel quickly. I'll have to vomit. I'll wait right here on the floor". Luckily noth- ing came but strenous reaching till the vessel arrived, and then very little, with quite a relief of very short duration ~ again and again- till the ambulance came and took the patient to St. Michael's Hospital for about 40 hours. . . There is another very interested party, a certain Mrs. Gordon Thorne, quite a benefactor who without effort could donate the whole Prize ($1,000,000.) and possibly will do as much, if successful in her present efforts to break away from a trast-company that has been charging her $40,000. annually for their service. She is preparing for a battle in court on this score next Monday, 25th. She expects them to appeal the case if she win. .. She asks for prayers. A daily communicant and quite a "live wire" , with far-reaching views, she seems solicitous to make up for lost time while her non-catholic, though seemingly very charitable, Husband, Montgomery Ward Thorne, lived. Among other works of charity she is figuering on building an orphanage for His Eminence, Samual Cardinal Strich. She has been sending us his diocesan "New World" which recently received the gold medal as being the best all=round Catholic Newspaper, The Rev. editor, Father Daly, as it seems, wants to come over to learn about our "essay proposition". God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind recently received. I am enrolling your Sister and her Husband in the Seraphic Mass Association - emergency and special - and I hope you may be able to send us a favorable report. Thanks be to God, we have notable reports as through this source of blessing every day. I am sure that if they turn to God as best they can and pray to Him with confidence as we all ought to try to do, He in His mercy will enable them to give the doctors and all concerning a good surprise. Something they could do specially to please the good God in case Mr. Sherman is cured, in thanks-giving; would be to: "like-promise" to be earnest in finding out for themselves, some-(thing) about the difference of the relationship of the methodest denomination with the Mother-Church; or that they will look into and find out some of the reasons why Catholecs try so much to imitate Jesus in his love and reverence for Mary, His own dearest Virgin Mother. "Behold thy son." Jesus said to His sorrowing Mother and the foot of the Cross, referring to the youthful Apostle John - and in him as theologians and the fathers of the holy Church have always taught, - in St. John - refering to all followers of His doctrine. Then as in the same breath to St. John: "Behold thy Mother." If religion is the greatest science of all ages - "The science of our happy dependence on God and our neighboy.", which definition no one seems to question, then there can be but one religion. In like manner if: "We are Christians only in asmuch as we believe in Jesus Christ and keep His words - His doctrine - so there can be but one Christianity. Therefore, its up to each one of us individually to examine into our own conscience whether we be Christians in reality or only in name. Too, it ought to be our happy privilege to prefect ourselves in that faith more and more, and to findout its infallible Guide on earth.

God bless you Granma Kauffman: you and yours. But what is this we hear of you? Brother Leo and Mrs. Whitman, Norma, tells us you have been not at all well; and that you are in the hospital. I kinda wondered when reading this, if you were following my bad ex- ample. Well in that case, I hope you will have fol- lowed the good part too and get well in short notice. Four of us drove over to Milwaukee for the Unvailing of the big statue of Father Stephen, with whom I worked when first ordained and for several years off and on. Well, there were a couple dozen affected by ptomane-poison and, according as one looks at difficulties and crosses, I was one of the dozens of unfortunate or would rather say fortunatie ones. It was surely to nature a very unpleasant experience; but thanks be to God! I feel that my soul profited greatly by the experience of about a month in hospi- tal, -in Saint Michael's Milwaukee and St. Josephs, Ft. Wayne. It was a "bitter pill that turned to sweetness of soul and body", as St. Francis tells us in the holy Rule, about his personal ex- periences with the poor, dear lepers of his day, and as many chaplains and soldiers tell of what the went through in the 2nd World War". Now dear Mrs. Kauffman: I hope you are turning this breaking of life's monotony - all unpleasant as such experiences are to nature, - into sacrifices of great merit. This you can do by thinking on the sufferings and Passion of our dear Lord and offering your sufferings in union with those He suffered for all us poor sinners that in His infinite condescention deigns to call us His brethren. And more than this, that it may be no empty title and as a last bequest, gives us His own blessed Virgin Mother to be our dear, gentle Mother too. !!! Incidently there is something wherein you could do me and my dear Guarding Angel a real favor; ... Offer something of your restlesness for God's blessing on a pro- ject I - let me venture to say, we - have been working on for many months. If we put it over, as with divine assistence we hope to do, it will mean much toward the true peace of billions. Deo gratias! Pray too, that God's Holy Spirit guide the deliberations of our fathers in the coming Chapter in Nov.

God bless you and yours. I hope this finds you all well, especial- ly that your outlook is hopeful and brightening. Please pardon my tardiness, etc I think the following will be a decided asset to Father E's rhyme -letter. NOTE. The following rhyme-letter, "a remedy for the blues", from a missionary in the Philippines to a Rev. Brother - 12 years his senior and located in Yonkers, N. York. senior brother's health-failure in his early clacics. NOTE. The following rhime-letter, "a remedy for blues", is from a missionary in the Philippines to a senior brother brother in Yonkers, N. Y. Health-failure on part of the senior brother in his early classics had sent him home from the seminary, heavy-hearted, - a family disapointment. For twenty years working for vocations to makeup for his own failure and, on oc- casion of his serving at the first holy Mass of suether of his junior brothers he had decided; " ... to try it over again". He had joined the junior brother (now the missionary) in the seminary, and had preceded him to the holy Priesthood just one year. The letter, at once humorous and poetic as well as ascetic and thoroughly philosophic, offers food for every thinker. (a third Britger)

My Dear Friends: God bless you and yours. God bless all our afflicted brethren of good (will). I received your pathetic letter yesterday and I surely do sympathize with you. What a disapointment to any loving parent to hear such a diagnosis. "Blindness, Deafness". I surely hope D. J. will give the doctors a surprise as nearly always happens when we trust in Almighty God. At all events how merciful has not God shown Him- self to you in blessing you with another bright boy, and even in Donald's case, otherwise endowing him with such happy faculties! And yet dear friends; what are all purely physical or temporal blessings in comaprason with the faith that God has given us? - You and me, even though (we) differ, as may be, in some essentials. Besides, we have somuch in common - and this we can say of all who honestly believe in God and hope in Him, that we ought surely to be patient with weaknesses so common, if not in systems of religion at least, in application and practice. The fact too, that there seems to be such an avalencehe of atheism - the very climax 02 intellectual insanity and of moral depravity - threatening to inundate civilization: That ought to bring us all into mutual agreement and harmony of some kind. At all events, we shall be pleased to join our prayers with yours in favor of poor dear little Donald Jay; viz. in "storming Heaven", that God be pleased to give him sight wherewith to glorify God Himself and promote - be instrumental in promoting - peace among men and nations. . . Afterall, as a science (and religion is, notonly a science, but the greatest science of all ages) there can be but one religion, viz: "The science of our happy relationship with - dependence on - God and our neighbor." In the face of so much - such brazen and threatening atheism, is it not time we come together and get humanity to consider something about whither it is tending without faith in God and without fostering this greates of all sciences, which outside of the comparatively few, refuse in their blind- ness even to recognize it as a science atall? .. Pardon the digression. We shall hope and pray that little D. J. give the doctors a favorable surprise.

God bless you again. I intended to reach you with the above acknowledgement a day or two after its reception but was ashamed to send in so muddled a condition and am disapointed in my failure to have it rewritten. However you and your little Donald Jay have been on my mind and in my prayers continually since receiving your letter. I am confident You will understand something of what I wanted to write you. Had I a little more time or if I were a real typest I would run it all over. As it is however, I hope I am not too presumptious if I con- gratulate you on the answer to our combined prayers. I do hope you re- ceive a favorable report tomorrow. I am hoping, mailing this To-night. Hoping for good results.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your favor of September 30. Your "write-up" in the best weekly news-paper, THE NEW WORLD, was very ood. Father Elmer, the Master of Novices, smilingly called my attention to it. I do hope you get time from your busy duties of nursing, to be as successful with your "write", about the, comparatively little known though prolific Seraphic Mass Association. In regard to the benefits and blessings reported as through this quiet little organization, I have longsince been convinced and have frequently exclaimed ---

God bless you this happy feast of our dear blessed Mother Mary; Queen of Lourdes, Queen of Mercy, Queen of the Universe and of the Most Holy Trinity. It is really time to retire, but I must at least start with a few words to you before this date is gone, - even though it be as yet only a "duplex." I received your letter of Wednesday last evening and, as much as time would permit, have studied it since. I want to go into some details in response to it but can not do so just now. In general, however, I must say that I am greatly encouraged at its upright tone and the good will it indicates all around, - an example of patient forbearance and of gentle readiness to relent in charity. 15th 9:30 P.M. - A late start again. God Help us! It just seems that I get nowhere; and yet so many things I ought to be doing. Glory be to God! I did remember you in my holy Mass this morning and blessed you at the end. In fact your request for Tonight's "break" has been pretty well on my mind since Saturday, and in my prayers. I trust you had a favorable ex- perience rather than any serious embarrassment, - both for your- self and your teeners, ... etc. This, however, excluding what- ever might check anyone's already too weak tendency to love the really life-giving humiliations that so often gently lead us to love Jesus more, and to follow Him. But dear Sister, how fortunate you are after all now, under such circumstances as are yours, without realizing it! How fortunate in having a Rev. Mother at once so decided and yet so condescending! Surely you ought to keep in close touch with her and inform her about everything that transpires as affecting this, your so really threatening and fearful experience; - an experience that I for one, have not the least doubt is - for your final "doing or undoing", for time as well as for eternity. But what a morcy of God to be, the second time inside as many months, received back a "prodigal" on the simple obedience - the coveted boon itself - of again putting on the holy Habit of your Order: Where in all history is there another such example? It surely speaks more than any works, for poor, dear Mother General's confidence in her wavering daughter. Ah! To me it looks as though Jesus Himself were someway behind Rev. Mother on that occassion, - as indeed He does seem to be someway coaching every- thing that tends to smoothe off and, notwithstanding her many infidelities, to facilitate the return of His, sadly inconstant, Constance. Still, the enemy of souls will ask - and the destroyer of the souls' peace - "If ... "and "Why" .. and will dare to intimate that there is something wrong - something other than mercy and wisdom and power and love in God .. . concerning His adjustments of our individual cases. Ah! These "Ifs and Whys" ! Do they not sound like the wily philosophy of Grand-Mother Eve's garden adviser? ... Yes, it is disappointing to nature, to be deprived of a chance for self-justification. .. No doubt that is because of our corrupt nature's want of realization that in the science of the saints, and in the sight of all Heaven, self justification before creatures, is never a victory for the Christian soul. Ah! When we behold the astonishment of the Roman Governor and his whole court - Pilate before Jesus divinely silent. - What a contrast to our noisy self justification! Sad to say, I feel myself to have been many times a "past- master" at that kind of worldly cleverness. Just that kind of cleverness is still one of Fr. Solanus' unhappy weaknesses. Hence, another instance of mercifully sparing from embarrassment. in the sight of Heaven a wavering daughter, -- an inconstant spouse - so solicitously smoothing embarrassments away, before the Guardian Angels and all the triumphant Church and Heavenly Court, - really preventing some one from still further making a F. of herself. Ah! Dear Sister: you had cause for wonering at Rev. Mother's not seeing you other than in your holy habit; but was it not - should it not have been wonder at Mother's overwhelming gentlenes and forethought? Rather, was it not Jesus again smoothing off difficulties and embarrisments?

I want to catch mailman. Please God you ll here from me shortly - suppliment to the above Your pathetic letter of a month ago has been on my mind ever since, as your vocation, has been increasingly in my prayers: seeing your intricate problems, your growing embarrassments, your so fearfully threatening dangers to temporal welfare as well as to the (spiritual) - and sadest of all your seemingly unsuspecting blindness, till thanks be to God! your very last, but redeeming paragraph

Dear Sister Mary Constance: God bless you and may He be your Stay , your Refuge and your divine Guide these days. I have hoped that by enc- couraging you as I have been trying to do these several months, that with the many prayers that I know are being offered for your guidance,- your conversion indeed - you might, by cooperating with God's holy grace, be fully convinced that your only salvation, for time as well as for eternity, is a generous and whole-hearted sacrifice of your --- your everything to God. Your desperate experiences these same months (hair-breadthly border- ering on fearful tragedy), -- experiences -- inthemselves and in reality extraordinary manifestations of God's mercy to you Sister Mary Constance, -- which ought surely to help convince you that such is about the only con- clusion for you to come to. While I have still more than hope that during these fearful experiences, you have not strayed mortal-sinfully from your Rule; nevertheless I believe on the other hand that, had you been really faith- ful to your vows and absolutely turned down the promises and the allure- ments of the world, the flesh and the devil as you should have done (two years ago), God would have promoted you before this to an incalculably more intimate and happy confidence and espousals with the divien Lover of Souls - to something vastly surpassing your highest ideal. You have lost out fearfully Sister: but your mistake is not irrepar- able. By the mercy of God and your humble and grateful cooperation therewith, you can, not-only regain your former standing in the Hearts of Jesus and Mary; but like St. Paul who from even a zealot persecutor of the Church became an all-surpassing Apotstle, Vessel of election, you too can -- and out of humble gratitude ought to -- become outstanding on the side of Truth and justice in the already-raging warfare against Antichrist and atheism. Your mistake of seeking solace and peace from other sources than in the Cross and the Crucified, and innumerable lesser mistakes that in consequence have followed since have evidently disturbed and muddled your spiritual waters, to say the least and beclouded your vocational horizon. Otherwise you would hardly moralize with so many "ifs" and "whys" and we might say "half truths." .. Yes, love in itself is always beauti- ful, but when and inasmuch as even love becomes inordinate it loses that native beauty and like an immortal soul in sin, becomes hedious in the sight of God and Heven. Illegitimate love is always inordinate; not always visa versa. Here is an actual example of the latter: Just about twenty years agoa certain practical school-mam married and was blest with a family of six boys. Every thing was bright in the beginning and indeed promising till a while after the first baby came. The attitude of her Husband became indifferent and even cold. For several months she never suspected the source of this unnatural attitude. Never suspected, till she herself had lost much of her affection and respect for her Husband. Ah! It dawned on her and she rememberd, -- ashamed of herself -- She had been giving all attention to the baby and been practically mono- polizing its affections. That baby is now in its latter teens or early twentys but there still evident traces of an inordinate mother-love IN THAT whole family. She still writes us; still laments . but hopes.

V. Dear Sister Mary Constance: God bless you and yours this holy season -a Blessed Eastertide if not too late. I hope this finds you well and tasting at least something of that peace which the great triumph of the RisenSaviour ought to inspire and insure. I figured on reaching you two weeks ago/but you Easter-card on top of such an unwantedg silence sort o'checked my decision. I almost wondered if it were a reality or had I only dreamed that SSrs. M.C. and M.B. had been here. Not a single syllable of reference from any quarter as to such a conference; and this even though Sr. M. Now I am writing to ask your prayers for a party whom I have known and in a way admired for twenty years or more, whose long- distance lament of perpetual Good Friday reminded me yesterday of a more recent friend of ours whose cry/essentially the same 18 ago. I do hope that by this time the latter, becoming a little more acustomed

Your kind letter of Feb. 5 has been received. Rest assued that your intentions, and of those near and dear to you, shall be included in my prayers, and in the prayers of every member of the community here at St. Felix. May the Good Lord Bless you all, and give you His Peace. God be praised in all His Designs. Have Faith in Him Who Loves us so much.

God bless you these days of unrest and suspense - you and yours. I have read your pathetic letter and do surely sympathize with you and your dear ones. I hope that the good God may manifest something of His merciful designs in favoring you with such a peculiar cross; for indeed, from sacred history the truth of the old saying - of St. Paul (? ): "Whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth", is most manifest. We've had several cases similar to yours and some of them alto- gether more tragic and hopeless - turn out to have been indeed real blessings in disguise. A single example: It must be ten or more years ago that a certain modest lady, having waited close to an hour, till all else had gone, introduced herself: " ... I's not Catholic, but I would like to get a bessin too. I's always had head-aches". Her accent rather than her color indicated something of her particu- lar origin. About three hours later a well featured but very dark visitor of the same name and identical accent asked for a rosary. I told him of his namesake who had been in about Il a.m. "That's my Wife". She had come home without any headache. Glory be to God! They had been praying for a family for thirteen years and were naturally discouraged or becoming so. They believed in Christianity but had never been baptized. ... It is next to "Unbelievable", what diffi- culties they met with and, by God's grace overcame, before being re- ceived into the Church, and even for months afterwards. All Hell just seemed determined to shake them from their purpose. We make it a point to stress the importance of making sacrifice in recognition of a favor received - having started out with an under- standing, at least to that effect. For Catholics, e.g., more fre- quent holy Communion if favor is granted and preferable, by all means to start at once - to "get ahead of the Good God in generosity" if possible. For non-catholics, that they be earnest in looking into something of the claims of the Church; or something of the relation- ship - dependence of the denominations on the Mother-Church, etc and working accordingly. .... I almost forgot to tell you that having left Detroit the convert darkies returned after plus three years - three of them instead of two. The good God had blessed them with a decidedly promising young- ster, the picture of his appreciative Daddy. .... I hope that may offer you an example from which to draw a practical lesson. - one case in thousands. Thanks be to God.

God bless you Frater Don Bosco. I hope this find thingsmore promising with you and yours than seemed to be when you wrote me last week. The intentions you wrote about have been in my mind pretty much ever since reading your letter; and I hope in my poor prayers. .... No, I had not heard of your steping out of the Clericat. I was sorroy ofcourse and disapointed; but do hope that the Holy Ghost - the divine Spirit guided you and that in the end it will turn to have been to your advantage and to the glory of God. Glad at all events, that the trouble was nothing more than physical; for even from the clean sports' columns like in the lives of the saints, we find innumerable examples where such difficulties only heightened apprediation for the hoped-for ideal and Goal. One of the great advantages of a study of the lives of the saints, is the supernatural courage that such studying tends so positively to foster. And at the same time appreciation for one's vocation; - appreciation - the natural foundation of gratitude which, in its turn, - "Gratitude, the very first and surest indication of intelli- gence." Hence the poet's happy dictum: "The lives of all great men remind us that we can make our lives sublime. "And, parting leave behind us worthy footsteps in the sans of time" . footprints Pope Pius XII; peerless and outstanding champion To-day of dogma, of morality, of peace among men and nations; stresses this virtue as man's first and gravest duty. Lives of saints? ... In 1909 I had completely lost the hearing in my left ear and the same condition was rapidly threatening the other side. I had returned a certain Thursday-evening from the specialist with a throbb- ing ear-ache after a very painful treatment and very delicate and dangerous propositions. Five years before that, I had read the life of Sister Therese Martin, till then seemingly quite unknown, and had greatly profited thereby; happy in the communion of saints as I felt, on having met another heavenly little friend. I had felt from thefirst reading that she would be canonized. Well, in my anxiety that night I made a "mental proposition" to her that if she would help to save my hearing I'd read her life again. I was even then confident that she could help me and that being already in Heaven, she would. John Martin - Frater Don Bosco, o. f.m. cap. (at least in spirit and hope, I trust) With no further trouble that night I slept well, and next morning at the first douche of water on my face, there was like a bubble broke in my bad ear and I thought: "Thank God! My drum is not broken". Be- fore 24 hours my hearing was perfect; and, what is further notable, I've had practically no trouble with my hearing ever since. Thanks be to God and His little spouse, now Saint Therese "The Little Flower. I have read her book fifteen times since thet and have had at least that many favors. The above will give you an idea of how I would advise you if you still hope for a vocation. Praying for vocation, if not a poitive vo- cation in itself, is surely an essential and outstanding feature in the character of every ideal Christian as well as in every practical missionary. Think it over, Encourage, foster vocations. Wherever we may be or whatever our state in life, we may in many ways become in- struments of the Holy Spirit by praying for and promoting vocations. Now, as to your "big problem"; as well as the minor interests to which you refer. I think you ought to be able to find a practical solu- tion in the above, as primarily intended for your own personal guidance. I am inclined to congratulate you on your place of imployment, Mt Olivet Cemetery; and on your privileged connection with the boys of Holy Name Parish. It was a privilege of mine to be assistant in that dear parish twenty-five years ago and chaplain at the - then - comparatively new but leading cemetery.

God bless you I surely do sympathize with you in your manifold troubles. However Saint Paul assures us, for our encouragement no doubt and for our consolation; "Whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth." have been long since convinced of the inspiration of this saying. · I The fact that Almighty God has permitted so many and such trials and crosses to come your way, till in a way you are forced to seek help where otherwise you would hardly ever dream of turning, indicates to me that the Good God must love you specially. I would wish I might express something of the peace that I hope will come to you as a direct result of your bravely humbling yourself just to appeal as you have done. God bless you for such effort. After all, I am sure that such reluctence on your part was nothing less than a temptation of the enemy of our souls, to divert you from the path to peace you thereby took, - the path to that peace of which the unbelieving world has hardly any conception; therefore, as Saint Paul says simply: " ... which the world can not give. ... which surpasseth all understanding" . As to your not being Catholic: You are probably more so than you imaginge, - if you only just knew what Catholicity is. I am confident that you will agree with me when I claim that, whatever we may call our- selves, - you or I, or anyone else, - we are Christians only in asmuch as we believe in Jesus Christ and keep His word, His Commandments. There can be but on Christianity, for there is only one Jesus Christ. Moreover, if we define religion as a science - and who can doubt, if properly studied, that it is the greatest of all sciences, - then there can be but one religion; only one such science. Truly scientific and educated peoples have in all ages understood "the Science of the Saints" to refer to religion, i e, to the relationship between Almighty God and His rational creatures.

Here's an envelope which I thing I must have addressed to you early in August, wanting to thank you for your kind favor received some- time befor that; so because I neglected to do that even last Monday when you were here, I'll at least acknowledge same favor. Fr. Gabriel came down Thursday and is conducting the 40 hours Devotion in S S. Peter and Paul Church - our Parish. Everything seems quiet and satisfactory. Deo Gratias. Pray for the multiplication of vocations and for the conversions of poor sinners. God help us. . .. That we be appreciative and make at least some progress towards real gratitude.

You and yours this beautiful feast and holy season. I do hope that you keep well; glad of course that your dear Parents and the others seem to hold out as years ago when I use to helpout at Saint Paul's. How imperceptibly time does fly! I certainly wish you success with your plans relative to taking-over that long-since dwarffed and recently orphaned episcopelian church of St. Peter. May the good God bless at once your confidence in the Committee in charge and their unbiased and -- in the face of present internat- ional atheism / -- reasonable judgement and prudent generosity. In the face of international atheism? Yes. And this should be stressed in dealing with any and every such committee. If the members thereof are able to think for themselves, as surely their honorable responsabilities presupose they are, at least in this instance, then they ought / realize that, whereas; the faith of perhaps the great majority of men these days having become weak- ened, hope and charity, its necessary accompaniments have likewise waned. In consequence, religion, the great science of faith, hope and charity, -- the science of our happy dependence on God and our neighbor is refused recognition even by "educators", God is being ousted from our systems of education and, as a just judgement from Heaven on humanity's apathy atheism -- "the climax of intellectual insanity and of moral depravity -- is marshaling its diabolical forces, ready at the first opportunity "to take over" in place of God and religion. We need only to look across into red, communistic Russia to see some of the temporal . . s.

I do hope you all keep well and that this finds you in hope- ful outlook. After all the present is so passing and so quickly gone that in the sight of Heaven it must appear nothing more than momentary. Many thanks for your kind remembrance of January 15th under such "prorsus" unwanted circumstances. Also that of the day-before yesterday. May the dear Lord Himself be your Reward. I am applying this latter as an enrollment in the Seraphic Mass Association, of the Holy Souls inPurgatory; -- especially the deceased of St. Paul's little Maltese Parish on 4th Street as also the deceased and living- benefactors / to whom we are appealing these days for prayers and for material assistance. Among these latter, as I suggested several weeks back I have had in mind the model and saintly Monsignor Connolly and his eminent Brother the Judge, both of whose early deaths Detroit so much lamented. I had the privilege of meeting the former for sev- eral years and of helping-out in the church that / his proposition and what few know about, his prophecy of a new Cath.

It is getting a little late for Easter greetings but neverthe- less I do wish you a blessed Eastertide; hoping that something worth while may come your way before Holy Trinity Sunday to brighten your path and ligten your horizon, that may offer you and your dear Mal- tese People at least a sigh of relief. This most especially for your poorly, dear old Parents. But dear Father Cefai: as your one-time privileged assistant I am going to kinda beg leave to scold the Pastor, lest he lose sight of or forget -- as we are naturally so inclined to forget -- the primary rule and purpose of spiritual progress, in every thing from common sense to the very climax of highest asceticism; viz, "Charity begins at home." It is quite probable that Fr. M. Z. feelshe's doing just that, in his solicitude for his people and his parish. In a way he is. But laudable and all as is such sol- icitude (and even in laudable: "No quid nemis") it is never rightly -ordered charity for me to forget that the primary purpose of my creation and of my existence as a rational creature, Is to recog- nize and to know, to appreciate and to love -- with an intelligent, personal grateful love -- God my Creator, my Redeemer, my Sanctifier. Zeal and solicitude for others is certainly praisworthy and pleasing to Almighty God and edifying to the Church and to all observant men. Such is the vocation of, not only the Priest and the Pastor to whom it specially refers; but if, "Gratitude for favors received is the very first and surest indication of intelligence", then it applies also to every Christian and indeed to every rational creature; viz, in the spiritual world especially, to gain souls for God; which means too for their own hope, happiness, glory.
Mrs. Philomena Discenna, for speedy sight improvement, God willing - - Special

I hope you are well and that by this time things have brightened in regard to your little Mary. I put your letter aside - having noted your favor, for which many thanks, a special Mass at the time - and then lost track of it, I wanted to answer it personally. I surely sympathize with you and your family. We have had quite a few cases similar to little Mary's, the majority of which, thanks be to God, have come through astonishingly well. They sometimes seem miraculous. Glory be to God.
Ven. Sister Mary Leoncia O.S.F. for special Intent., God willing and for His holy guidance - emergency special "And the Lord said to me: for thee ". My grace is sufficient

- forpatient progress in virtue - Why not offer our temptations themselves to God - for perseverance in purity, etc of inexperience, youth, etc .... fostering confidence in God, the very soul of prayer. Bles'd be God in all His designs.

God bless you this glorious Feast and Easter Season, you and yours. May the divine Prince of Peace Himself breathe His Spirit of good will and harmoneous enlightenment on all and each of those unselfishly interested in Mercy-Hall activty, -- present, past, future. Glory be to God; what a record is not the story of that fair flower of Christian activity; and of practical Catholic action! -- a record of struggles sometimes bordering on the desperate, and of escapes, hair-splittingly close to disaster; struggles with and escapes from financial difficulties and bankruptcy, from envy and suspicion, from misunderstanding, calumny, etc. And some of all this in a way, before the idea of Mercy-Hall was fully conceived or its Heaven-sent "blue-prints" unfolded. -- as it was unfolded in that "miraculously" developed and unfading blooming slip of im- mortal from your Girl-Friend, Miss Daly's grave -- ) and it was de- finitely and urgently counseled: "Get started; if necessary, with a single patient in some old atic. God who loves tiny beginnings, will know as He always does know, how and when to provide develop- ment." Ah! Blue prints? Struggles? Escapes? Crisis after crises? Thank God for them all. How wonderful with the inestimable gift of faith, whereby, with our cooperation, all and each such trial turn to have been blessings in disguise. Thank God too even for the present -- seemingly the supreme -- crisis. If "The memory of past difficulties is pleasant." as an old Latin proverb has it and if according to Saint Paul and every teacher of true asceticism: behoves us, by many tribulations to enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.", why worry about struggles, etc, -- past or to come? Why not rather focus all attention on thanking God for having seen us safely thus far notwithstanding our many, many, innum- erable weaknesses and sins !!! ? Let us go a step further and thank God ahead of time for every trial and cross He may see fit to permit our meeting in this "vale of tears" -- that, in His mercy and wisdom He so often sweetens into tears of joy? We do well it seems to me, to in- clude in this ascetic idea -- this exercise of confidence, the trials and probable struggles of the happy death awaiting us, notwithstanding whatever adversities in His infinite wisdom and loving mercy He may see fit to permit. I hope you still pray to Miss Daly, even while praying for her she has been praying for you all these years. - I believe that - Naturally, therfore, she would be disapointed as at a want of appreciation of her Girl- Friend down here on earth if you should fail in this; because too, as a certain sister for whom St. Theresa of Avilla had prayed long and earnestly, - on its way to Heaven- assured her " . . . Pray for you Mother Terese! Ah! Mother: . for there is no place for ingratitude in Heaven." If you honestly humble yourself, dear Miss Gibson, -- and this applies to each and every one of us - your victory will be certain. In other words, in as much as any of us can immitate our Blessed Mother Mary, Mother of God, who the more she was hon- ored, somuch more did she humble herself. Ah! Because next Jesus Himself the supreme, the divine Model, she too was indeed: "Meek and humble of heart." Let us not blame anyone for suspecting or persecuting us, as at first we are naturally inclined to do. On the contrary if we have a little patience and pray for them instead, thus we will surely be following the diving counsel and in the end have the consolation of converting them and of gain- ing our own Triumph.

Ah! the aurora of Salvation's Day. Next to Jesus Himself and always with Him may she be ever our refuge and our stay during this pilgrimage on earth, in reality so very short at the longest and still, at times so seemingly long. Indeed I say again God bless you, and May Jesus the true Light breath His own Spirit of good will and of harmoneous anlightenment on each and all of those unselfishly interested in Mercy-Hall activity, - present, past, future. This has been my prayer for you and for them. Glory be to God! What a record is not the story of that fair flower? -- a record indeed of genuine, Christian activity and of really practical Catholic Action; a record of ups and downs; a record of struggles, bordering on the desperate and of escapes hair-splittingly close to disaster: struggles with and escapes from financial difficulties and bankruptcy, from suspicion and criticism (sometimes honest and well meant), and from envy and ambitions intriguing and consequent misrepresent- ation and calumny, etc. -- and in a way some of all this, before the idea of Mercy Hall was fully conceived or its "Heaven-sent blueprints" unfolded and it was at once stressed: "Get started. . if necessary with a single patient in some old attic." intimating at least in effect: "God who loves tiny begin- nings will know -- as He always does know best - how and when to provide developments". "Heaven-sent blue-prints"? Indeed! For that "miracilously- developed", unfadingly blooming, little slip from the girl-friend's grave was nothing less than just that, Heaven, sent blueprint. In a way it was more; for who with a spark of supernatural faith in God, could even behold that phonimally-blooming little slip without a decided heightening of his faith and confidence in the super- natural and in the divine providence of Heaven? In His merciful, unfathomable wisdom and goodness, Almighty God left that little relic with you as long as you needed it for just that kind of inspiration. And when it had served its purpose and Mercy Hall was well started, He lifted it away from you, (how, is quite secondary. ) lest curiosity and consequent want of appre- ciation and of reverence mar the delicacy and the supernatural fragrance of that -- ? -- His own little blue-print? . · · · Aye! Glory be to God and blessed be His holy Name in all His designs! and in these designs; not merely including, but positively stressing just the knocks and the humiliations we meet with and the crisis after crisis He sometimes permits even while by His grace He fortifies us to profit by them all more than by anything else, save by the actual reception of the very Sacraments themselves.

God bless you Miss Loretta Mry Gibson God bless you and yours these unsettled days - glorious days, however as always, ... for men who for men of good will. can humbly appreciate what enables them - us poor sinners - to glory in actually holding a place of trust Even near - at least in sight of - the General - our crucified Jesus. I am sending you a copy of the, "Prayer for Peace," of which you have likely known away ahead of me. I heard it first, only after coming to St. Bonaventures last January. . . It strck me at once as from a saddened heart. My own heart filled up, at my first official praying thereof.
We shall be pleased to see you as proposed, or at your convenience. not be disapointed. We hope of course that you may

I am certainly pleased to see your hope and confidence in the mercy and gracious wisdom of Almighty God in regard to your little Maurice. I had a very dear and amiale brother of that name Maurice Joachim Casey. He was very talented and from earliest childhood seemed to dream of being a priest. When 16 in his 3rd year in the seminary his health failed and he came home - a family disapoint- ment. However, he worked generously in promoting vocations and was extremely pleased to others take his place - especially our 2nd youngest of ten brothers - just now back from the missions in the Philippines with his mission Headquarters in St. Paul, Minn. - Rt. Rev. E'd F. Casey. - Well after 20 years roving when I was ordained and he served at my first Holy Mass, he decided to " ... try it again and after seven years further study was ordained - at 43 instead of 23. Thanks be to God a billion. So we will hope an for something of a miracle for little Mau- rice. I am going to pray my deceased Rev. Brother Maurice - and especially our Father Stephen Eckert - whose relic I am herewith inclosing to pray for him and if it please God that he be spared - and have a vocation. For Father Stephen especially we a hoping for miracles so as to promote his Cause of beatification first and then his canonization.

God bless you Rev. Dear Mother Mary Hilda. May He be favorable to you and to all your benefactors - most especially those in Beech Grove Hospital and bring them more and more to realize and to appreciate the privilege of harboring a religious "so tempted and tried in the humilia- tions of extraneous "warfare in the world. July 21st. Dear Mother Hilda. God help us! You see I did not get far a week ago. I do hope you keep up courage and persevere these trying times, - glorious times if by God's grace we persvere in "keeping the faith: and, God willing, having the privilege of finally giving our life its defense. For surely "civilization" has been rapidly losing its one- time rational balance. Thank God however, there are still members of society - of the human-race - who like the seers of old and the prophets and apostles keep faith with God our divine Creator and Preserver; but, Alas! for modern society! civilization! humanity! If ever the words of Isias, have been applicable to a people or a generation of nations, they are surely appropriate today in reference to the majority of our modern "scientests", "educators", "statesmen", "Governments": "With desolation is all the world made desolate, because there is none that thinketh in their hearts." "Scientests" that refuse to recognize as a science, the most privi- leged and most fortunate relationship and dependence of the rational creacheron the divine Creator and Preserver of the Universe! "Scientests" and "educators", etc, that fail to see or refuse to recognize "general principals the truth of which can be plainly perceived by the light of reason"; as Pope Leo XIII, in his Encyclical on the Holy Eucharist de- clares, - giving - "for instance", the most important, all-outstanding principal whereon rests to humanity the sanctity and the soul of the Ten Commandments of God and the authority of all legitimate, divine authority; - "for instance, that the dominion of God our Creator and Preserver over all men, whether in their private or in their public life, is supreme and absolute; that our whole being and all that we possess, whether individually or as members of society, comes from the divine bounty; that we on our part are bound to show to God, as our Lord, the highest reverence, and, as He is our greatest benefactor, the deepest gratitude."

God Bless you Mother Mary Hilda this happy feast day of most priviliged Grand-Mother dear St. Ann. I have started to write you several times these last more than six months, and whatever the trouble, I can hardly excuse myself for such negligence in failing to express my appreciation for your kind remembrances and to say thank you, as I want to do now at least, with a thousand times God bless you. I do hope that you keep up in health and courage, persevering in keeping the Faith and helping Jesus our Savior in the saving of poor sinner's souls - including our own of course, charity beginning at home. God help us! How little we appreciate our privilige of being given opportunity after opportunity of suffering in diverse ways and of offer- ing all in union with and for the intentions of the Sacred Heart of Jesus! I have been reading: "The Way of Divine Love; or The Message of the Sacred Heart to the World", as jotted down and noted by a most privi- leged contemporary of our own, the little, kitchen-lay-sister Josefa Menendeth, born in 1890 and called to Heaven December 29, 1923. - all in strict though gentlest obedience to Jesus and her superiors. What sufferings of soul and body she went through - what agonies she learned to welcome! - for the sake of helping Jesus to rescue straying souls! Glory be to God! Would that we might be convinced - that we might real- ize - in the time of temptation, of trial and struggle, and when the clouds seem most threatening that just then it is that Our Dear Lord in nearest and that just then too we ought to offer all to Jesus - turning to Him with the holy fear at once and the confidence of the Apostles :" Lord we perish! - Save us! " As still a child at home struggling to support herpoor parents, whose modest means had become exhausted through failing health and un- forseen family expenses, including the early death of her father, Josepha had learned many a practical lesson in patience, resignation, confidence in God; - humility permeatingall, supporting every step toward the heights of Calvary and confidence in Heaven.

Sept. 17, 1951 - God bless you Rev. Mother Mary Hilda. I hope this finds you - still on the way of the cross, the best school wherein to learn appreciation for and love of Jesus Cricified divine lover of souls. Our friend Miss B. from Decatur was here this P. M. with her two sisters, niece-in-law and little girl, - pleasantly surprised on hearing of your visit, etc. Afterwards I just came across the above started letter which I had pulled out of the machine about a month ago to get something off that seemed more immediately urgent. So, hoping that it is not too late or too inopportune I'm sendingit just as it is. However, as a sort of key to the letter from Miss Gibson which I gave you Sunday, I am going to try to get a copy for you of the letter she wrote me a week or so before the trial when things seemed so very threatening. I am sure you will enjoy it - as heightening the interest and beauty of the one that followed. obvious lesson it ought to stress, as seems to me, is the old addage or An motto: "Per aspera ad astera", - "Through trials to triumph": or straight prose as St. Paul gives it: "It behooves by many tribulations, to enter into the Kingdom of Heaven." Bles'd be God again in all His designs - not only including them simply - but stressing the trials, the humiliations, crosses, disappoint- ments, etc. whereby, next to the reception of the holy Sacraments in impor- tance, it would seem divinely providential that those whose motto ought to be: "ALWAYS EXCELSIOR", be purified from self conceit, so natural to origin- ally tainted human reason, and introduced gradually into the light and in- timacy of confidence with the Divine.
God bless little Marty O'Hara and speed his health back to normality -- God willing -

I hope you are well and that things are coming favorably for you. I am sure my failure to acknowledge your appreciated favor of December 6th last, must have been deeply disapointing. Please pardon! I can hardly explain further than that, wish- ing to thank you personaly for such a favor, I put your brief letter aside and, some how or other it was simply "snowd under." However, I am sure God has blessed you just the same, and you have been included in our prayers as noted at the time. Besides this, I am going to offer my first - next - "Free Mass" for your intentions, your guidance, and welfare. Incidently we have the privilege of two such "free-Masse " each month.

Many thanks for your pathetic communication of June 20th, which I had to put aside at the time and which frankly, till I neared its conclusion, I was inclined to ignore. However, though the situation is not essen- tially changed, I feel bound to offer you something of encouragement for the "problems" of which you complain, viz, about God and about "science and religion". For "practical children of the Church" such problems are to a great extent solved at baptism; so that by the grace of that Sacrament the principles of the "triune virtue of Faith - Hope - Charity" are divinely infused into the soul whereby, from the very start it be- comes docilly inclined to believe; and to behold the Church and to confide in her with growing conviction as divinely founded and as infallibly guided in her capacity of mother and mistress of immortal souls - of human candidates for the life of eternal glory; of which St. Paul writes: "Bye hath not seen, ear hath not heard, nor hath it entered into the heart of man to conceive what things God has prepared for them that love Fim". But let us first lament your failure - which is not yours only but humanity's to which we both belong. Perhaps our sadest failure, notwith- standing our faculties for thinking and reasoning, notwithstanding our advanced steps in every phase of science and, (what ought to count most of all in the natural order of conclusion) notwithstanding uncounted ages of bitterest experience of men and angels, that ingratitude to God never pays. We have in great part failed to recognize as a science, the one, in the sight of heaven, greatest science of all times and of all places wherever pertains to rational creatures. We have failed to recognize as a science OUR MOST FORTUNATE RELATIONSHIP - absolute depen- dence on the Almighty, all merciful God, and together with that, our dependence on our neighbor.

Many thanks for your pathetic communication of June 20th. Because of the hundred and more letters before me that claim response I was about to make very short work of yours before I had read half of it. However, I put it aside. Today, though the situation is not improved, I feel I must give you a few words. If you were a faithful "child of the Church", you would escape the danger of many of those problems of which you lament, viz, problems about God, science and religion. I must be brief. First let me lament your failure - with your so-called science - you fail to recognize as a science, the greatest science itself of all times and of all places, viz, the science of our happy dependence as rational creatures, on God and our neighbor. That is RELIGIOS; the only science that in the end - amounts to more than the snap of one's finger. Like every other science, though there be a thousand systems (denominations) there can be but one such science. It might be defined also; "The science of saving our souls or simply: "the science of charity", whose primary purpose is to foster what is sometimes called "the triune virtue of faith-hope- charity". Because they are essentially one virtue, the positive contrast on first glance of "Atheism-despair-hate" of which your first two sentences seem so positively to lament, viz, someone's own agnosticism, hatred and consequent, worse than disturbance. I was going to say above, that practi- cal Catholics know without a doubt what to believe concerning the referred- to problems. Besides; the more anyone of good will knows about true religion viz, the system of divine and infallible religion - the infallible system of religion - established and founded by Jesus Christ and proclaimed by His Twelve Apostles - watering it with their blood in imitation of Jesus their divine Master; so much the clearer does the whole Christian system unfold before the eye of common sense, and of the highest reasoning, as well as in the light of divine faith - all true sources of science and all phases of true religion the crown and final purpose of all.

We all hope this finds you well - which, for one ex- periencing what you have been going through these several months, must mean that you are keeping up courage and by the grace of God continuing to foster confidence in His merciful wisdom and goodness - all the better of course if the physical condition, at least does non get worse, till we see a decided im- provement and final recovery, God willing. The purpose of this card, since I cannot finish the letter I wanted to send you, is primarily, to just reassure you that we are keeping you in mind and please God will not forget you in our prayers.

God bless you and yours these days of grace. For days of grace are these our days and days of God's great mercy to all men of good will, notwithstanding our lamentable want of appreciation and of gratitude for His inestimable graces and His uncountable favors. Days of grace too, notwithstanding the threatening avalanche of international red-atheism even now be- deviling millions of humanity more and more brazenly and presump- tuously aspiring on earliest opportunity, "to-take-over" for rel- igion. Nay - in places behind the "Iron Curtain", actually taking over and, instead of keeping highest promises, is doublly grind- ing its dupesinto abject slavery of body and soul: while at the same time it is going to the limit of its power in trying to play Hell with every decent subject who dare profess other than what tends to kill true religion and belief in the Supernatural. Atheism! God help us! "The social octupus-cancer of mind and spirit"! Atheism? The no-God-monster proposition, when philosophy and commonsense as well (as) revelation and faith in the Eternal -all- proclaim, "appreciation and grati- tude for favors received, the very first and surest indication of intelligence."? Atheism; the stifler of every phase of science that down the ages has fostered gratitude to parents and bene- factors as to God's representatives and that, instead of, "Hope, the very soul of happiness in this world", would inject the poi- sonous nightmare of eternal despair? Aye! Aye! God help us these days of God's grace and mercy, against the atheism of Anti- christ: -- atheism the unqualified climax atonce, of intellectual insanity, of moral degeneracy, of diabolical blasphemy and of et- ernal despair. God help us! Pardon me Dear Mr. O'Brien I hope this is not boring you, but it seems to me that, when we behold the general outlook in the material and materialistic world today and the inordinate tendency of thot-less humanity to worship this passing existence as though it were our final destiny and the only life worth striving for (unfinished draft.)

Many thanks for your appreciated favor of August 20ch which I just finished reading. I hope this finds you well and improving! For you, that means that by the grace of God you persevere in His holy grace and ser- ice -- resigned in all circumstances to His adorable wil1. Of course it is not wrong to pray for improve- ment of health, etc. But perhaps more meritorious to even offer ourselves to suffer something in union with our dear Lord's suffering and death for our holy Redemption -- remembering too that: "whom the Lord loveth He chastiseth. " Keep courage therefore and I hope that before long - God willing - you surprise the doctors and all concerned.

God bless you and yours. I do hope that you are well these days and that our dear Lord guide you always. For as years and decades pass we realize more and more clearly, with Holy Jobe that, "The life of man on earth is a warfare". Indeed a warfare it is that, notwithstanding the innumerable graces and safe-guards that surround us, is fraught with pitfalls and dangers at every turn. How can we ever appreciate as we ought, or be grateful for having from infancy been blessed with the supernatural certainty that the True Faith alon can inspire and insure? ! Deo gratias a billion. I have been wanting to write you these several weeks and especially since Sr. M.C. was down a couple weeks ago. I know you are interested in her welfare and that, like many of the rest of us, have been trying to help her find her bearings and the peace of soul she seems temporarly at least rather sadly to have lost sight of. However, I feel that if we can just keep our heads and, especially if she can only be induced to have patience and to humbly foster confidence in God; I am sure, as I have been trying to assure her right along, that Almighty God is permitting all this trouble of hers - seemingly a real "night of her soul", to come as a blessing in disguise - as a feature of her preparation "sine qua non", of her arriving at that peace the world knows nothing about; the peace of soul she once most probably dreamed of but, of which, for her vocational maturity she has been permitted seemingly to lost sight these years and sadly to have forgotten. True, she has made innumerable mistakes and stupid blunders. Who has not made them? Nevertheless and notwithstanding all such and even were they multiplied.

God bless you and yours. I hope this finds you well and that your dear Mother's health has improved since your short visit here to Saint Felix. Thanks be to God we are all well notwithstand- ing our prevalence of real "grip weather. Dear Monsignor Hickey: you will hardly be surprised if I tell your Right Reverence that for quite some time I've been want- ing to write you; and this concerning two problems, some details of which I am sure will be a relief to your Rt. Reverence - as the release, I feel will be to me. For whether a matter be trifling or tremdous the wisdom of Jesus' dictum must always hold: "Know the Truth and the Truth will make you free." The first problem concerns the origin of the Mercy Hall Cancer Hospital of Detroit. I probably should have given you the details long ago that I now finally propose to release - details - which few, if any other could offer, details which, together with the here inclosed letter, (as a sample), will change your view of said institution and with the grace of God, I trust may completely reverse the hitherto shown attitude toward the foundress by your Rt. Rev. Paternity. Ah! for your own joyous relief as well as her estremely tried fortitude. I beg pardon for such culpable hesita- tion. Glory be to God. Following are a few details. About twenty-five years back two young nurses came to Saint Bonaventure Monastery in Detroit seeking guidance in regard to starting a cancer-hospital. I enrolled them in the Seraphic Mass Association and promised to pray for them and their project. This repeated itself a number of times for two or more years; so that I was inclined to take them for a "sort of dreamers" (?) . . . Finally while Miss Gibson was sice in a Detroit hospital her girl-friend the other nurse - her "saintly friend" as she consi- dered, (a certain Miss Daily), died in New York. Just another knock for the girl-friend left to weep and to pray - - - of whom she was wont to speak as being a saint and on the help of whose prayers she still seems to have confidence. Having lingered at the Grave . . . Miss Gibson plucked a slip of an "immortal" (a little plant grow- ing on the grave), and simply put it in a little, round "vanity-box" perhaps two inches wide and a 1/2 of an inch deep, half saying to herself: "This will be my relique." Shortly afterwards she was packing her trunk to come West and without further ado, like tossed it into the trunk to take care of itself. Weeks afterwards she was looking for something else when the little "vanity-box" unexpectedly appeared. "O!", she thought, "Here is my relic!". Her emotion on finding it not only fresh and green but perfectly in bloom was un- speakably more than surprise. To me, when first I saw it and as of- ten as I saw it - which was quite occasionally for more than a year -- it was a "Blue-print from Heaven" and nothing less, of the insti- tution that she and Miss D. had been dreaming of and praying for . . . . "Get started ", came to my lips the first thing following my astonishment. "Get started if necessary with a single patient in some old atic. and God Who loves tiny beginnings will know, as He always does know best, how and when to provide development." She did not have to start in such extremes. Her said little "miracullous blue-print" would seem to have carried her successfully at every turn; for she carried it with her everywhere and never hesitated to show it where appreciation for the supernatural might be expected. All this till Mercy Hall was well established and to stay. . . Aye! "A really Catholic Hospital, with everything in detail and up to date . What a contrast after three years when Chapel and Altar were gone and no visits more to Jesus or reception of the Sac- taments! Still Miss G. was a Catholic. Still her Catholic pictures and statues were in the corredors and parlors. Stell, though she wore no "habit" she was keeping up reception of the Sacrament her- self. She had aged more than three years. Less than a quarter of an hour's visit was sufficiently revealent. Dr. Mcclellan was my hoste and chauffeur, and he had an operation scheduled that morning and we necessarily had to be brief. One could only wonder as to the cause or the purpose of it all. . . . . But: "Who hath known the mind of the Lord? Or who hath been his counsellor? ! ! As much as I remember I had not seen either of them for some months. They had always come together. Now Miss Gibson comes alone with such unwanted tidings. More remarkble still however, though of a happier color is her story of a phenomena in connection therewith and which bring us nearer to our purpose. our problem. After her own recovery she - Miss G. - had taken a trip to New York, visiting friends and relatives as I understood - her own and those of Miss Daly - the deceased nurse-friend and nat- urally the latters place of burial. This visit or visiting lasted for some days (five to be exact, as she tells me now). At all events, she brought back with a slip or sprig from a little "im- mortal" already growing on the stell fresh grave where she had lingered these days and prayed and fostered supernatural hope. She had placed, the tiny sprig in a common envelope and when about / return / Detroit had placed it with some letters, etc, in her hand-bag. Some time afterwards, on opening the envelope she had been astonished at finding the slip, not only not withered and dried, not only fresh and green but actually having grown and in perfect bloom . . . . It is easy to speculate on the more than surprise that such a greeting offered the beholder . . . . That, for just now however, must be secondary. Suffice to say that her whole attitude was beaming. Her every move corroborated convic- tion. Spontaneously opening a small "vanity-box" to which her "relic" had been transfered, she like triumphantly displayed her "supernatural immortal." To me it was a marvel. To me it was a "blue-print" of what the nurses these late years had been dream- ing about. - - a sort of mystical fore-shadowing of how their yearnings to do something worthwhile for God and humanity were to be realized and their institution was to flourish, viz. quiet and unassuming, hidden-like from the unappreciative.

I surely congratulate you the privileged step you had on the 49th anniversary of my first Holy Mass, Feast of St. Ignatius. Glory be to God! I should surely like to have been there. I am sure Father Edward will be pleased to hear of your progress. But its only when we shall actually reached Heaven that we'll be in contition to ap- preciate the real meaning of heavenly joys. Because as St. Paul assures in his letter to the Romans: "Eye hath not seen, Ear hath not heard, nor hath it entered into the heart of man to conceive what God hath prepared for them that love Him." .something like Fr. E'd concludes one of his poems; his "Valley of Plains" ( in Montana) "O God! What the glory of Heaven must be! when its feeble Reflection on Mountain and lea, Enrobes the dull clay in a beauty sublime! -- Eternity's breath -- on the ashes of time." P.S. An old adage : "Finis Coronet Opus" "The end crowns the work."

I made a copy of it and am sending you the original. I must memor- ize it. How mercifully provident is not the good God in making us His creatures dependent - next to Himself! - on one another! Hence the beautiful definition of the greatest science of all times and of all places: "The science of our happy dependence on God and our neighbor -- Religion! Ah! - . Ah ! Glory be to God! how natural and how easy to understan; if we remember that we are all individually our own first neighber! Best wishes and God's blessing to the Chaplows. It would be nice if you and Mr. Birxhill could come down with them. . "As a Rational Creature. God made me to know Him. O! what a bless'd aim! To love Him and serve Him sure rests in the: - It's Heaven - Begun for the grateful on Earth: (to know God) To treasure aright! ? - Highest Heaven its worth.

We surely sympathise with you and your family under your peculiar affliction. Would it be possible that some of your folks have not been going to he holy Sacraments as tey should or not atall? Some years ago in Detroit a young girl - 19 - was brought to our front-door curb-stone who had been sneezing for five days. She was already unconscious and the doctors had given her only 24 hours further to live if remedy failed. I asked them about their Easter Dduty. The children had been going regularly but the mother had not been to confession for five years and the Father since he came from Europe They came back the next thirty years before. morning reporting: " ... Still sneezing and still weaker." We enrolled her a second time in the Ser. Mass Association and the parents promissed they would make their confession this P.M.

God bless you Patrick Gainer. Many thanks for your favor of several weeks ago. Please pardon delay. I pray for your good will and for God's holy guidance in regard to the important step you have been considering. I am sure that if you go to the holy sacraments frequently and earnestly, God will not let you go astray.
