I think when the weather settles a little more it would be a nice trip down here - though it must be further than Detroit ....

I am glad to know that your Mother feels well enough and is looking forward to making the little trip down to our Monastery here just up over the hill from Huntington. I think an experienced driver ought to be able to make the trip easily enough in five or six hours. It is only about 125 miles from Chicago, and it ought not be difficult to cut off fifty of that by a straighter route, e.g. via South Bend, Elkart or Coldwater. This last might be out of your way but in case there is a direct highway from the North I could guide you pretty well from that point. The Fathers of Detroit and Huntington usually go that way when driving. Its just 100 miles out of Detroit. That would be to far Eastward for you. Well we'll just pray the dear Lord to be your Guide - Maybe as He was to the young Tobias, through St. Raphael. P.S. Coldwater is 70 miles from Fort Wayne - I think its 17 (Hi-way) out of Coldwater - there from FrWay 30 miles S.West #24.
Foster Confidence in God - courage reenforced by the divine "whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth."

I wanted to call you Monday evening. But the first thing I knew it was so late that I was ashamed to call and the follow- ing ev. you were up to George's. I sure was pleased the your Mother so evidently enjoyed the trip and the little visit. I went out a couple of times after dark that night to find it not dark at all but beautiful moon-light. I was confident that you were having a pleasant moon-light return to Muskegon. Thanks be to God. ... . I was not surprized that you all liked the photo It always brings back to my mind a really beautiful and touch- celebration; and thanks be to God again the first half of the 16 to cross the border into eternity, have gone beautifully, in peace. Now Miss Doris: I would sure appreciate it if you would send that photo to Father M. Joachim Casey (my Brother to whom it belongs as I think I told you. Please God I'll let you know about the Chapter as soon as we learn the results, etc.

As requested I have made the enrollmens - of Grace and Thom also. And have just noted Grace's request, received yesterday. Many thanks for your kindness in sending the large family - photo to my Rev. Brother M.E.J. I am sure he will appreciate it.
God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your practical "Loose leafs" just arrived this morning in perfect condition. I hope to remember you someway in prayer as often as I shal use it.
Many thanks again for your favor of Nov. 11th. I am here -- I expect - till next Tuesday; possibly a few days longer. Am trying to reduce my unexamined letters, over fifty.

Hope this finds you all well. Was a little disapointed the other night. I hoped to get in touch with you all. Well, when I heard Grandma's voice I thought that would suffice and I told the operator "OK." I want to thank Grace too and George - and all the others for their favors not always acknowledged. I hope you all have a Joyful Christmas in the peace of the Lord. Also I ask you all to continue a little prayer for this poor sinner once in a while.
Just a word to ask you in case you send me anything .... please do not have it elaborate - just something I'll not be ashamed to use and may remember the donor in using. P1.

God bless you and yours. I hope things are brightening and that Grace is slowing down a little with her hustling, etc, and feeling better. No doubt I am giving you a little surprise by returning the enclosed check. I hope it will only mean just a little smile, and when you read the following explanation, I think that is about all it will cost you. You've no doubt long since forgotten about your having waited for its return and made up for it before this by other proofs of generosity. However, I want to thank you just the same as I would have wished to do had I received it in Seattle, with your very timely greetings and wishes. We surely did have touching celebration and a pleasant family re-union. Thanks be to God. Here is what my "baby sister" says relative to the cheque. "Dear Father Solanus -- We are moving next week to another house, and while cleaning out his desk, Pat ran across the inclosed enve- lope. Thinking it might be an ad, Pat opened it, and so we are sending it on to you. How it came to be put away in Dad's desk, I do not know but it could easily have happened, so many were in and out at the time of John's First Solemn Mass." So that ex- plains my silence from Seattle coming three years ago. And this releases you of all obligations pertaining to the checque, -- save a smile and just a little, silent prayer. Thanking you again for your many proofs of kindness and gen- erosity, and wishing God's blessing to all and each of the Panyard Family and their many friends, I beg to remain,

Many thanks for your generous supply of my favorite general remedy, Ben Gay -- Baume Bengue. The same ought to hold me a long time, now that my Eczema is pretty well cleared up. I hope this finds you all well and well dis- posed for special graces these blessed days. -- and a Joy- ful Easter tide.

God bless you Miss Doris Panyard. Many thank for your king favor of May 4th, duly Rec'd and noted. We'll pray for that. Rev. Father and will hope something bigger and better may follow the $1000.00 turkey dinner. Glad to hear of Grace's favorable surprise. Thanks be to God for every blessing.

Tomorrow is the Vigil of the glorious Assumption of Mary our B1. Mother. Thank God! How privileged we are in being able to say so much! How little we can possibly appreciate her in this poor exile from Heaven !. You asked me sometime back about what Rae should do with certain money given him for promoting the "Mystical City." ..... Until about a year ago I had hoped that he would eventually be the publisher. However; when Jerry called me from Notre Dame and I was tempted to ask to speak to his Father - who I knew was there waiting to speak to me - I changed my view. It came to me immediately after that something like as follows: "God chooses the weak things of the world .... to do His greatest works. ." What Humiliations did not V.M.M. of Agreda meet before succeeding in writing the out standing master- piece the 2nd time!" It became clear that little K.S. wished to help L.W. Bern'kn. Only in conjunction with L.W.B. it seems to me for the present may one hope to help . Only in harmony and in conjunction with L.B. may anyone hope to get any where. I ought to rewrite this but you will understand ... I am sure. . . ·

God bless you Doris Panyard. I hope this finds you well and that things are brightening up by this time. I wrote you about a week ago, hoping to reach you next day after George phoned, but spoiled the card and this is the late result. I received a wire this Morning from my Rev. Brother Edward that our other Rev. brother, Father Maurice Joachim, died this Morning at 6 o'clock. R.I.P. Please pray for the repose of his dear Soul. Thanks be to God he was well pre- pared - over 81 years of a warfare - and probably one thousand of pitched battles. last.

God bless you and all yours: Miss Panyard, almost time ... I am trying to get this off today. Many thanks for your kind favor Rec'd yesterday. Please God I'll remember you at least as often as I use same.

I hope this finds you all well with hopeful outlook. I want to thank you for your kindness recently received - the writing materials, etc and especially the very nice little "Storm of St. Therese's Glory". I surely find it very interest- ing. This favor came Monday - day before-yesterday. Many thanks too for the beautiful boquet just came in this afternoon. God bless you. May He speed up your plans and perfect undertakings!

I hope this finds you all well and that things have been going at least not too bad. I want to thank you for Wartime Correspondence between Pres. Roos'vlt and Pope Pius XII ... It is quite a masterpiece of compilation of masterpieces of master-minds on basic principles and parallel lines in Church and State in time of crisis pulling in perfect harmony together. It could be well placed in the hands of every 8th grader as well as every high- school and college student. Its tripple introduction ought to insure it an immense circulation. Of course expression of any suspicion of communistic influence in hurrying Roosevelt out of the picture would be out of question in such a work. But if his ideals as expressed in these letters were known, it is certain that the communists would not hesitate at such a liquidation as many seem to suspect Roosevelt's to have been ..... At all events, I thank you again and may the Lord guide you and all of us. Will try to call (Saturday or) Sunday after 7 P.M .- Det. T.

God bless you and yours. Y' asked some time ago for the publishers of that War time correspondence between Pres. Roose- velt and Pope Pius XII. It is the MacMillan Company, New York. It is fine work. Its "tripple introduction" ought to insure it a wide circulation .... again, Many thanks.

Many thanks for your generous favor received yesterday just after our "long distance". I am trying to get this off To-day and its time the collecter were here so pardon haste. God's blessing to all the works and undertakings of the Panyard Setup.

God bless you Grace and many thanks for your favor. I've mis- laid your letter just for the moment; but before neglecting it further and then forgetting I am just sending this card that Br. Rufin started. Please give "Best Regards" to George and and to Mother especially and to Doris. I hope these latter will enjoy their trip to Wisconsin and get back in good shape. Thank Doris also for her favor of last week.

God bless you Miss Grace Panyard, I was just in at my Hour and thought of my promise of the leaflets etc. Here they are and I am sure you will like them. Please tell Doris that it is three 3: 15 P.M. a little after that we expect that Fatima - Statue of Our B1. Mother Mary to arrive here at the Monastery, in case she's in the neighborhood.

God bless you and yours. I write your Brother Fred yester- day and now I come to your favor of Febr. 12. Many Thanks I've just noted your request for the Poor Holy Souls .... and hope that things brighten up soon. Tell George I send him one of my good ear pulls. Tell him "life" that the world is so inclined to worship is too short to act discouraged about anything in it. Ha Hal

God bless you Miss Grace Panyard. I hope this find you with brighter out-look and more confidence in our Blessed Lord God. Many thanks for your many kind favors. I told Doris recently of a venerable candidate for Beatification, --- Countess Mary Therese Sedochoska, whose life I recently read. Doris said she wold a copy and get acquainted with her - and ask her to help. I am sure you will join with the rest of of us in learning to know her and in turning to her in all kind of emergency. Tell Georg not to get discouraged whatever turns he meet with. Instead of worrying - never any good - tell him, let us spend some of the time in gratefully thinking over some of the innumerable blessings Almighty God has surrounded us with and still surrounds with.

God bless you and yours. And before I forget, let me congratulate you on your 24th anniversary. I'll try to reach you by the end of the week if not interrupted too frequently; so that you may have a reminder on the solemnity corresponding to that on which you were born, - Passion Sunday. I hope you are well and keeping the faith; for in these days of un- rest and of international turmoil when atheism - the positive climax of insanity - is so rampant, it is no trifle to keep in mind the great pur- pose of our creation and to live consistently, as for God. Ah, how often has not that second question of the little catechism we used to study while romping with grazing cattle on the slopes and wooded lowlands of pioneer west Wisconsin, come back to me! "Why did God make you?" And the beautiful answer: "To know God ... "! !! If according to philosophy: "To know is to appreciate." may we not say that, to know is to love the good; is to reject the bad, the wicked; is to adore the Divine? Could we think of a higher purpose? .... What hope this should inspire when we remember that the mercy of God is above all His works! What an outlook for poor sinners! What a sublime horizon if, "Hope is the very soul of happiness here" and the purpose of the rational creature TO KNOW GOD, which covers everything, be kept in mind! Hence, thanks be to Divine Providence. God made me to know Him. O what a bless'd aim! To love Him and serve Him, sure rests in the same. Its "Heaven Begun" for the grateful, on earth; To treasure aright ! ! ! Highest Heaven its Worth. You are possibly surprized at the above introductry details; and it did strike me as remarkable that a letter from your dear Mother, together with the first and last that my little namesake B. ever sent me, should unexpectedly fall into my hands on the eve of the "New Baby" Owen Joseph's twenty-forth birthday. From letter dated "May 2, 1919." - first anniversary of your dear GrandMa Casey's + .. Dear Br. Bernard; Well, thank God all my sorrow has most certainly turned into joy; for we are again happy over the birth of our forth child little darling Owen Joseph .. " and she adds a P.S. to B's letter: "Dear Bernard - Here is a sample of young Bernard's letter-writing. Pray that if its God's will he may follow in your footsteps." If he keep the faith and try earnestly to save his immortal soul which means success in the one thing necessary, then he is following the footsteps of all the saints. I certainly trust you are all so doing. From the "first and last letter ... " so far: Dear Father Bernard I was 7 years old March 7 and am in the second grade at school. I made my first Holy Comunion just a year ago. I have a May alter and love to say my prayers at night in front of it. Thomas is 5 years old. Rosemary is 3 years old and we have a new baby Owen Joseph he will be 4 weeks old next Sunday .. ... "I like my Sister at school very much her name is Sister Bernard. Papa and Mama are well and are good to us children. Please pray for your little nefue Bernard Brady". Quite a letter for a little seven-year-old. Not? · There were indications quit often since that little letter was penciled, that the writer would land somewhere nearer a monastery than would at present seem ever likely. God's ways, however, are so sublimely above our limited reckoning that we are simply lost when we venture to fathom even their shad- ows. So let us praise and adore Him in His decrees and in the very shadows of His adorable omnipotent wisdom - Power - Mercy - GOODNESS -- PROVIDENCE. I tried to get this off yesterday but it is now Friday. . . God bless you and your associates as well as your dear Parents and all your dear ones -- your enemies too if you have any, that they - that we all - be converted to God. P.S. - after return from Texas and Washington. "I walked down the Valley of Silence; down the dim voiceless val'y alone And I heard not the fall of a footstep around me, save God's & my own, "I walked in the world with the worldly. I craved what the W. never gave And I said "In the world each ideal that shines like as star on life' wave Is wrecked on the shores of the real and sleeps like a dream in a grave Do you ask me the place of the Valley, ye hearts that are burdened with care It lieth afar between mountains, and God and His angels are there; And one is the dark Mount of Sorrow; and one the bright Mountain of Prayer.' Pardon for spoiling the Blind Poet, Father Ryan's beautiful "Song of the Mistic". I undertook to memorize it some years ago and just lately again. I find it a sort of nerve tonic from the tales of misfortune and of sorrow and disapointment so almost continually brought to the Monastery Office. ... Since the above - upto and including manuscript - took its air trip on April 9th I have received official information of Fr. E'd's well being and good work Deo grt. It just returned from Washing (dead letter branch) this a.m.

God bless you and yours - your dear Parents especially and His mercy and your dear old Grandma and her good Husband. Sorry I could not have seen her before she became childish. Now all we can do for them is to remember them in our prayer and Masses. I am glad to hear from yourself - that you are still with us. I think it was when you were three the doctors would not have bet much on your living. Well, thank God for Everything .. . Very best regards and wishes to your dear Parents. I used to quite enjoy my visits over there to the West Side twenty years back. Thanks be to God, my health has been good ever since I went West for a vacation to the First Mass of my nephew in Seattle, Wash'n. It is much easier here though it is not a small job to keep the letters from accumu- lating. I am inscribing your name in my emergency list for your speedy im- provement and recovery - please God.

God in His infinite wisdom and merciful power give you His peace! He will give it to you - sooner or later. He must have a purpose, how- ever, in permitting you to fall - even like the rest of us. - even like against our wills. ..... He is the Master and the Judge, to recon the depth of our guilt and of our humiliation as well as how high above our- selves in His own good time He will raise ua. Only we must have patience till He change His attitude: because God is always figuring on our best. "God condescends to use our powers - if we don't spoil His plans by ours." And all this even though we be stupid sinners. For that we all are, though the whole world proclaim us heros and saints. But why dear Sister be so anxious about tomorrow? The morrow like yesterday is in God's keeping. To worry about the past or the future is really to no purpose. Quite a different thing is to regret our blunders - and God knows we have all made plenty of them - and humbly deplore them. But worry and fret? No. Because that hell wants us to do. Rather draw good out of them by praising God for His mercy to us and His infinite patience in not kicking to blases as good for nothings .... Dear Sister Mary Dorothy: I have not been forgetting you I've had your letter of June 29 here on the desk before me ever since. I've wanted to write something worth while but am always falling be- hind with my work. To-day on coming to yours of the 14th I started this just to assure you I'd write soon. You have no idea how much I need prayers - conversion as well as u.

I am enrolling you as an emergency member in the Seraphic Mass Association. I do hope it help you - and, God willing, that you be able again to sign your name. We'll pray for one another's con- version - physical and otherwise. In your case that it start - as would be perhaps best - with your hand and heart together ....?

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your charitable favor of Jan, 26th duely receiven and noted. I surely sympathize with you on the passing away of your dear Mother. I wanted to wrote before but it is difficult for me to get through with calls and letters that demand attention. Thank God, however, that she seems to have been well prepared and willing to respond to God's final call. May she rest with the saints in the peace of which the unbelieving wordl never dreams - awaiting all and each who try .. The same day you wrote, we had a very notable celebration in Detroit, - a solemn Mass of thanks giving as commemorating, my fiftieth year in the Habit of St. Francis. By this time you will no doubt have heard a number of the interesting features. Rt. Msgr. Edw'd and Br. Owen wired of their coming the day before to arrive in Det. at 7:10 p.m. Grace - Mrs B. Brady in the meantime, flew in from San Francisco and met them at the depot - all three arriving at the Monastery together about 7:45. To go into details is so out of the question here that I'll simply have to leave that to others. If I were only one tenth as grateful and appreciative as I ought to be I would hardly be able to do more than wonder and weep for joy at so many and so great favors following one another for 50 years, etc, all leading up to such a solemnity - as to just another decided "landmark" on the way of an individual's pilgrimage to real LIFE with the God of everlasting glory and the unfading love of the chosen servants in Heaven. How can we ever thank God as we ought for the inestimable gift of the true faith? A on the other hand, how lament the unfortunate lot of the vic- tims of atheism? - "The climax of intellectual and of spiritual insanity, the hopeless conclusion and the desperate refuge of shallow thinking, of edgener- ate minds and ( fearful to say), damned fools, none other their primary leader than Lucifer himself the prince of diabolical darkness. . Rt. Rev. Msgr. E'd had to get back to St. Paul. So left Tuesday P.M. Grace went to Toronto and will probably meet the Uncle Ed Traynor and Family. Owen came down with me Saturday Feb. 1st but went back next day. Yesterday he wired from Seattle that our Brother Patrick is not well and just now ( 11 a.m. ) a wire from Minneapolis from Msgr. says he hopes to see Pat by Friday a.m. in Seattle. I sent Br. Patrick an air special yesterday after Owen's wire.

God bless you and yours. Many thanks for your kind favor of just noted. We are enrolling your little Maureen in the Seraphic Mass Associa- tion that if it be God's holy will she may give the doctors and all who may be interested in her case, a good surprise. At the same time I would suggest that you get as many of your friends as possible to help you storm Heaven by frequent and daily Communion. And I might add, that you promise the Poor Souls - especially your own family- relatives, there doing penance and always interested in the welfare of their dear ones there left behind, that you will do somthing special for them if join the rest of friends as well as they may, by their pleading the cause of little Maureen as best they can. I've seen wonderful results and have had astonishing reports as throuth enrolling the Poor Souls, e.g., for a given percentage of the a- verted "doctor-bills". Thanks be to the merciful condesntion of Almighty God - and the all surpassing intercession of our B1. Mother Mary
- for speedy improvement and recovery, God willing - Courage is half the battle - Confidence in God the soul of prayer - Foster the latter and you have both.

Many thanks for your kind favor of the 27th. God bless you too Maurice O'Connell. I hope this finds you improved and improving. However, I think you would do well to see a good Chiropractor. I was doctoring for at least three years for my feet and legs - using a cain for several months and quite lame. ..... .. In less than three week Dr. Ralph Schorn had me on my feet - with my cain a forgotten thing. His of- fice is just across Gratiot Ave. from the Airport - 10050 Connors Ave. Hoping this finds you 100% in God's grace and service.

I hope this finds things brightening some way with you. You know that only God can work miracles. And when we turn to Him with con- fidence He never turns us down - if He forces it is for the good of our souls and to His glory. If not He always gives something better for us than what we ask for. At all events, try and get as many of your friends to help you "storm Heaven" for help - a cure or improvement of some kind so as to carry on and be at least resigned to His holy will till the end. We are enrolling you again and will pray for you and hope for results soon.

Many thanks for your favor of April 29. Please pardon delayed ac- knowledgement. Thank the good God for your improvement reported. May He continue to brighten things for you. The holy Masses have been solved. I am sending you herewith something will, I hope be satisfac- tory in place of what you ask. P.S. Am opening envelope to incert card. - "more haste less speed !. "

I just came across your pathetic letter of Nov. 12th '47 and was wonder- ing what might have come to your little Dan. Not sure if I ever sent you an enrollment card for the Seraphic Mass Association, I am sending you one now. At all events I would be pleased to know if little Danny is still living or is he already gone to Heaven - for to die in a state of such innocence as he was in, and his physical condition, would mean that he would go to Heaven at once. In such a case, how supremely for- tunate for the little saint! Also how fortunate the parents. . I hope too, your new Baby is already able to fill your home with sunshine.

Your letter and kind favor of Mar. 5 is gratefully acknowledged. Certificates of enrollment in the Seraphic Mass Assn. have been mailed. Glad to hear the good news about your brother in law. May he persevere in God's Holy Grace, and thus eventually gain his eternal reward. With regard to joining a "Third Order" or an order of "Oblates", to the Good Lord, it really doesn't matter which one you join, since you can insure your eternal salvation in any or either one. The important thing is the motive for joining, and the observance of the spirit and rule of the one which you belong. From a human standpoint however, we would be inclined to join the one that has the most appeal to you, since then our human nature would readily conform to the spirit and rule of that order. I would suggest that you obtain information on all three, taking all things into consideration, and after spending sufficient time in prayer and medi- tation, join that one which you feel will do you the most good, in regards to your eternal salvation. I will be only too glad to see you anytime you find it convenient to make the trip. Rest assured that I shall continue to remember you and yours in my prayers ..

Many thanks to you and our dear friends who has so generously remembered me in their prayers and other alms - especially in their Holy Communions, Masses and rosaries. I have been including them in my prayers and holy Masses and will offer my next "Free Mass" for your and their individual intentions and holy guidance. ..... . I would like to write each one but that would not permit me to perform more urgent duties. So I'll have to be brief. Praying that you each and all be blessed with God holy grace and health for the coming privileged holy season and feasts - Immaculate Con- ception - Christmas - New Years and following again around.

Pray to the good Lord for guidance, and to guide all concerned. If your Sisters and inlaws want to do something to promote justice and peace, they should join you in prayer for guideance while you consult a confessor, a priest. But you must turn a deaf ear to any other dictations. You took care of your mother and dad through the grace of God, and God in His goodness arranged for you to have the homestead because of your kind- ness to your mother and Dad. So in all justice you should keep what the Good Lord arranged for you to have.

God Bless you Dear James - but now I must God bless Father James, So at long last and hearty Congratulations. I started to write a couple times since receiving your personal letter and now I feel almost too late. Anyway I am remembering you and all the folks over on Colorado and hope to see you Sunday.

Only Today did I come to your favor of February 24th and though several times interrupted have just finished it. I hardly know what to advise you, other than that you simply practice patienc with yourself as well as with your neighbor - whether in the class -room or in the Convent or elswhere. For we may be sure that we come nowhere in the practice of virtue or in spiritual progress with patiently humbling ourselves in the face of the difficulties where-with the divinely jealous Lover of our poor souls is pleased to cheque our selfconceit and pride. If the Dear Lord has deigned to invite you to more than ordin- ary virtue and if on your part you have, perhaps again and again, seen something of the privilege of such an invitation, - finally concencenting even half generously to follow the CRUCIFIED SPOUSE, then you may quite naturally - locically rather - expect difficul- ties of some kind or of any kind to exercise you in the virtues that put the enemies the Cross to shame and make Heaven rejoice. Such virtues are ofcourse first of all Humility from which all other virtues worth while in God's sight, take root and nourishment I am inclosing a letter, written several years ago by the pre- sent Rt. Rev.Edw'dF. Casey, who was rescued from a Jap prison a year ago - Febr. 23rd 1945. I am quite sure you will proffit in its ear- nes perusal and study. At all events and whatever comes turn frequently to our dear Lord in the Tabernacle and next Him, to our Blessed Mother Mary, begging for the grace to correspond to the graces that He is always lavishing on our unworthy selves and for patience and HUMILITY. Just while I think of it and space at least permits . a few verses frim the pen of the same writer: CONSOLATION (I think is the title he gives it) . "Tis pain that purifies the human heart. Let this a gentle consolation be When bright hopes fade and dearest friends depart and love itself seem but a memory. "The hours that fill the soul with silent grief, - that flood it with unutterabl woe - Become, whin time hath given calm relief, the fountain whence a hundred virtues flow. "The mourner's tear hath furrowed kindly faces and left the light of love abiding there. SWeet sympathy and tender deeds are traces of pain and sorrow, soothed in silent Prayer. "Christ wraught Redemption from despair and sin. By His dear Cross the clouds of grief "Tis Bethlem and Calvary that win, from pain and sorrow, the seets of Heaven were riven. E. F. Casey. as a student. Hope you'll lake the lines herewith inclosed. Pray for the conversion of sinners - always including 1st yourself and then the writer.

We hope this find you improved and improving. However, we must be ready to face facts. Please pardon brevity, but your letter - rather your description of your trouble sounds like trouble which sooner Every sister - if she live long enough should expect. So in case those dizy spells continue do not be upset about but have a little patience and offer all for the intentions of the Sacred Heart.

Many thanks for your favor of yesterday, just noted. I would be pleased to see you any Saturday or Sunday convenient to you. In case you drive down, a good way is via #112 (and Willowrun), to Coldwater and then, Coldwater 2 - to - via #24 to Jefferson Ave. Huntington: turn up to right 3 - to till St. Felix is seen a half mile off to the left. to Fort Wayne take #27. If it should be muddy and soft, better go back two or three blocks to first paved street. St. Felix is only about one and a half mile from the center of City. In the mean time I am sending you a coppy of a letter which if read prop- erly ought to help you greatly to shake off that excessive worry you seem to be laboring under. That of course you ought to fight against. Because it is never good to worry and in nine cases out ten the worry is about something that has no real foundation, therefore, never happens. P.S. The Wabash train leaving Detroit about 7:30 A.M. stops at Huntington.

Thank you for the kind favor of November 20. The Mass for your dear mother was said yesterday. Please understand God is a good Father. He knows what is best for our souls. So no mat- ter what He gives, sickness, health or even death, He does so for our best interests. So whatever lie does, praise His holy Name. God bless you, your mother, and those close to you.

Its nearly a year now since your little visit the St. Felix Friary .. Many thanks for your kind favor of June 11th duly received and noted. I hope you proffit by your stay in Phoenix and that on your return home to Hamtramck you find mother and Sister better than ever. I hope to leave here and return to St. Felix shortly. How little we can appreciate our health until it fails us. So we really ought to thank God for trials and crosses as well as for joys and consolations.

and many thanks for your kind remembrance and and treat which latter, came in very handy for several guests who came last evening this a.m. twenty-six novices took simple vows at the solemn services .... Deo gratias. However, I'll now have to rather change my tone and scold you for your un- wonted soliditude about health or doctor or anything else. ... You surely want to get to Heaven. But how? Without dying? ... Ahl but in so vigerously pro- testing against this or that trouble, you as much as tell Divine Providence (in a way at least) "if I can't have at least something of a choice .. it will be all off; I can't make the grade." ... Just think, dear Soul. What would have become of humanity if in the Gar- den of Gethsesemini, Jesus had insisted on His own will: "Heavenly Father its too much! ... ", instead of: ... Not what I will, but what Thou willst ... ". 01 Where is our faith? Where are our proofs of love of Jesus, if suffering for the sake of the loved One be a proof of love? ? ? ! ! ! We ought to keep in mind as much as our poor frailities permit, especially in times of pains and sorrow; the thought of ETERNITY and the contrast of it with momentary passing for each one of us and the vanity of temperal phenomina - be they pleasant or painful to nature. We ought to thank God for both - for each and all these experiences. Even Jesus could not have accepted that decision of His heavenly Father, according to His human nature and with the divine nature, viz, without the grace of the Father. Hence, His continual communion with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Hence too our obligation to imitate Him, at least try at a distance. To get to Heaven! Think of it. 01 Is it not infinitely more than we can pay for it whatever way we consider it? When it was so great in the estimation of the Son of God Jesus and His for each one of us that He died for each of us! Then, what matter if I die with cancer or TB or a martyr some other way - To- day, tomorow or fifty years ahead? Shame on you as well as on myself. Stupid we are every one of, in our feat of following Jesus to Heaven even if the cross and death the way. P.S. Shake off that worry-half the victory over any trouble. ...

How can we ever thank God as we ought to do, for all His mercies and blessings to ug - - His wonderful designs and works and ways. I wanted to write several times but ...? Wondering how poor "Mack" were doing - - and his many (non Catholic) friends. .. Keep up your prayers - courage and always on guard against worry, etc.

Surely it is a promisin turn in the outlook for a five- year paralytic. Their fraternal-Christian interest as shown in response to the Chaplain's appeal for a so helpless sister-Mrs. Mary O.D., is surely to the high credit of the Boys in Cap (at the Gross Ille Base") . If every one of Mary's friends do what they can to please God and to sanctify their own souls, God in His merciful wisdom and power will give them the surprise of their life.

God bless you these days, you and yours. I hope you keep well. I hope too that Mr. Rand recover soon, as also your Niece -- . We will pray for them. Why not suggest to each of them - for that matter to any one in trouble -- that they make a proposition to do something specially pleasing to God if things go more favorable, if an operation be averted or a favorable surprise of telling importance come their way? I think I can honestly say that is one of the principal secrets of the many many favors reported at our monasteries as through the Ser. Mass Association. Stress especially offering holy Communions and praying for the poor missions. Nothing like frequent Holy Communion and holy Masses for the intentions of the intentions of our dear dear Lord; and surely one of His outstanding intentions is that one for which He pleads : " .. . The laborers " ... The harvest indeed is great but the laborers are few. Pray ye therefore, that the Lord of the harvest send laborers ". God bless you again. Sincerely Yours in Christ and His mission works. P.S. We are sending Mr. Rand his certificate. I hope it will bring him encouragement and an increase of confidence in God - and, God willing, speedy improvement.

You must think that there must be something not exactly right with that old Fr. Solanus down at Saint Felix. Indeed there is plenty wrong with him - has always been, at least as long as I can remember. Deo gratias. I wrote Rev. Mother yesterday and gave her every every assurance of my approval of your joining them - in fact congratulating them on your aquisition and enrolling their community in the Seraphic Mass Association in the hopes that you may in one or more ways presage a speeding up of vocations -- Ahl God willing, a speeding up in numbers and holyness before God. God bless you again Miss Haf - as above. It is time for the collecter. So please pardon my abruptness. Remind me again of the Clairs, and about your poor Brother too. God help us.

God bless you Jerry Mccarthy; - you and yours. We have been praying for your health-improvement; and although reports were not too good yesterday and today; still we hope this find you improved and improving. At all events dear Jerry, make the best of the situ- ation by offering everything to God in union with the sufferings and joys of Jesus' sacred Passion and victorious Resurrection. Not only that dear Jerry; but let us Thank God ahead of time for how and by what blessings He may see whereby best to answer our pleadings. I proposed yesterday to Miss Franklyn that we all join in "sort of storming Heaven" for Jerry's speedy recovery, God willing, and that we each make some little sacrifice of somekind. She surely seemed to fall in line with the idea at once. I am sure you will smile some day when she tells you the suggestion proposed. I was surely pleased at her willingness manifested. Sorry I could not talk with your whole Personnel - of whatever denominsyion. I cer- tainly was pleased to meet them as we did have the privilege to do so December 10th last. Glory be to God. Dear Jerry: I hope this may not have bored any one too much. When we get a little older and we may have a little more leisure I'll have to tell you about my Uncle, another grand (old) Jerry Mccarthy, who died in Neutown, Massachuttes at the age of 104. God bless you agani Jerry: and that you may profit by this little holdup you are experiencing these days, just try and take the whole thing and all its difficulties as from the hand of the Allwise and Merciful and Gracious God. Thank Him at all times and possibly when you get a little stronger you might think of some little way wherin personally to improve in His privileged service, possibly more frequently to receive if He speed the return of your health and surprise the doctors and your many friends. . . Deo Gr.

"Come to me all ye that labor and I will refresh you" Sept. 28th 1927, God Bless you all !.... See that you Save your Souls! Mrs. Margaret Bennett - for speedy recovery - Apr. 22, 1942, God bless you Mrs. Bennett. Keep Courage and pray for the conversion of the rest of us ... Fr. Sol. -- ho of course including Mike B. Praised
